Since release I've been quite interested in this one as it's premise, general artstyle and character design are to my liking. After completing it now it turned out to be an "great, but" - case, on the verge of being awesome but being hold back by some problems, giving it an almost schizophrenic feel. Nevertheless it has been a very enjoyable and fun journey, that I suggest you might take a look into. Under the Ecosystem of Steam Visual Novels, that are no re-releases, this is still one of the better ones. Now diving into futher details:
- It's a Kinetic Visual Novel (no choices that effect the outcome of the story, mostly bad-ends), with an quite interesting setup as stated above, which gave me the impression that this story will center around unraveling a mystery in a detective esque way with a focus on Cyberpunk-themes. Like: what you are and how much your memories define your personality, the usual Cyberpunk stuff. BUT the first 3rd of the VN uses themes that I really didn't expect, which hold my interest pretty high throughout the course of the story. A good chunk of the themes that it takles are overall pretty straight forward and generally not that fresh, but presented interestingly enough throughout the story. Sometimes it presents very interesting core ideas and executes them well. So throughout the story, when it seemed that the themes get too stereotypical and uninteresting, they were able to spice it up, which is what I meant at the outset by it feeling almost schizophrenic. It's an up and down of Storyquality: Sometimes really awesome, sometimes okay, but never really bad. The World spanning conflict that is introduced in the last 3rd felt a little bit tagged on though.
- The Middle is the only really weird part, as the VN takes it's time to establish a lot of quite interesting characters with some conflicting interests, that could have lead to cool scenarios for the latter part of the story. But they all suddenly dissapear for the last 3rd of the game. I hope that they will be expanded upon in future entries. But on the other hand the characters you will spend most time with are really well written. The struggles of the protagonists, it's solution and therefore his intereactions with the characters around him were really intruiging, especially with the main female character, Orikasa Reina. They really made a great team. She was easily as intruiging as the protagonist, though her conflicts weren't as good as the main character ones. The other characters that the game gives enough time like Kakeru, Sorano and Aoi are also pretty good. On the Antagonist side it's sadly a little bleak. The "Midboss" Antagonist is pretty boring and while I appreciate the idea of the Main Antagonist Kuroda, as he gets nowhere near enough time, his character is tried to be explained in a handfull of hours, which doesn't work that well.
- The Artstyle is awesome. It also leaves a great first impression with it's main menu, simple but visually pleasing. The Backgrounds look colorfull and varied. The characters look great from an Artstyle point of view. From an Visualdesign however, almost all of the side characters that get discarded for the last 3rd look a little bit weird. Some are quite different in their design compared to the maincast. The Soundtrack is also pretty awesome, some quite memorable tracks to be found. I should also mention that the game is voiced in Japanese which is also done really well.

The art did at times (rarely) felt lazily-done when in descriptions it said that the character was crying/bleeding, but the art didn't show it at all whatsoever. Despite what I said, I still think the visuals were amazing or maybe the art style was just something that suited my taste. Definitely the strongest aspect of this VN in my opinion.
Another positive aspect of this VN is the sound. The soundtracks are majorily good and the voice acting was pleasant to listen to.
The premise definitely grabbed my attention when I first came in contact with this product (I bought it through HumbleBundle). The setting's interesting, but I can't help but feel that it just didn't reach the potential that it could have reached. The sci-fi element is kind of blurred out mid-way by the introduction of supernatural elements/characters, so if you're in for the sci-fi aspect then don't expect too much.
The story was okay. Some mystery here and there, but since this is only the first installment it gives the readers an open ending.
The main characters are okay. Side characters aren't explored in any way whatsoever and are just tossed away after a certain point. Hopefully they re-appear and are explored deeper in the sequel installments.
If there was an option to give this a meh instead of a thumbs down/up, I would've given that.

I don't write reviews often, but everyone's leaving a negative review so I might as well say something. This is gonna be a long one.
Disclosure: I hardly played singleplayer and I never used mods, but on mods;
Banning a popular modding tool doesn't get rid of the other tools people might use. It won't magically get rid of older versions of the tool, it's not going to get rid of mods people already have, and thus it's not going to stop hackers online. Even if, there's nothing stopping some random person from editing the files themselves, especially when some hacks aren't dependent on modding tools.
Plus, banning mods just hurts the playerbase. Not everyone plays multiplayer, and a lot of people on youtube make GTA singleplayer mod videos.
Anyways. I have a ton of problems with this game, so let's begin.
First off is how many hackers there are. You can see how much of a problem this is when a popular modding tool is banned, even when in the past, Rockstar has said "we're fine with singleplayer modding though" (though to be fair, TakeTwo banned it, with/without Rockstar agreeing)
You'll join a lobby, do whatever, then suddenly a hacker joins and spawns a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on your head and locks all your controls and blows your car up randomly. Then they'll do the same for your friends until you leave, switch lobbies, repeat.
They'll also spawn moneybags for people to pick up, which everyone will because getting money in Online mode is a huge grind (I'll get to that later). Plus, if you pick them up, you put yourself at risk of getting falsely banned. Check some other reviews. You get banned for a month and your character is completely reset at worst.
Now another problem is money. It's just a huge grind to get a good amount of cash. I've got over 100 hours and I've only ever broke a million. Not two million, one million. You might say "but that's still a lot of money, isn't it?" For singleplayer, yeah, sure. Online? Not really. Anything you want to do with money is level locked or insanely expensive.
If you want to get a good amount of money, you need to do heists, which also have some pretty silly requirements too.
For example, you almost

One of those very, very rare games I would gladly wipe from my memory just so I could once more experience it for the first time, and again fall in love with its excellent level design, addictive and challenging stealth gameplay, superbly dark atmosphere and clever, subtle storytelling.

It is amazing to see how such a well crafted game still holds up to our modern gaming society through the amazingly constructed environment with smart and big level maps. Each level is just as the other (These levels can be massive!!!), walk into a building/area, each unique to one another, just to find that there a multiple ways to complete most of the quests.  For example, steal a key from a guard, open the front doors, overhear a guard talk about a back entrance, or find a hidden passage which you heard from a diary within this environment.  The possibilities are endless!!! I highly recemend this game also because it is such a revolutionary title.  This game is the first game to apply lighting and sound to the stealth franchise.  Great consept even though the story may be lacking and the dialog sound terrible. I personally highly recemend this game to anyone who loves playing classic games, who loves taking their time and thinking things through, who just wants to play a revolutionary game, and wouldn't mind to get their butt kicked in the process through this games purposeful difficulty.

Main purpose of this review is to cover some FAQ though:
1. I didn't find much use for separate run and walk keys -- I remapped keys to the "wsad" pattern, with "w" for run. When I need to walk slowly, I use "shift", works just fine.
2. The game itself works OK on Vista (64bit), but without cutscenes. Pressing "Intro" button yields nothing too. I found lack of story/narrative to be quite disquieting so I started looking for a solution.
3. As always, there were a lot of bull$hit solutions proposed on the Internet, like TTLG/TFix/etc, but IMNSHO you shouldn't tamper with Steam version using 3rd party patches that may contain every sort of malware while no guarantees whatsoever. The Real Solution for Thief Gold on Vista and Windows 7 is to set "Run this program as administrator" flag on THIEF.EXE (C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\SteamApps\common\thief_gold\THIEF.EXE --> Properties --> Compatibility tab), this brings cutscenes back (don't bother with "Run in WinXP SP2 compatibility" mode, it doesn't cut the mustard).
4. You can use resolution higher than 800x600 if you manually edit both cam.cfg and ddfix.ini (TFix boasts that it enables this to be done via in-game Video menu, but I didn't bother to verify).

This is a remake of a 90s old school shooter.
Rise of the triad is an old school shooter so the story matters least and is almost completely forgotten during gameplay.
The gameplay is your good old-old school shooter where you explore levels going from point A to B and killing everything along the way but rise of the triad is somewhat unique amount old school shooters:
You have the choice of 5 different characters to play as who all vary in speed and toughness,
You have a four weapon limit where you have dual pistols with infinite ammo and no reloading, you have an mp40 with infinite ammo and no reloading, and you have one more spot of shotguns and various and fun and interesting rocket launchers and flamethrowers, and a mystical baseball bat, and a staff,
You have power ups which are: god mode(literally), dog mode, and getting high…
The health in this game is porridge which gives you much more health if you cook it first,
You do have reloading but it’s a joke on modern shooters! It does nothing, it’s just an animation,
The music is mostly rock but it doesn’t really sound that good, it is quite good but when you compare it to the songs in serious sam, the soundtrack to painkiller, the soundtrack to DOOM 1 and 2 it’s not that good.
You also collect coins and you have a bit of platforming and some interesting level design.
Problems:
The pistols and the SMG aren’t very fun too use.
The voice acting is very bad and the main characters are very annoying.
The final boss is really cheap in terms of difficulty to the point where I was playing the game on hard but I had to but it down to easy on the final boss.
This is a very good game and serves as a reminder of how dull and boring and easy shooters have become, defiantly get this game if you like old school shooters.

The aforementioned power that your character has, is the power to change the Fate (aka Killing people with glowy weapons. If you kill them with normal weapons, it's fine, but killing them with glowy things changes their fate, because screw logic), and since you died and was reborn, you are a person without its own Fate.
I love this game, it is amazing, and everytime I play, I have fun with it. I think it could be easily compared to Skyrim due to the mechanics, with Skyrim having superior graphics and a First Person View.

I'm a little late to the party with Brütal Legend, as I had seen the game release about 8 years ago and now I've finally played through it. At the time of release, I was interested in the product but had seen it sink under mixed reviews and so was delayed playing it until now, when I could get it on Steam for a cheap price.
So what do I think? The game is... fine. There's a lot to like. The setting is a satire of metal as a genre and its imagery. The game starts off explosively and gets you engaged with the world and its music. The music itself is an excellent and extensive collection of metal, focusing mostly on Traditional Heavy Metal, Thrash Metal and Black Metal.
Within the actual metal scene of the 80s, Hair Metal rose as an abomination meant to be commercially marketed to teenage girls and brought MTV to life, and the game certainly acknowledges this as a parody. One of the main villains is named General Lionwhyte, who takes the stereotypes of Hair Metal bands like Mötley Crüe and Warrant and blows them up to disgusting levels. This isn't to say that I don't like Hair Metal, but I appreciate that the game acknowledges the history of the genre and parodies the attitudes of the people of the time. It makes for quite an interesting character and faction that follows him.
The game also has a few cameos from stars like Ozzy Osbourne (The Guardian of Metal as it were) and incorporates stage and album imagery into the world (for example, the Screaming Wall, which is a giant cliff of amps). In addition to this, imagery from the metal culture (occult symbols, fire, demons, black clothing with spikes) creates an excellent atmosphere.
Your guitar can be used as a weapon to play solos (which have a number of both combat and non-combat functions) as well as strike enemies with lightning from afar as a ranged weapon. The in game menus are designed to complement the atmosphere and they do it well (they were designed by Joe Kowalski who worked on some of the Guitar Hero and Rock Band games). Last, the main menu is designed to look like Jack Black is looking through the packaging of a vinyl disk and is easily the most unique menu aesthetic that I've ever seen. Jack Black too also voices the main character Eddie and does an excellent job with it.
Where the game fails is in its gameplay itself. It's essentially a shallow hack and slash, with some clunky driving portions. Where the game really suffers though, is the RTS gameplay. There are a number of campaign missions where you're required to build a stage and use groups of units to take down the enemy. You must also hold checkpoints, which are essentially geysers that spout of fans (of your band) and allow you to summon more units. I like the audacity of attempting to combine a hack and slash with an RTS, but the RTS moments are just so poorly implemented. They end up feeling like a chore and heavily detract from the game. And while the game world is interesting at first, the farther you delve into it, the more you realize that is has no depth and becomes quite boring. You can do side missions, but the more I got into the game, the more tired the gameplay got and so I didn't bother.
So is the game worth a recommendation? I'd say yes. I think if you're a fan of metal as a genre, you'll appreciate what this game was trying to do and the love that went into it. I believe that a single play-through is worth your time, but because of the subpar hack and slash gameplay, as well as the poor RTS implementation, there's not much replay value. As a fan of metal, the game is worth the price to me (as of now 9/22/2017 it is $15).

I expected a 30h game, so here is my note divided by 6 (will update if they ever fix the crash):
[1/10]

Let's talk about the positives first. This is a very pretty game if your hardware can handle it. I've seen my GPU use 7.3Gb of VRAM at 1080p with everything maxed and MSAA x4. I've had no stutters or huge framedrops etc., and the game has been butter smooth with none of the missing textures or problems others have been reporting. The story is classic Deus Ex. If you liked DEHR especially, you're probably going to like this, although the hacking, weapon upgrades and Jensen's augs have been tweaked slighty (in a good way, I think). A lot of staples such as conversation branches, side missions, weapons, stealth, hacking and exploring are still a huge part of the game. It's been said in professional reviews that there is a lack of variation in locations, but I've found enough variation between the locations that I've not become bored. There's always plenty to explore and an extensive sewer system too! I will say though, that some of the dialogue and lip-sync work is a bit 'bad kung-fu movie' in places, but I find it quite amusing TBH.
I'm 19 hours in and I've been having a total blast until now . However, I've just run into the mission 14 crash-to-desktop gamebreaking bug, and I'm not best pleased. I think it's unaceptable that an AAA game should have game breaking bugs like this when it's already been delayed to by six months in order to assure quality. I hope the devs fix this ASAP. I understand sometimes bugs fall through the net, but this and the other known bugs are a huge issue for a £40 game.
If you're thinking of buying this, I would advise waiting for a while. It's been a lot of fun and it is essentially a good game, but this game needs fixing before I could really recommend it. Also, you'll need a decent rig to get the best from the visuals this game offers. With that said, I tested on 'medium' to 'ultra' on an Nvidia card and the scaling was pretty good.
Time will tell how much the bug fixes and eventual DX12 patch will go toward making this game realise its potential...

Started as a free flash web-browser game in 2003, the "Samorost " was a fun little, point and click adventure game with gimmicky puzzles. "Samorost 2" the award winning sequel definetly surpassed the first. Samorost 2 is pretty much the same as the first, but much more improved, better grahpics, harder puzzles and an awesome soundtrack by Tomas Dvorak. However, the puzzles are much much harder... which can easily frustrate some not-so-patient gamers, you need to squint and try to click on every tiny detail in some stages.. which kind of damages the beautiful graphic experience. There is no inventory or lots of gathering like in most adventure games, instead you solve puzzles at every stage and proceed to an another. Collage-esque graphics are rare in video games, but Jakub Dvorsky definetly knows how to make some very lovely and astonishing backgrounds and artistic graphics in general. If you are looking for a challenging, lovely and a bit weird experience. Samorost2 is a great choice.

Memory’s Dogma Code 01 (MDC-01) to me is a just above average visual novel. It has good voice acting and artwork, an average and mostly linearly plot, and slightly underwhelming world building. It is probably worth full price if you like VNs that get straight into the plot, enjoy a thriller, and don’t mind unresolved minor plot points.
MDC-01 is a visual novel for people who prefer a story to get moving instead of idling through multiple slice of life scenes. This story opens with a death and a near death set in the near future where dead people’s memories can be digitally stored. As the setting suggests, the protagonist sets out to access a dead person’s memories, and the story almost never stops moving from that point.
The best aspects of the story are the great voice acting and pretty artwork. The voice acting makes every dialogue more alive by giving emotions to the characters. The artwork is pretty despite the slightly simple feeling to it.
The route structure is very simple and linear. There are several choices to make throughout the story, of which only a handful have a wrong choice that will quickly lead to a bad end. In a way, the lack of long branching routes is a good thing because it allows the reader to experience all the great voice acting and artwork without having to repeat content several times.
The world of MDC-01 is built through gradual releases of information bites, so the reader should easily understand the world. The details and plot developments are sensible at first blush, but some of them don’t stand up to scrutiny. The story’s conclusion resolves the main plot point, but offers no closure where the side characters are concerned. Current information points to the developer, LizArts, planning Code 02 and Code 03. The open plot points may be resolved then, but release dates are unknown.

I enjoyed this VN, but not sure I can recommend it for its original price.
Let's see... The choices in this game are very minor: either just a little bit of dialogue changes or you get an 'instant' bad end, in which the game sends you back a little before the choice so you can make the correct choice and continue on the story.  So, it's practically a kinetic visual novel, just so you know.
A lot of the characters... it's hard to really get to like them.  A lot show up, and then end up leaving pretty soon.  The main character is beyond rough to sympathize with in the beginning, but he grows as the story progesses.  A few of the characters were pretty interesting, and of course everyone loves Reina!  She makes up for everyone else really, so it's okay.
I liked the music.  I liked the art.  I really enjoyed the story overall, it kept my attention really well and wanted me to continue on to figure out just what the heck was going to happen next (very supsenseful, and it does this well!)  I'm also a fan of sci-fi stuff, so this was right up my alley.  It may take a bit of time before that happens though, the beginning was a bit slow.  And... it looks like I have 5.3 hours as my time, and that's pretty much everything (not much replay value here).
Apparently there's supposed to eventually continue on: there's a few things left in the air, but overall the story wraps up okay.
I had a lot of fun, but I got lucky and got this as part of a bundle, definitely tough to recommend it at full price.  Wait for a sale for sure, but once it comes, I would get it, it was a good experience.

Overview:
First off lets get this out of the way, the story, its cliche. However, sometimes a cliche can be done so well that it becomes entertaining to watch/read again. Continuing, the characters are fun, even though some of them you hardly interact with (I expect them to return in the sequals), but the main characters are a fun bunch. The music is really good for a VN in my opinion. The art, well its definitly got a style that I love so for me 10/10 there.
**************************
My Overall Rating 9/10                (therefore yes I believe its worth its price even when not on sale)
**************************
[More info on concerning rating at bottom]
Story: Lets start with yes the story is "good", please if its hard to get though just keep going becuase it does pick back up. Somtimes it just has to settle annoying plot points first. The game feels like it changes genre 3 times (at least) which in the beginning (after the first shift) I hated. Nevertheless, as I gloomily continued my way through that first genre shift I realized there was merit to it and it became an entertaining plot once again. Beyond genre shifts it has quite a lot of cliches (previusly stated in the overview) but it frequently plot twists its way around them and manages to straddles that border between "I hate this, I've seen this dozens of times" and "this is generally unique". 7/10
Charaters: Well I changed my profile picture on steam to Reina.... Anywho, the main characters are a fun bunch of friends who I enjoyed reading about even the most mundane parts of their lives. Now, get this, they are technically not in high school! They are in college... except for one. So overcoming that huge cliche (even though it was a very close call) was a breath of fresh air for any visual novel or anime for that matter. The side characters, well after finishing this game i stop and say "what side charaters" they hardly played a role in this installment, just advenced the mid story, I expect them to make a return in the later game based on where we were left at this end of this game though. Therefore 8/10
Music: Well I liked the music. It set the mood well and it was above average. Audio in general with sound effects and such met standards and/or exceeded. Therefore 9/10
Art: This art is in the style that I love. The colors are great and set the moods well. The characters are accented to match who they are. Backgrounds were nice and detailed (but not over the top). Also Still frames accessable from the gallery are very pleasing (which I dont find often). Overall the art was exactly what I wanted. 10/10
Togetherness: hah, this is my special catagory. The story was well organized and set perfectly with minor plot points and major points entertwined pefectly. The scenes blend very well with the plot and the music really does enhance it all. Now there are a few holes in the plot (the ones left are likely to be answered in the next installments). Now, in the begining it seems to be in completle dissaray the story does form together in the end once the minor plots are settled which actually got me hooked due to the suspence created by thought of dissaray in the story. 9/10
(7+8+9+10+9)/5= 8.6
Technical Rating: 8.6/10
Officail Rating: 9/10 (rounded to nearest whole number)

Trine was one of my favourite games released in 2009. Trine 2 follows in its footsteps, having everything that made the first one great, plus full online and cross-platform co-op modes, more diverse environments & puzzles, better (more challenging) enemies/bosses and ridiculously beautiful graphics. It's a 2.5D action puzzle-platformer. In Singleplayer you can switch between 3 distinct characters and use their abilities in order to overcome enemies, traps and other environmental hazards. In multiplayer everyone controls one of the characters, which gets interesting really quick as you now need to think of a way to not only get one character across traps but 2 or even 3. Tons of secret stuff & collectibles to find, New Game+ and an optional unique game mode for MP all add to the replayability. A Collector's edition is also available and comes with the official soundtrack as well as the artbook, if you are into that kind of stuff. Highly reccommend getting this game!

Pros:
- Beautiful graphics. Those spells man, they're gorgeous!
- Really fun and flexible combat.
- Good story.
- Nice characters, with voice-acting for every NPC. Quite well done too. Good facial expressions as well.
- Plenty of character flexibility, in terms of choosing how to play.
- Good DLC.
- Beautiful cutscenes.
- Very stable game. No crashes or glitches after 60h of play. Even after resuming the game after PC sleep.
- Very quick saving. Odd, but true. Esc>Save Game>Esc again to re-enter game fast. Other games need time to save.
- Player housing, which is both expandable and comes with beautiful rooms and useful features.
- NPCs are often quite beautiful facially and they also respond to event changes or differences. At one point, NPC A was talking to me and he then complained about a race in the game, the Dokkalfar, but my character was of that race, so he added something to the effect of "Ahem, except you of course". Very nice touch!
- Safety mechanism in place to stop you from accidentally hitting friendlies. So you need to press H to enable this. However this is less realistic than in Skyrim. To make matters worse, you can't always enable it, such as in certain safe areas it seems and thus you can't attack annoying people, as the games loading screen suggests...
- Makes you feel special as ♥♥♥♥ lol.
- Fast loading times between going in and out of buildings.
- Nice "junk items" system, where you go through your inventory, add the items you don't want to junk and then go find a merchant. Then you click "sell all junk" and you're done. Quite nice and easy.
- Many different items, both clothing and otherwise.
- Lots of hidden items and locations to find, as well as collectible armor sets.
- Many different kinds of enemies and areas.
- Possible to stealthily kill NPCs, although you only get a stealth-kill animation if using a Dagger.
- Really nice tarot-card-like destiny system, with good RP options, due to the descriptions.
Cons:
- No followers.
- Your character has no voice and so is silent during dialogue.
- Not possible to yield, if accidentally or intentionally hitting a friendly character.
- Sometimes clunky system of having to constantly re-do the same dialogue to make multiple selections, such as if you choose to buy all upgrades to a house at the same time. This also means you can't choose what gets added to your house, but instead have to follow a set order. So if you don't want an Alchemy room for instance, but the Alchemy dialogue option comes first, then you're forced to buy the Alchemy room to get to the next dialogue option, for other house segments.
- Character creation is based on presets mostly and thus isn't very deep or flexible.
- After creation, only certain features can be changed; not major things such as eye color.
- Mini-games such as lockpicking can be tedious and not as refined as say, Skyrim.
- Game is generally less "free" than Skyrim and is more cartooney, but still pretty. Less options.
- Less freedom of movement. It's one of those games where you can't jump over edges, but need a prompt.
- Character facial gear *always* gets removed during normal dialogue, annoyingly, so you can see their face.
- Combat can be annoying sometimes, because you can't always just stop a combo or spell mid-cast, to dodge or block. Thus when you do long basic attack chains, but know that an enemy is charging an attack, it's not possible to stop and block. Thus you often get hit.
- Shields aren't visible when you equip them. Instead, they just appear out of nowhere when you press the block button.
- No mounts.
- Shallow interaction with environment, such that you can't interact with chests or bookshelvs by putting things back into them, like you can in Skyrim. So once you take everything out of them, they stop their characteristic shining.
- Lacking a screen that shows which clans/factions you're allied with and their respective banners and your status within them. I would've liked this, even though it's not a big deal.
- Inventory system is annoying because if you have health potion A in your inventory already and you find a new health potion, you won't be able to add that potion to your existing stockpile of the same potion, if your inventory is full. Thus you need to clear at least 1 slot, in order to be able to pick this up. Quite tedious. On the other hand, ingredients from things like plants don't require space. As goes for crafting materials.
- If you press F to talk with an NPC, but they're in the process of laying down to sleep or getting up or something, then your character is completely immobilized until the dialogue starts. This is a small thing, but quite stupid.
- Lack of mods and steam workshop support.
- Block is simplistic, which means you can just hold down B for block and then enemies can't even flank you, as your character will automatically turn to block them.
- When you have just finished a quest, the game will, perhaps unless you've unticked tutorials/help, auto-select the main quest line for you again and add a pop-up notifying you of the fact that you have no quest. This is annoying, as it means you've *always* got a quest and can't just ignore it.
- When buying items, the game doesn't calculate the cost for you. So if an item costs 446 and you want to buy 3 of it, you get to select how many and then click buy and you won't know how much the final price is, unless you calculate it yourself. No pop-up shows how much money you used either.
- NPCs using weapons you can't get. I've seen a few NPCs use spears and I love spears. Yet I haven't found a single equippable spear in the game.
- Sleep is purely for role-play it seems, as there's no benefit to doing it, besides healing up to full health/mana for free.
- Unless there's an enemy in sight, you can't aim neither spells nor arrows, but only shoot straight ahead. Thus you can't really look up at the sky and shoot that way, for instance.

I'm a little late to the party with Brütal Legend, as I had seen the game release about 8 years ago and now I've finally played through it. At the time of release, I was interested in the product but had seen it sink under mixed reviews and so was delayed playing it until now, when I could get it on Steam for a cheap price.
So what do I think? The game is... fine. There's a lot to like. The setting is a satire of metal as a genre and its imagery. The game starts off explosively and gets you engaged with the world and its music. The music itself is an excellent and extensive collection of metal, focusing mostly on Traditional Heavy Metal, Thrash Metal and Black Metal.
Within the actual metal scene of the 80s, Hair Metal rose as an abomination meant to be commercially marketed to teenage girls and brought MTV to life, and the game certainly acknowledges this as a parody. One of the main villains is named General Lionwhyte, who takes the stereotypes of Hair Metal bands like Mötley Crüe and Warrant and blows them up to disgusting levels. This isn't to say that I don't like Hair Metal, but I appreciate that the game acknowledges the history of the genre and parodies the attitudes of the people of the time. It makes for quite an interesting character and faction that follows him.
The game also has a few cameos from stars like Ozzy Osbourne (The Guardian of Metal as it were) and incorporates stage and album imagery into the world (for example, the Screaming Wall, which is a giant cliff of amps). In addition to this, imagery from the metal culture (occult symbols, fire, demons, black clothing with spikes) creates an excellent atmosphere.
Your guitar can be used as a weapon to play solos (which have a number of both combat and non-combat functions) as well as strike enemies with lightning from afar as a ranged weapon. The in game menus are designed to complement the atmosphere and they do it well (they were designed by Joe Kowalski who worked on some of the Guitar Hero and Rock Band games). Last, the main menu is designed to look like Jack Black is looking through the packaging of a vinyl disk and is easily the most unique menu aesthetic that I've ever seen. Jack Black too also voices the main character Eddie and does an excellent job with it.
Where the game fails is in its gameplay itself. It's essentially a shallow hack and slash, with some clunky driving portions. Where the game really suffers though, is the RTS gameplay. There are a number of campaign missions where you're required to build a stage and use groups of units to take down the enemy. You must also hold checkpoints, which are essentially geysers that spout of fans (of your band) and allow you to summon more units. I like the audacity of attempting to combine a hack and slash with an RTS, but the RTS moments are just so poorly implemented. They end up feeling like a chore and heavily detract from the game. And while the game world is interesting at first, the farther you delve into it, the more you realize that is has no depth and becomes quite boring. You can do side missions, but the more I got into the game, the more tired the gameplay got and so I didn't bother.
So is the game worth a recommendation? I'd say yes. I think if you're a fan of metal as a genre, you'll appreciate what this game was trying to do and the love that went into it. I believe that a single play-through is worth your time, but because of the subpar hack and slash gameplay, as well as the poor RTS implementation, there's not much replay value. As a fan of metal, the game is worth the price to me (as of now 9/22/2017 it is $15).

You know how they always say "I'm sick of remakes; they never hold up to the original" or "Why couldn't they just remake the old game shot for shot, with updated graphics and more weapons etc? What is THIS crap??" or "It's an OK remake I guess, but it just doesn't feel like/doesn't capture the magic of the original"? Well, Rise Of The Triad (ROTT) takes exception to all of that.
After putting a ludicrous amount of hours into the original, I can say with confidence that ROTT 2013 not only plays like ROTT '95, but also captures that intangible "magic" or "feel" that made us all fall in love with the original. Even the sound effects and soundtrack are there (albeit updated). It feels like a mid-90's shooter, it has the same humor, and unfortunately all of the same weaknesses of mid-90's shooters. It's ability to warp you straight back to 1995 is its greatest strength and greatest weakness. It's easy to get somewhat bored with this game because it doesn't offer much over the original, that's how faithful it is. After that initial nostalgia high, there isn't much more. Then the little bugs start to become noticable.
The hit indicator is often incorrect, sometimes I'll be in a huge area with a straggler hitting me from some damned place, and I'll have no idea where, partially because of the inaccurate hit indicator and partially because enemies weapons are quiet and weapons have indistinctive sounds, easily blending in with the background music.
You'll die a lot in this game, as you should. That's how we rolled in the mid-90's. Games were far more unforgiving. Enemies are unfairly and ridiculously precise with their weapons, again how it should be.
If you've never played ROTT '95 or any shooter from that era, I'm not sure this is for you. If you're a fan of the original or just 90's shooters in general, this is a MUST HAVE.

For a long time I never replayed a Single Player Campaign twice, nor had the desire to repeat it over and over again. Besides Bioshock Infinite (yes I loved the gameplay, deal with it...) and Modern Warfare 2 (I don't even know... so don't ask) and like 3 or 4 more, it's Rise of the Triad that enters this rare list of mine!
It's 14€ title that is a remake of the original ROTT back in 1994 (?) which I never played to be honest. This one seems to be more...colorful than the original so I've been told, but it's not the color pallet that really matters here (though it's somewhat colorful, except in the indoor sequences which are 80% of the game...), it's the gameplay:
-It's superb! It's just simple, fast paced, rocket jumping fun, with a sprinkle of ludicrous gibs (yes you can actually get *LUDICROUS GIBS*! By gibbing many enemies at the same time with a rocket weapon, this will result in a pair of eyeballs smash into your screen alongside a big spew of blood and other body parts (including a lovely middle finger)).
Besides being fast-paced, it's just basic shooting! Rather than taking cover, the game rewards moving fast and strafing to avoid enemy fire, while hunting for secrets (which are very nicely hidden *looks at Hard Reset and Shadow Warrior '13*) that are very helpful along your journey, as not only they are a must find to 100% every level, but also give the best guns in order to help you take out the bosses which are quite tough.
Gameplay is pretty basic but it's so much fun! You have 3 bullet weapons (the single pistol, the dual pistols and the MP40 SMG) which all have infinite ammo and do not need any reloading whatsoever. And while this sounds like you can just hold LMB until the game finishes, you will not want to do that because the bullet weapons don't do all that much damage, and even some enemies are immune to bullets (the robots come to mind).
You have then the rocket weapons (and new patched Shotgun (or Dommstick), which doesn't make much sense, but it's quite amazing and feel like a Dommstick for real!) which have limited ammo but are avaliable pretty much everywhere so that you (pretty much) never run out of rockets.
Like I said, extremely basic gameplay but it's so fun to gib everything and the guns do feel very powerful (the Split Missile feels just, epic!) and that's what really makes the game so replayable in my opinion.
Moving to the story, it's non-existant (guys, it's a 90's remake ^^) or at least, pretty much non-existant, since you get introduced into it at the start of the game, where you are a HUNT team member (some special forces task force of extreme forces against other forces of enemy force) that go into an Island filled with suspiciously active triads and you must uncover what kind of♥♥♥♥♥♥they are doing!
After the starting cutscene (it's a comic book page flip btw) you get no more story indications except this: "If it moves, kill it!"
The end is...weird, it seems like Interceptor (the developers) will release Single Player DLC (paid or free I have no idea). Maybe they won't, who knows, I haven't seen any SP extras (except 1.4's Shotgun) since the game's release which was almost a year ago!
Moving on, audio is fine. All weapons sound great, interactions sound great as well (picking up the coins, jum pads making that distinctive sound, etc.) but the voice acting is very cheesy and poor, but it seems like in was on purpose, like on that B-movie "so bad it's good" type of voice-overs. Even the enemies, like Big John on E2L1 which sounds like a poor impersonation of Arnold Schwarzenegger, and it was quite funny.
Graphically the game is mediocre. It doesn't look fully realistic, it looks a bit (just a smidge) cartoony and it sets well the mood of the game. I must comment on the gibs which look absolutely terrible, and that is a bad thing since this game is all about the *ludicrous gibs*! Most of them look very poor (the torso gib looks decent).
I do have some issues with the game, and they aren't slight ones:
The Performance is terrible! The game doesn't look anywhere impressive to bring my PC to it's knees! The game is (like I said) decent at best when maxed out! And yet! I get most of the time 45 FPS, though it may go up to 65 or even 70 but that is quite far and between. Sometimes it drops to 23 FPS when there's "too much on the screen" and when I mean "too much" I mean "not that much", so the performance is really bad overall, though I must admit it was way worse back a few months ago! A game this fast paced is almost unforgivable for the performance to be this bad! Though the game feels not so high budget, so there you go...
Another issue is the bugs/glitches. The are many clipping issues, some stuff can be exploited, they even let us access parts outside of the map (which they shouldn't) which, just like it sounds, will cause you to go under the map, clip through materials and will FORCE you to reload a checkpoint (or a quicksave, if you remember to do that) which are very far away from eachother!
Another gripe is the first person platforming which is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t! You move WAY too fast for such precise platforming, which will cause you to rage sometimes. I raged once, though I didnt quit, I just kept trying and nailed it, and that feeling of accomplishment is really ♥♥♥♥ing awesome, I must say!
Angry gets stuff done I guess...
The enemy AI is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in epic proportions, though it feel like it was on purpose, to catch that 2.5D feeling into full 3D. And even though they are really bad, the game is reall really really REALLY hard! You must pay attention to avoid traps because they will take lots of health and then just a bullet will take you back to a checkpoint you reached half an hour ago!
I never tried multiplayer and honestly, I couldn't care less, the Single Player is just so much fun I just don't even look at the Multiplayer icon in the menu!
The game is also quite long, I beat it in 11 hours, but the last boss fight... It took me maybe 30 or more retries to get the boss, and I must adress: I killed him because he got stuck in the terrain so it was easy to kill him.
Overall, Rise of the Triad succeeds at what a every video game should go for: being fun! In fact I would say it's some of the most fun I've had in the past couple of years and maybe (just maybe) it's one of my GOTY nomenees of 2013 (better than Shadow Warrior 2013, in my totally honest opinion), despite it's massive flaws that really stop it from being the amazing game it could've been.
Thus I'm giving it 2 scores, a biased and an unbiased one:
-Overall, yeah it was fun, but everything about it mediocre except the gameplay and the level design, so it gets an unbiased score of 5/10.
-I found it just so ridiculously fun, gory and replayable that I want to ignore it's issues, though some persist and do break the experience for me, making give it a biased score of 8/10, thanks to the huge amount of fun I've had with it.
Fun is really the word here, so go out, buy it for 14€ or 15$ or whatever; or if the issues bother you, wait for a sale. It's totally worth your coins (see what I did there? :D)

As I begin this review, it is 1:54 in the morning. The entire upper half of my face and my chest hurt from the excessive sadness I have just felt and been exposed to. And I sorely regret getting all of the achievements in the first run through because all I want right now is a reason to play this game again. Immediately.
Like the other reviews say, this game is kind of short. My first real playthrough was maybe somewhere around 5+ hours (and I very much took my time).  My hours on record lie- I had Steam issues and had to start over from being about halfway through, and I accidentally have left Brothers open for at least four or five-ish hours.
Now, getting down to the actual content, I have to first say that I honestly saw the ending coming a mile away. And then I accidentally saw a spoiler that confirmed my theory when I was nearing the end. This did not at all soften the blow or lessen my experience in any way, so hey, MAJOR props to this game and the people who put it together. They really know how to design and I am thoroughly impressed.
This game's dialogue is nonexistent- the characters communicate through very purposeful-sounding gibberish, but they have very clear, deliberate story and emotion behind them. That's one thing I absolutely applaud about this game, and I think it was a very smart choice. For me, no actual voice acting using a current language could possibly trump this unusual but very fitting and beautifully executed method of communication.
The controls are very simple and easy to pick up on, and thanks to the really awesome design of the voice acting, anyone who speaks any language can probably play this game just fine.
A very important note- expect some dark themes in this game. It's not a fluffy adventure thing where you always feel triumphant and justified. This game doesn't care about your preconceived notions of traversing and saving the world with two cool brothers. It just does not care.
I played this game on my PC, using the keyboard. I was first trying to play this game using a controller, but the controller wasn't cooperative. I do indeed understand that this may have somehow made the game not as fantastic for me as it was for others, but despite maybe making some maneuvering tedious, I don't really see how a controller could make Brothers any better than it already is, so if you're more comfortable with a controller or a keyboard, I say stick with it. But if you have access to a controller, definitely give it a whirl and just feel it out for yourself which method you prefer.
Two notes I want to stress about this game (the second one I didn't really bring up above):
- It is emotional and beautiful and its core idea and communication of are absolutely brilliant. I
the story aspect of this game.
- You will see some things that may make your eyes roll into the back of your head, like a patch of rock that is a bright white sort of color, compared to the darker rock that makes up the entire rest of the wall, a turtle you somehow can't pick up because it's too close to the edge of a rock wall, a rock with a pitch black shadow, some absolutely asinine deaths on occasion for absolutely asinine reasons. These are mild and the game is very forgiving with its checkpoints and overall puzzle-like gameplay. Don't let this stop you from playing the game- just work past them. However, if the occasional inconvenience is just not your slice of pie, read some other reviews maybe, and see what you think. Maybe don't get this game if you're prone to frustration at setbacks.

Torchlight II has a charming style, and all the game elements synergize into a polished product, not what you would expect for a inexpensive indie title.
Ultimately at the end of the day Torchlight II has what I want from an ARPG:
-You feel like you acomplished something and you want more- to see the next dungeon/boss/loot pile
-the gameplay is fun- the spells/weapons/combat are fun. Also its fun to play with others.
More notable features:
- I like the artwork style, its distinctive and fits the mood of the game, which is a bit silly, but rich with detail.
Some of the story cutscenes are nicely 2d animated, which adds to the character of the game.
- 4 distinct classes, each with 3 talent trees that let you play your own style. Also the talents you can pick are based on character level, not abnoious prerequistite talents.
- a variety of weapons for each class, including dual wielding.
- everyone has a combat pet, that doesnt suck, and doesn't require micromanagment. You can upgrade the pet with items and spells. You can also send your pet in to town to sell junk while you keep slashing away.
- Animations are solid, spells are distinctive
- Audio and music are good and fitting to the game.
- I haven't experienced any bugs or perfomance issues.
- Items are upgradeble with enchantments and gems
- I have not looked into specifics mods, but I know by the game's reputation that it has an excellent modding community with lots of great mods that add to the replayability of the game.

Thief has aged very well, and it is still one of the better stealth games around.  In fact, it's far more advanced than and superior to the entire Metal Gear Solid franchise.  It boasts a distinct, wonderful style and really encourages exploration.  Levels are very large and non-linear, so you'll have plenty of ways to sneak around.
Gameplay mechanics are what you'd expect to find in a good stealth game, including but not limited to dynamic light sources that can be disabled, smart AI whose vision is actually affected by lighting, almost endless object interaction, you can carry and hide bodies, lockpicking is included, doors accurately block out sounds, good climbing system, the list goes on.  Play this game and the entire franchise, and remember to think outside the box and get creative.
Must be played with New Dark and HD texture mod, both of which can be found here.

YES, my favourite game of all times!!!
I remember the day I first played the demo of this amazing game. A dark and rainy day, as if it was made for gaming. I finished the demo after 2 hours. I explored as much as possible.
And played it through again after finishing.
The day the game finally came out I stood up early and was at the shop an hour before they opened to buy that game. I was not disappointed.
Since that day I have played "Thief: the dark project" more than 30 times. No other game ever made me so addicted. I made 1-2 speedruns for my own, explored the hell out of the game, played every difficulty. I love beeing a stealthy thief... Even my brother still plays it, though most old games he defines as "ugly junk".
Ok, enough of being a fanboy. Let's go to the core of the game.
Technical:
You are right if you think that this game is looking old. The game was made in the late 1990s and you can see that games developed quite much since then.
(Thanks to a quite active modder-scene several mods have been released that make the game better looking.)
In my case I don't care about that, because the game lives by a fascinating atmosphere, not by it's graphics.
The sounds are amazing for the time being released. It is quite interesting how "surround" the sound is. And well, this game is the example for "footsteps". Listening to them you can define how far an enemy is, how loud you are and how much attaction you will get. So leave your stepdance-shoes alone and take the "sneakers"...
Gameplay:
The controls work quite good, the stealth system is the best I've seen in a game so far.
You should use the shadows (It has some reason the subtittle is "the DARK project"), avoid noise, steal as much as you can and never be seen by the guards. Else the game will be quite short... So stay in the dark.
You will see it takes a lot of patience for this game. Looking for gaps in the patrols, seeking the dark corners of a house, most time hidden. If you love modern shooters do me a favour and buy them, but not THIS game...
The "hud" of the game has a small bar, that shows you how visible you are. A revolutionary concept in it's release. Did I mention: "stay in the dark"?
Loot is essential to buy stuff for the next level. Every worthy thing you steal will be sold and the money will be added to your funds. Buy a moss-arrow? Go for it. Buy some flash-bombs? Here you go. You need an water arrow to put out torches? You're welcome.
Story:
Well, I won't spoiler anything here now. You are a thief in the "middle ages". Stay in the dark and steal as much as you can. The rest you will see...
To come to an end:
A great game (in my case THE greatest game of all times) worth buying it (even after so many years).
...
...
...
Did I mention: Stay in the dark?

The first time I played this game was back in 1998 when I had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Pentium III with an 8MB graphics accelerator S3 Trio, which was completely incapable of running the game in its glory. Had to play it in software rendering to play it. Even with that compromise in quality, the game offered absolutely amazing immersion factor and gameplay mechanics, meaning no two game modes can be the same. Especially at Expert difficulty, when you're forbidden to kill anyone and are required to accomplish additional objectives, this is where the lore of the game truly shines.
Fast forward 15 years, and I'm amazed at the level of support this game has garnered from its fans. There was a patch recently released by the loyal fan community, which pretty much fixed the game and made it compatible with modern hardware. Running windows 7 with quad core processors, latest GPU technologies & gobbles of RAM, alongwith a 1080p widescreen monitor, no problem. The patch fixes them all. There's even support of OpenAL for Creative's old Audigy 2 ZS cards which makes full use of EAX sound effects which we haven't heard of since XP days. It so good to finally play and listen to the game the way it should be after so many years.
If you're a fan of first person sneakers, and haven't yet played this game. Do yourself a favor and buy it. Games like these only come out in decades, as the sad demise of its deveoper studio meant nobody took the reins and pushed the franchise forward until now. Hopefully, the new development team can do full justice to the game franchise, though the absence of Stephen Russell is extremely unnerving. He was and always will be the voice of Garrett.
Highly recommended.

I had my eyes on this visual novel since it was released on Steam. The concept really caught my attention, it all seemed so intriguing. But in the end there were a few elements that both pleased and bothered me at the same time.
From what I understand this is the first game of a three part series which still is in production. Code 01 had a great start, with a good introduction of the characters and of what was happening. The narrative is from the point of view of the MC, Hiroki. I liked the fact that his character was voiced like the others, that made me care more about him (maybe that’s not relevant here. But well, I enjoy a lot when MCs have an actual face, voice and a personality, and don’t act just like a “viewer” in the story, they actually do stuff). Anyway, it gets more interesting and intriguing especially when Reina appears; everything changes quickly, and now Hiroki, his friend Kakeru, and Reina are caught in the middle of something bigger than they could’ve imagined.
Then the story reaches its middle, and it gets…
A s*hitton of new characters appear (and never show up again), taking the attention from the sci-fi theme; the reader spends a significant time learning about all these new people that will disappear and won’t do much (or nothing at all) to impact on the story. They might (at least I hope) have a great importance on the following titles, but honestly, they weren’t necessary on Code 01. It just made things confusing and like I said, it branched out too much of the sci-fi theme and it suddenly became a “let’s meet new friends” theme. I have nothing against those kinds of story, in fact I enjoy and I read a lot about them. But I wished that Code 01 had sticked more with the sci-fi and suspense, just like it started. Hopefully Code 02 and 03 will be more dynamic.
Overall, I enjoyed the game. The ending was predictable tho. Still, I recommend this game because the concept is interesting and I believe that this story has a potential, with the possibility of getting a better and less rushed script in the future.
6/10. Also, the art style and BGM are great. VA is awesome too and even despite the flaws I mentioned above, it made me enjoy the story and empathize with the characters.

tl;dr:  I feel like this could have been at least a decent game if the developer had spent another 6 months or a year cleaning up everything.  The story needed lots of editing to give it a single strong theme that gives the reader information gradually, instead of trying to info dump at the beginning and end.  At least then I'd be able to recommend to to fans of the chuunibyou* genre.  As it is, the story is all over the place.  The art could also have gotten some more polish in that time.
This is not a sci-fi story or one about coping with death.  Any of the descriptions on the page are likely to lead you to believe that, but after the first chapter any pretense of being a serious story falls apart.  Fundamentally, this is a chuunibyou* story.  Lots of random super powers?  Check.  Protagonist goes from zero to hero?  Check.  Mystery organization trying to take over the world?  Check.  Lots of angst and screaming?  Check.  Have to save the world?  Check.  Big bad villain that tells his plans at the very end?  Check.  Big bad villain that tries to recruit the protagonist too?  Yeah, there's even that.  We've even got a blue-haired, emotion-less wind-up doll just to finish things off.
Ok, so it's a chuunibyou* story, but if you like those, then it could still be good right?  Not particularly.  "Memory's Dogma" spends too much time trying to pretend that there's actually a serious mystery, which keeps the action from flowing well.  The story could really use some editing throughout.  There were tons of scenes that ran way longer than they needed to, there are tons of random descriptions of unimportant things (e.g. 3 screens of description about how to copy files on their MRDs/computers.)  Several of the characters could have been cut completely and the story would have been better for it.  The three police officers and two girls that are dressed like they're up for some cosplay were pretty much pointless to have around.  But, hey, at least the pen that Reina carries around in her pocket got used... once.  Way too much superfluous material here. A sequel might make use of some of it, but that doesn't seem likely.
The final conclusion is also rather unsatisfying:
There were also numerous scenes where you might think that the action's really going to get going, only to find that the scene ends without resolving anything and the characters are back in the same position they were in before.
The technical side looked better, but there were a number of places where it felt like the game was rushed out the door.  The background art is almost invariably impeccable.  You can see texture on objects and detailed shadows.  At least until you get to the lake scene and the tree looks like it was thrown in a half an hour.  The rocks there are even worse, and look like they didn't even get 5 minutes of work.  But the vast majority of the backgrounds are amazing to look at.
The character designs for the women are great.  Unfortunately, they look like they were scanned in from paper and digitally colored, but no one took the time to clean up the line work before compositing onto the digital background.  The result is that you can frequently see the different in quality and style.  Oddly enough, Reina has a couple of holes near the bottom of her shirt when she's facing away from the viewer.  These allow you to see the background through her.  The guys look like they got even less love.  The quality of the art on the guys is noticeably lower than that of the women.  Add in the fact that the mens' heads are smaller than the womens' and things look really bad there.  Despite the amount of time that was clearly spent on all the art work, you can also see aliasing all over the place where the dev clearly upscaled some low resolution art work.
The music didn't do much for me, though game music rarely does.  The only track that stood out was one of the battle tracks that sounded like an odd mix of electronic and 8-bit hashed together.  The voice acting was great, exactly what you would expect from veteran professionals.  The translation was also good,   There were a couple of typos and questionable translations, but nothing egregious there.
And for those people who care about such things, there are two shots with nudity.  One for Sorano and one for Reina, though in neither case will you be able to see their naughty bits.  There's also a scene with torture in it, including cutting off a finger with gardening shears.
*

I first started playing this game when it came out in 2010.
I still play it frequently, +7 years later.
This is, without a doubt, the best game I have ever played.
I remember going over to a friends house, back in 2010, to play it on his fancy computer, switching off every death. Once I could afford my own computer that could play it, I sunk even more time into it.
Nothing in the game really stands out as special (other than the mod community), but the sum of the whole is something unique, alive and full of choices. This is still the sandbox game. I say this because if you simply start a game up, stay in the city and come back the next day or two and look at the game map, it will be vastly different each time. The world feels alive, you are a nobody at the start of the game, no one has time for you or wants to speak with you. Lords will insult you regularly, in some mods, good luck even getting into the citadels without renown. But, after forging friendships, making enemies and gaining renown, you will notice how other lords will treat you. Suddenly, an offer for vassalship is sent to you from a king, a major lord in your faction wishes you to marry into his family, noble knights turn a good word to you due to your honor rating. The progression is truly beautiful.
Possibly the best part of this game is the modding community and how easy the creators made it to mod. Instead of Bethesda's mindset of "oh well the mod community will fix this buggy, rushed, mess" there is the mindset of "let's make this as easy to mod as possible". And because the engine supports it so well, some truly amazing projects have been completed on this now (relatively) ancient engine. Mods can either do minor fixes, or drastically change the gameplay mechanics. With the hundreds that exist, there's always something new to try, always someone pushing the boundaries of what people thought could be done with Warband.

I'm not really a fan of Heavy Metal (I like the instrumentals, dislike the vocals).  I'm also not a fan of Jack Black (Annoying).  However, this is a great game, even if you don't like either of these things.  It is funny and very creative, combining Action and RTS into one game.

That way, you can cross off the one's you've found.  I didn't do this until about half way through my playthough and couldn't find/keep track of everything I had found.  The game doesn't help you keep track of any of these things.

I kind of want to not recommend this game....
I have a love hate relationship with Jack Black, well not really Love hate, more like Hate Hate, I'm just not a fan of his, but at the same time I liked him in Goosebumps, and I like him in this game for the most part.   He's not an awful person, I just find his persona to be a bit annoying.
At the same time I like Metal music, I'm not an uber fan, and I feel like at times this game expects you to be an uber fan of Metal music to really love this game.  Since I'm not at that level, I still enjoyed the music, but banking so much on one style of music is a pretty gutsy move.
The story feels like it almost lags in the second half of the game, what began as a really interesting and funny premise seems to be monotonous in the second half.   You go from a gorgeous landscape to well three rather dull locations.  The game switches from the action adventure feel to more RTS battles which each feel quite dull especially after you had a Zeldaesque experience.
And finally there's the gameplay.  I like Zelda, and I mostly like RTSes, Brutal Legend though found a way to make me kind of hate it's gameplay as a mix of the two.  The RTS sections aren't exactly thrilling, and the adventure parts of the game are dull.
So clearly I dislike it right?
Well the first half of the game has a lot of great moments.  While the second half really isn't as good, the first half is pretty sweet, the second half just is ok.  The gameplay as an RTS isn't annoying like many RTSes and it allows you to fight instead of just being an RTS, so it's not fully committed to RTSes, where some games are all or nothing, and the final battle is kind of cool and different.  It's not a battle you can just win, but you have to just barely survive, if you know how (and if you don't, you'll have to figure it out)
The metal in the game is awesome.  Having Ozzy Osbourne have a cameo is brilliant, so much of the music is awesome, and the story is quite metal.  In fact the entire sound and music in the game is AMAZING.  Definitely worth playing.
And as I said I'm not a huge Jack Black fan, but I liked him in this.  So that worked.  Even his over the top antics works great for when you're doing a stage slide past an enemy and grinding on a guitar.
This is a game where I recommend it with some big caveats.  If you don't like heavy metal (or just metal/rock in general)  you're going to have a bad time.  If you don't want to play an RTS (because make no question about it, this is an RTS even if it starts off as an adventure game) you're going to have a bad time.  If you want a really strong story, you're ... you get it, right?
But at the same time I'm not a huge Tim Schaeffer/Double Fine fan, and most of his games leave me a little flat.  This game really made me happy, even if it's not perfect, so I recommend it, but you really have to understand that even the demo doesn't give a good representation of the final product, and that does kind of annoy me(the bait and switch).  But if you want to see a new take on an RTS, or hear some awesome Metal music while playing a game, this is really your only option.

First game in the thief series, the story revolves around the master thief Garrett as he, unwillingly, gets sucked into a conflict between two of the more powerful factions in The City, a sprawling steampunk metropolis. As the title suggests, the primary goal in the game is to rob a variety of places of their conveniently large stacks of money with your name on it. The game was the first to take FPS game mechanics and apply them to a less combat-oriented game. Though there are plenty of opportunities to fight in the game, the highest difficulty levels require the player to manage to jump through an assortment of hoops without killing anyone. The game doesn't look beautiful by today's standards but does run without a problem usually and this edition contains several new levels not found in the original game. The mission videos, incredibly well done considering the technology limitations at the time, may not play without some custom troubleshooting in some cases but can be viewed on YouTube if it is too much trouble to fix. The game is one of my all-time favorites and the following games are equally well done. The bundle containing the three games released so far is relatively cheap and a fourth game (a reboot) is due to come out this year and is currently available for pre-order.

While I still plan on putting hundreds of hours into this entry, just like the previous ones, I'd like to write a review on my initial impressions.
As a next-gen fighting game, Tekken 7 is miles ahead of much of the competition, in performance, content, and mechanics. The combat feels more fluid than any Tekken before, though it's a shame we may never get a Tag Team game on Steam, because those combos were the♥♥♥♥♥♥ ! Inputs are very wonky on keyboard, so do yourself a favor and either use a controller or buy a good fight stick.
Each fighter is very unique; and while the customization items can make characters completely unrecognizable, each was distinguishable by their varied move sets. This is one of the least intimidating fighting games ever, but it still retains the depth to make the pros feel pro.
I was never really into the story or lore of Tekken, but the plot in 7 feels above average for the series. It's confusing as hell, don't get me wrong; and it can't hold a torch to the excellent stories of Netherrealm games. However, for long-running fans of the series, it provides some great character moments and epic fights. I haven't completed the entirety of the story plus all character chapters, so my opinion may change depending on the ending.
Lastly, the online is stellar. The netcode is great, for the most part. Bugs and lag haunt some overseas matches, but it's still manageable. For newcomers, even quick play will kick your butt; but keep trying and one day you will join the gods of Tekken, a.k.a the pretentious a-holes. Quick note, though. Do NOT use Rage Arts in online. It's generally frowned upon, since the whole feature is kinda game-breaking. It may be tempting at times, but keep your fingers away from that bumper and you will show more self-restraint than most of the newcomers. (Rage Drives are fine, though!)
The price is a bit steep, though this game is more complete than most fighting games recently. At the price, I'd give Tekken 7 a 4/5. Great combat, fun roster, hype music, and DECENT ONLINE help sell the latest entry in this legendary series. With a price drop of about 10,000 Won (About $10 USD for the American plebs) and some nice DLC, this game could easily be elevated to a 5/5.
Also, why the heck is Eliza not in the season pass? ;-;

I was a backer of Memory's Dogma because I was captivated by its concept, art, and PV, and I am glad that I could be a part of realizing this visual novel's release. While the visual novel indeed has its shortcomings, I still very much enjoyed its storytelling and its conveyed messages, which I think are the more important parts to a VN than its execution.
I tend to write a lot, so bear with me heheh
Let's first talk about the things that needed more work, the execution. The sci-fi plot attempts to tie together the concept of human hidden potential, combining genetic engineering and superhuman abilities, and the possibility of digitizing memories. After finishing the game, I was convinced that the main sci-fi focus was the former, but I can't forget how I wholeheartedly believed in the beginning it was about digitizing memories and its villainous uses and later felt a little betrayed. There was also a little "inequality by genetic difference" mixed in there, maybe it was part of the writer's inspiration. So, if you are looking for a game all about digitizing memories, this is not for you.
Although I liked them all personality wise, the side characters' purpose and design were of questionable quality. The biggest problems were Akane and Ema. Why were they partially cosplaying (real weapons)? What was this organization that they were in? Read on and plot holes linked to those two keeps appearing. The police officers group didn't make much of a sound and pretty sure was just there to pad for the development of the main characters. Loved Haruna's CV though; the fact that she looks like Misaka from Railgun is probably not a coincidence heh. The miko took me out of immersion as well. It felt like she was using a little knife chipping away at the 4th wall. However, I did enjoy Aoi's role, she was nicely done. Hopefully these plot holes will be addressed in sequels.
Near the ending, I was praying to the lord to not strike down and give me a deus ex machina, and BAM it happened, and now I am still troubled over whether or not it was done well. It provided a definite wrap for the ending, and it served some purpose in reinforcing central themes, but it did seem out of place.
WHY was there a dubstep track in the soundtracks? I loved every other track EXCEPT the dubstep one. Thank goodness it only came up during short action sequences. Out of everything, this was the most immersion breaking thing in the whole game.
The spellchecking team did not do their job perfectly. Probably rushed. C'mon guys, I paid over the listed price, and I didn't get a game with perfect spelling?
The engine was not friendly to me. First, I wanted to change the text box visibility, but somehow changing it made it permanently invisible (no box, white text against bright BG), so I just defaulted it and said screw it. Second, I don't know how, but clicking on the tips in some specific fashion locks the game up, and I had to reload previous saves multiple times. Plus there was also the time the text in the save/load screen strangely appeared the reading log.
Onto the good points so let's turn that frawn now. Art 10/10, loved it. Day/Night environment CGs are a requirement in current day VNs, and this was wonderfully done. CGs at key points in the story also greatly induced immersion. Music 9/10. I will probably use the OST as BGM while I'm doing school work now. Voice acting, 9.5/10, only CV I didn't like was Sigma's, whose voice I found lacked enthusiasm. Other than that everyone was on point the entire way through.
One thing I want to especially praise is how the VN makes its branching choices tied tightly to the central theme. For mechanics I like the timer on the branches, making it even more of a test on how well you are reading and how well you remember. The choices in this game made me think back more than other VNs have, made me question why I made the correct or wrong decisions. You should quicksave, but make sure you know that making the correct choice is Not the point.
I enjoyed the storytelling and the main characters' development. I cared about all the characters, and the characters cared about each other. Hiroki and Reina were in the spotlight, and their development were well paced and flowed smoothly.
I realize that I pointed out more flaws than I praised the game, but that's because I am hoping for a better sequel. The VN is nowhere near perfect, but it is still a nice read, definitely recommended for those who seek for a little struggling and suffering in their games.

For once, we have a visual novel on Steam which can stand on the strength of its story and characters, and not just on the size of its female cast's breasts.

5/10 - A Mediocre Visual Novel held back by a limited engine and various design flaws.
Game Length: 2.5-4hrs
Story:
Before going too far, please be aware that like many sci-fi stories, many prediction's of society's future, usage of science, and other related items are incredibly questionable, so please take the game's science and logic with a lot of salt. With that said, the story itself is a fairly typical story of a guy trying to save his girlfriend and uncovering a much larger situation that involves super powers and large organizations. The writing itself is passable with events passing by at a comfortable pace, but very little attempt is made to make viewer entertained. The character's dialogue is very much just focused on the task at hand with almost 0 jokes made.
The story does offer a few decision points, but they either lead directly to a bad end or doesn't matter at all. As a result, you really have to wonder what was the point of making decisions, and you might as well treat it as a linear novel.
Engine:
Probably the worse part about this game because the system is fairly barebones. It has your standard save, load, quick save, quick load, skip, auto and backlog. However, it doesn't have a lot of nice features like jumping to next decision, jumping to next scene, rewind,  or even a scene select. This becomes a major issue when you hit a bad end and are forced to go back text that takes skip 5min to catch up to where you where and worsely make other timed decisions that could lead to a bad end.
Talking about bad ends and decisions, the decision system in this game is slightly flawed. Almost every decision in this game is timed, which is fine, except you can press quick save/load from the bottom of the screen during this section, making that functionality useless. As a result, you can't use quick save/load to sample both choices but are forced to one of them and hope you made a save before hand to test the other choice.
Music/Sound:
Fine for the most parts, but there were some questionable sound effects like a sword cutting glass that is described as painful to the ears has a sound effect of someone thumping on a door. There were not many moments where things felt out of place, but on the other hand, there wasn't a time I was blown away by the music. On the flip side, the voice acting was great.
Art:
Decent, not an amateur artist but also nothing that blew me away. However, there were times in the CG where you can see jagged edges or parts looking a little rough caused by rushing or bad editing.
Conclusion:
For $15 this is an incredibly difficult sell for the length and quality. If this game dropped under $5, it might be worth checking out just to sample, but otherwise, there are probably better uses of your money and time.

Pros
+ Whatever server issues they had on release are ALREADY fixed, so no worries there
+ Excellent sound (Shooting, voice, footsteps, etc)
+ Shooting is quite fun and responsive (Also the ragdolls are immensely satisfying)
+ Reload animations are pretty good
+ Uniforms are majestic and accurate AF
+ Naval battles are also really good
+ AMAZING light effects, actually affects battles that wear into the night/dawn

I recommend this game even in its early access state and implore all Warband: Napoleon players that the grass is indeed greener! There's already a healthy population and servers are active 24/7 but the more the merrier!
