An above average game.
You play as two brothers trying to save their father and control them simultaneously while trying to work your way around the landscape, which invariably leads to puzzle-solving, platforming, and some parkour.
I liked how the game took so many twists throughout the story, as it starts off lighthearted but eventually it takes a turn out of nowhere to some crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥and gets surprisingly dark, which really helps eliminate the tedium and repetitiveness that these puzzle platforming games are often plagued with.
However my two main issues with this game are:
One, these brothers are ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, and when I say ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s I mean REALLY big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. Throughout the entirety of the game they harass villagers, break♥♥♥♥♥♥ steal livestock, steal vehicles, PURPOSELY MURDER creatures, DESECRATE the dead, and BATHE IN BLOOD just so they can save their father; how is ANYONE supposed to end up liking these main characters?
Two, I can't see why this game is held by a lot of people to be more artistic than any other regular game out there. Sure the game looks nice, but just because a game looks pretty and plays differently than other games DOESN'T make it any better artistically, and I think the games price (about fifiteen dollars) is a tad steep for the game you get. And honestly, the game's premise is very generic. The story is basically "father falls ill, sons go on a quest to find medicine to cure it" and that formula goes pretty much how you would expect it to. Even though the game does take a lot of twists and turns, the ending ends up being very predictable, and the game fails to try and make you care for the brothers other than with its cheap gimmick of controlling both brothers at once.
Overall I'd recommend buying this game if you like platformers or like these sort of "fancy" storytelling games, no offense towards those types of games and the people who like them (I am one of them), but acknowledge them for what they are and don't think just because these games have a different style than most other games they're somehow "great art".
EDIT: Playing this game with the keyboard is fine, don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

The thing about stories is that they are not strictly Point A to Point B affairs. It's the journey that makes the narrative, not the reaching of Point B. Asides, characters, and details are there to bring protein and flavor to a narrative. If you do it right and know when to stop your narrative or reach Point B, then you can make a story really, really good.
Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons does not know its limits and does the video game equivalent of not knowing how much is enough, resulting in a game where nothing really happens for half of its play time.
So before I tell you why I don't recommend it, here's what I do like: It's got a very movie-like feel to how it shows and conveys its story (Josef Fares, a filmmaker, collaborated with Starbreeze for this game). I like the art-style, the way the point-of-view is set up and the way it tells its story with no discernable dialogue. It reminds me of a short from the always-excellent The Animation Show DVD compilations. The storyline, when it's not being stretched out to an unsustainably thin pace, is classic fairy-tale stuff with stakes that get properly set up. The puzzles are not hard, but they are fine when paired with the challenge of controlling two characters at once. You can pretty much distill all the things I like about this game to 'everything that is not the pacing'. So if I like everything else about this game, why am I not recommending it?
Here's the lone, fatal flaw: It goes nowhere for half of its playtime. What should have been a series of short scenes fleshing out the world ends up being an extremely boring trek through caves and forests. Of course, you can say that about virtually any game, but that's usually covered up with gameplay. But in Brothers, the gameplay here doesn't quite do the job of lifting the game above the 'endless road-trip' feel, pitting the game into a slough of mediocrity past the first fifteen minutes. And this is for a game that supposedly takes three hours to complete! I've pretty much finished half of it and it's still taking its sweet time advancing, like a tour guide taking the most circuitous route for an 'interesting pieces of litter I found in the forest' tour.
And when it does start showing interesting stuff, it zooms right past it! There's all these neat little set-pieces that can be fooled around with, but they're very insubstantial, and once they're done it's time to GET BACK IN THE CAR AND PLAY SLUG BUG WITH YOUR LITTLE BROTHER FOR ANOTHER LONG STRETCH OF ROAD.
I mean, hats off to Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons for being a wonderful game for all these little moments, but it finally wore my patience down to the point where I don't want to play it anymore.

CHALLENGE.
This game is really hard. I like it, because there was no dumbing down for consoles when games like this were around, which means it's nice and hard. (well,  depending hehe). You can get lost, but if you use your brain and study the map, you can 'figure it out'. Make sure to check for secret levers and false panels, hidden passageways, for they more often than not lead to loot or an easy gain.
GAMEPLAY.
The more loot that you manage to find in each mission, the more equipment you can buy for the next job; Therein lies the reward for your efforts. Being conceited as I am, I personally like completing the game having killed not a single soul, which is possible to do. However, Garret has a Bow and an array of Arrows at his disposal, if you just can't resist the urge to snipe that unwitting guard!
Timing is everything. You can rush in like a steam train, but that is just not the behaviour of a Master Thief now, is it...Also, if you play on Expert, then you cannot kill anyone, adding a lesson in Master Stealth. Enjoy :)
INTERFACE.
The maps are basic handwritten suggestions, aimed at giving you a hint rather than a dumb arrow pointing you the way. The key bindings take a little getting used to. But I am a veteran and I can tell you they ARE easy to get used to. There is free reign on personal key binding. You can save many configurations, depending on how you play. Okay, so the physics are a little rough and ready, but this was the cutting edge of technology and it is all about the stealth. Get used to how the player behaves in the environment and you won't have a problem.
GET IT?
If you like games with a real challenge, requiring patience, a game that delivers punishment for idiotic decisions, immersive and scary environments with appropriate abience and music, Levels that are varied and difficult, then the Thief series is certain to please you.

Shortly put? This is one of the best stealth games that you will ever play.
But for those who want more than that:
Gameplay:
Let's put it like this: If I was ever going to become a thief and steal anything that's not nailed down in a fortified palace, I imagine it would feel pretty damn like Thief Gold. What I love about the stealth in this game is that it's realistic. While a game like Metal Gear Solid decks you out with a soliton radar and boots that make no noise whatsoever, Thief forces you to rely on your own senses and instinct. You must lean to see enemies around a corner. You must be aware of the surfaces you walk on, as certain surfaces make more noise than others. You must freaking press your ears against doors to HEAR if there's an enemy in the other room! It's absolutely fantastic and incredibly enjoyable. 10/10
Soundtrack:
Not so much a soundtrack, more like ambience. It makes sense that blaring music would feel intrinsically wrong in a stealth game and Thief realises this, so music is kept to a minimal. Where there is music however, it perfectly suits the scenario- case in point the mission in the opera house. On the other hand, there are instances where the same loud music is repeated again and again, and you find stealth has suddenly become much harder: in a negative way this time (case in point- the freaking first part of the downwind thieves guild mission). 7/10
Story: Captivating. The first few missions feel, admittedly, a little disjointed and unrelated, but eventually the main plot reveals itself and it is a spectacle to behold. I for one very much enjoyed it. 8/10
Extra content:
Thief Gold improves on The Dark Project in that it brings three new missions. One completely unrelated to the story and two that fit nicely into the story (The mages tower mission is probably the best mission in the game!) 9/10
Overall: See the first few sentences of this recommendation. 10/10

Diablo II ate so,
many hours of my life, and, so far as developers go, this is the true heir to that glorious lineage, not Diablo III.  And yet, somehow, Torchlight II utterly fails to recapture the magic for me.
Perhaps Torchlight II is undercut by its graphics, which strive to be cartoonish in some ways and grimdark in others, and don't end up achieving either.  Perhaps I am bored by the skill trees; they seem heavily loaded with area-damage effects that feel interchangeable.  It could be that the flexibility with which each class can be built (any class can use any weapon, except some uniques, and learn any spell) drains them of their individuality and homogenizes the experience.  Maybe it's that the plot is uncompelling, or the monsters are a uninspiring parade of not-especially-menacing beasties and mooks.  It might have something to do with Torchlight's innovations to the genre (pet ownership and fishing) feeling like peripheral and unimportant add-ons.
The "magic" element of a game is ultimately a hard thing to identify.  But where I spent endless hours at Diablo II, excited at every new bit of progress I made, here progress doesn't feel thrilling, and every new dungeon area I discover brings only the dejecting promise of more slogging.

FOREVER FALL UPDATE (3.6 Hours, 5/6/2016) -- What a great update!  There was a lot of content in this one.  Extended the multiplayer and singleplayer campaign to about an hour total now. As far as the taunts go, it is great to finally have them, however each character only gets one taunt and it can get kind of repetative and annoying hearing the other teammates doing the same taunt 20 times in a row.  The new map is beautiful by the way.  And I really like the incorperation of the new enemies.  Keep up the great work RT!
ORIGINAL REVIEW (2.1 Hours, 5/5/2016) -- I love this game.  The combat is probably my favorite part... blending aspects of Kingdom Hearts and Dynasty Warriors.  The music is amazing, and the voice acting (though there isn't that much voice acting) is solid and engaging.  It's really cool how the gameplay runs like a Left 4 Dead combined with Kingdom Hearts.  Also, unlike most games nowadays there really aren't any bugs (at least none that I have encountered in my short gameplay so far).
I only have a few criticisms, and I'm assuming they will be fixed with the upcoming updates;  Content wise, at 2.1 hours I have already beaten the "campaign" twice, this is quite short so far, but tomorrows update may extend the campaigns length.  There also is not much of a variety of enemies, but that is generally to be assumed from early access.  It seems they are promising more enemies later on towards the actual launch.
Some things im not quite sure about (positives or negatives, you decide); The developer isn't very clear/open with the community about upcoming content.  This may be a good thing in that they are focusing more on development rather than marketing, however, it could also be bad in that there isn't much forthcoming content.  Im not sure which it is, but we will figure out soon enough.
All that aside, I have had an insane amount of fun playing this game, and it would be interesting to see where it goes with PvP / Team PvP as well.  As I said I have played through the "campaign" twice and found it very enjoyable so far.  I can see myself spending much more time replaying it with friends.  I recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a good hack n' slash game that's not overly complex and is willing to support a developer and wait a bit for new content.

This game is really very good. It is so good that from the bottom of the heart you want it to be a masterpiece. Unfortunately, it is not ("just" solid 9/10). Nevertheless, it is one of the best visual novels I played. It has very good climate. I felt protagonist, characters and story. This novel at one point quite abruptly detracts from what some call "hard science fiction" and introduces "fantasy" elements (justified within the world's science... yet still a little striking). It was the first sign that it will not be so philosophical as I hoped it to be.
Soundtrack was ideal in my opinnion. Creepy when it needed to be and melancholic when it needed to be. I love static (as in 'radio static') motives and similar (I lack words to better call it). Visuals also. Artists have done really great job.
I managed to end the game without bad ends in the first run (but I was in a constant doubt if my choices were good, which I absolutely loved!), and because of that I had a feeling that game has really very much to offer because I was really curious what would happen, if I have made other choices. I was kind of surprised that ... not much. Really, if you hope for routes for different heroines, stop (unless I missed something, but it's not likely). There is de facto route for only one heroine (also the best one :)). I have a feeling that producers had ambitions for distinct routes for every "heroine", but quality and time limitations prevented this. The duo from the novel should have got more screentime. Also, all choices in the game are timed. This surprised me in the beginning, but now I want this system in all novels I will play from now on. I noticed it makes you go for decision which is most true with you, instead of those meta-game consideration we all know to well. It makes you more engaged.
Final remarks: for me this game was more absorbing than Fate/Stay Night visual novel and felt a little similar during play. I have impression that authors had taken some inspirations from Fate and also from series such as Serial Experiments Lain.

I went into the game completely blind. I received the key from LizArts for being a supporter on Patreon, and figured I might as well try it out. It seemed to be quite a normal VN at first, but as it went along, I became more and more engrossed in the story. LizArts has done a fantastic job crafting loveable characters and providing a lot of plot twists. After sitting through an hour or two of it, I just couldn't stop playing, and well... here I am after playing it for just over 10 hours straight. It was an amazing ride and I can't wait for the sequel. Let me give you a quick idea of what you're in for...
Synopsis: The VN is set in the not too distant future, around 2030. Technology has advanced to the point where the memories of the dead can be held so that their loved ones can contact them, or in some cases, the memories can be used for criminal investigations (in the case of murders). The main character, Hiroki, is directly connected to this. He recently lost his best friend, and wants to find out what truly happened to her. He was told that she threw herself in front of a car, but he knows she wouldn't do something like that, and goes to investigate. It's soon revealed that something's not right, and well...  the rest you'll have to find out for yourself!
As for the game itself, the visuals and storytelling are top-notch. The music also sets the scene perfectly. I think the best part about all of it, though, is the writers did a very good job talking about the world and how the technology works. I really appreciate it when writers do that, because it allows the reader to become more immersed in the story. Another good VN that I can compare that technique to is the fault series, where they have a whole separate section where you can learn more about the world (its technologies, important organizations, etc.); this game does the exact same, and I really appreciate how much effort was put into that. Overall, I highly recommend this VN. It provides a great mixture of suspense and mystery. I forgot to mention, the voice acting is a nice touch. All the VAs do a great job.
Addressing other people's concerns:
- Your choices don't affect the story
This is pretty much given, since it's a linear story. It's not that kind of VN.
- Lackluster characters, the way they act at times don't make sense
I saw many people didn't understand the way the MC, Hiroki thinks. Personally, I connected with him quite a bit since I have problems with depression and all myself. When you obsess over something a lot and give up on life, you may resort to those kinds of things. For more social, problem-tackling people, that way of thinking may be hard to understand. ...For those of you who haven't played the game, you may not be sure what I'm talking about. Let's just say the game tackles some pretty dark issues, such as suicide.
As for those who aren't given much of a background (the "cosplayers" for example), I'm sure their background will be revealed in the next game. This game was very much focusing on Hiroki and Reina. Now that their story arc is finished, so to speak, I'm sure we'll get to know the other characters in the next arc. Don't let that one thing ruin your experience. The game overall was still very good.

I first started playing this game when it came out in 2010.
I still play it frequently, +7 years later.
This is, without a doubt, the best game I have ever played.
I remember going over to a friends house, back in 2010, to play it on his fancy computer, switching off every death. Once I could afford my own computer that could play it, I sunk even more time into it.
Nothing in the game really stands out as special (other than the mod community), but the sum of the whole is something unique, alive and full of choices. This is still the sandbox game. I say this because if you simply start a game up, stay in the city and come back the next day or two and look at the game map, it will be vastly different each time. The world feels alive, you are a nobody at the start of the game, no one has time for you or wants to speak with you. Lords will insult you regularly, in some mods, good luck even getting into the citadels without renown. But, after forging friendships, making enemies and gaining renown, you will notice how other lords will treat you. Suddenly, an offer for vassalship is sent to you from a king, a major lord in your faction wishes you to marry into his family, noble knights turn a good word to you due to your honor rating. The progression is truly beautiful.
Possibly the best part of this game is the modding community and how easy the creators made it to mod. Instead of Bethesda's mindset of "oh well the mod community will fix this buggy, rushed, mess" there is the mindset of "let's make this as easy to mod as possible". And because the engine supports it so well, some truly amazing projects have been completed on this now (relatively) ancient engine. Mods can either do minor fixes, or drastically change the gameplay mechanics. With the hundreds that exist, there's always something new to try, always someone pushing the boundaries of what people thought could be done with Warband.
I own three copies of this game. One I bought back in 2011 on CD. Another I bought online as a download when my CD didn't make it back from the ROK. And finally I bought this copy to futher support the developers and to not have to worry about patches. I don't regret spending a single penny on three identical copies. It does mean, that I have no idea how long I've actually played this game, but if I had to guess, it would be a number of hours expressed in four digits.
It really is that good.
So very enjoyable and satisfying. Run around with a couple hundred crossbowmen and enjoy.

My review of HoldFast: Nations At War.
Let me first start by saying that it has been well over a year since a game has been able to bring an actual smile, applause and a quality chuckle from me. I am very pleased to say that HoldFast: NAW has remedied that.
When I decided to buy into NAW I wasn't expecting more than a few hours in such a game. A quick hold-over until say the next Total War game or BannerLord. I quickly learned that I had made a mistake in judgement and as I sit here at work typing this up I can't help but feel anxious to run home a play! At a price of $19.00U.S it's a relatively cheap and for what you will be getting its well worth the purchase. So let's talk about some of the Pro's and Con's that make this game.
The first thing that will separate any quality game is many a time the Development team. As some of you may know, this is three young men working in an Indie studio, however don't let that fool you. These three men are well above their peers and have done an excellent job in programming, design, as well as production. This team knows that this game is their baby and their ticket, and they are incredibly active in and out of game with their communities. The time that I've been browsing the discussion board and every match I've played there has been a quick response as well as at-least 1 Dev showing up. This isn't one of those cases where people say "The Dev teams active with the community" and you see a reply once every three weeks to a month. No this is the real deal, daily notification kind of team!
The second most important thing is gameplay, how does it handle? While you be immersed? Gameplay is far from polished but still the game finds a way. Firstly, the game has era accurate rifles in design, as well as uniforms/music. There is a multitude of game options available as would be the norm for Line battles of the Era portrayed. One of the most interesting concepts is the Naval warfare, yes this is what you think it is. You, a few player crew, controlling a ship/boat and living out your Pirates of the Caribbean fantasies, if those fantasies were blowing the holy bajeebus out of your enemies. Pair this with the Combined Coastal siege and your day is made! Oh I forgot to mention, 150 man battles. Now think Regimental Guilds on Community Events. Oh yes I feel that cold chill as well, it's as glorious as you think.
Rifles, Muskets and other weapons while not as accurate as they were in the real world, still pose an incredibly huge threat and if played properly, a Rifleman on a ridge or a Lineman on a Line can and will hold their ground and wreak havoc on the opposing team. There are also other classes such as Musicians (Drummers/etc) who can play a few period era songs if that is your thing, and boy is it great if they are in unison playing the proper song. It really rallies the blue-berries! Then of course there are Flag-holders, Officers, whom are the most inspirational and notably are taken up by the RP guys who even in random matches can get groups in a line which is neat to see. Lastly there is the Carpenter class which I haven't played but they do have a shotgun that rocks me.
Immersion is fantastic as well, the burst of smoke as your rifle fires mixed in with the heavy sound of those era-muskets is  an ear-gasm if there ever was for a game. The Cannons, clink of shots, screams of fallen foes, and the music; provided you have a somewhat decent headset (a $20 Logitech will do you justice), will put you on the field. The game also supports dynamic weather which really changes the battle, lord help you if your fighting at night with fog, on top of the smoke from rifles. Que a bayonet to your face if so. This is early access as well so keep that in mind, this will only get better with more classes, sounds etc. -Bagpipe class is on the way-
Graphics are another thing that aren't as important but for me keep me playing a game and the reason for that is immersion. I personally have a hard time if the game looks like a potato macgyvered to shoot a musket. So what does NAW do? Well it takes it's predecessors ideas and puts them together with a realistic quality 3D artistic style. One that clearly defines the roles, the bright uniforms of the era, all the way down to the differing details of faction rifles. I'd also like to point out that it is a real treat to see the fancy uniforms of the French Grand Army, especially the Guards and Musicians. There are many other fine details such as quality grass, water, dirt and grime and the textures (other than the houses) seem to be very HD.
This all being said, it's still Early Access and the game does have it's flaws. I'll put them in order of what I've seen, and the rate at which they've impacted my experience.
Cons:
1st: There is no Auto Ban, Vote Ban, Server Kick yet for the general populous. So expect to be killed by trolls that for some reason dropped $20 to TK. Luckily this is going to be a quick fix and the Development team has responded to numerous threads, first come will be Admin controls for private servers to turn on/off Friendly fire, followed up by community Auto Ban. So that's promising.
2nd: Melee, The Melee is pretty terrible, swings miss that should have hit, and one guy with his cavalry sword can bunny-hop through 10 guys with guns and slaughter them up in 20 seconds. God save you if you try and bayonet against a Cavalry sword. This has resulted in many players filling the Rifleman class and Officer class just to use the Cavalry sword for Kill-Spam. This however has been replied to by the Development team and is the #1 priority fix and will be dropping in the next few updates.
3rd: VOIP, I like to have line battles, I like to lead. I also don't have the time to regiment stuff all day as I wish I could. So to gather a few friends, or few randoms in Community server would be nice to do. The In-game voice is hit and miss, the radius is incredibly small so chances are you'll only hear people at initial spawn. I hope to see more implemented
4th: Customization, this is coming so it's going to be fixed. It will have a realistic approach so don't plan on running with Goku Hair, a hot-pink musket, and a cat tail, but do expect good realistic gear from the era and uniforms that will help you stand out alittle.
5th: Server latency, I personally haven't experienced this but it's a big enough concern throughout the community that it needs to be addressed. Luckily the Development team hears the concerns and from day 1 have already released two updates working on this fix. More optimization required.
Lastly these are my specs, I get 50-60fps (I've gotten Lucky, there is optimization that needs done)
i7 6700k 4.0Ghz
970GTX
16GB RAM
250 SSD
50'inch Vizio TV 1080p
I really hope this helped, and wish you the best! This game is very much worth it, and the community is great aside from a few bad apples! Happy Hunting!

Usually when I consider buying a game, I take into account the time I am probably going to get out of it and compare it to the cost. I only took 2 hours to beat this game, so that means I payed a pretty steep price for this game considering. That said, this game was worth every penny. Don't pass it up because it's short, because this game is a must play.

I hear this was a bit bug ridden at the start, but 30 hours in I have yet to meet a bug with the current build. Based on what others are saying I think it's safe to say general complaints about the technical quality of the title should be discarded at this point.
As for the quality of the game as a fighter, it's just a really fantastic offering. I think I've played just about every fighter made and I'm going to say this is likely my favorite 2D fighter of all time. It does reward aggression, but it is by no means a shallow game getting by on flash and gore. It balances fun and depth with great success, and it does it looking better than anything I think has ever been done (with Injustice coming up right behind it.)
There were a lot of past MK entries where the characters started to blur together, but this one does a wonderful job of making all of the characters feel unique, and the variations mean that almost any character you want to use has a chance to fit the way you play AND be competitive with high tier characters.
I love it. I really, really love it.
***update
With news today that the PC version is not going to receive the Kombat Pack 2 content, this version of the game may have just became a sale only item. MKXL looks like it will be wrapping the game up, not just with some extra characters, but with what is appearing to be massively improved net code for online play. The early beta testing is looking very positive, but we won't be getting that. This means you will need to be happy with playing the game offline, short 4 characters, and with dated balancing (new balancing is showing up in the net code beta.)
That's unfortunate news among some really good news. With upcoming KI and SFV showing strong dev support, serious PC gamers may need to look those directions.
For everyone else, if the game goes on sale then it's still a really good buy for someone that isn't looking for online play and doesn't care if they are playing with the latest balancing. If you want to take the game seriously then you will need console, but otherwise there is still a lot of game to enjoy.

I would  like to give this game a positive review.  For all the good points, please go read any of the many positive reviews.  I agree with most the other reviewers' points concerning sound, combat, UI, etc.  There are two reasons this gets a thumbs down from me.  1)  Remapping keys doesn't work.  Well, it does, sort of.  You can add new keys to binds, but you can't remove the old ones.  The default key bindings don't go away when you make new binds, and there's no way I've found to fix that, and if you bind a new function to a default-bound key, you get the default bind plus the new bind.  EG, by default SHIFT is used for blocking.  If you bind sprint to SHIFT, it will now block and sprint, mutually exclusive functions since you can't move while blocking.  Yeesh.  And yeah, "block" is on the SHIFT key and sprint is on the CTRL key.  Double yeesh.  You know what games use SHIFT for sprint?  EVERY OTHER @#$% GAME EVER MADE.  Fortunately you can use a controler, which is the option I went with, rather than messing with decades of muscle memory.  The second reason I'm thumbs-downing this game is because, on Windows 10, on certain boxes, it crashes to desktop randomly and without warning.  A search of the net led me to a horde of disappointed gamers with the same issue.  The usual tricks, running in compatibility mode, disconecting peripherals (the game goes loopy if you've got a graphics tablet plugged in) didn't help me, and since the devs are no longer, there will be no patches.  I'd hoped, in vain, for a 3rd party patch, but couldn't find one.  From what I have seen during my anywhere-from-five-minutes-to-an-hour-before-crashing game sessions, the game looks great.  It would be nice if it was playable.

Man! This game... I spent hours playing this on PS3 and I had to get it for PC. One of the most overlooked RPG titles, it's a diamond in the rough. This game was poorly marketed, and released at a weird time. It feels generic, now, but it's a very worthy game.
If you've ever played WoW and thought to yourself, "What if I could play this just by myself?", this is the answer to that question. Cartoony, yes. Generic storyline? Yes. But, this game offers so much that other contemporary RPGs don't.
This game is nearly flawless in its execution. It's complete - the kinks have been worked out. It's a game in its prime, not like a lot of the new games which release with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of bugs. This game is 100% smooth. Movements are smooth, the quests are smooth, the graphics are very smooth. It runs well on low-spec machines and still looks FANTASTIC.
The only reason this game is overlooked is it feels generic - if you're an RPG player. But, there's only so much you can do with fantasy games, at the end of the day. This game's focus is on fun and exploration. I haven't really ever played anything quite this polished.
The inventory system is great, the leveling system is great, the story is good enough to keep you interested and the combat feels awesome - especially with a controller.
I've played a LOT of games, and I always keep coming back to this game, because it's BIG. But, at the same time, it's one of those games where you don't need to commit hours to a raid, you can just save and quit and pick up where you left off, not feeling like you missed much. Because the story line is so simple, as long as you remember the gist of what's happening, you can hop right back in.
This is the perfect game-between-games. It's not like the storyline sucks you in, but it's just a fun game to play and it feels very well done. As far as VALUE goes, dollar for dollar, this game packs a major punch and is worth every penny - imho.
The ONLY complaint I really have is I wish there was a co-op option, but then again, not every game has to be multiplayer. As far as single-player games go, this one stands out in the crowd of half-finished, half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥games, at a very approachable price, and with an easy learning curve. 100% recommend.

I got this game as part of the Steam Summer Sale. I don't get to play my games all that often, but I do not regret picking up this title. It's a little wonky at first due to the lack of PC optimization with the controls, but once you get used to the weird quirks of having to use the keyboard to go through menus, it's a great game to play. The story is pretty well fleshed out as far as I can tell, the world looks fantastic, albeit a little cartoony, and the fact that you can re-spec your character for a different playstyle without having to start a new game is really nice. The crafting system is quite nice, it's simple to use, and stays relevant from early-mid game all the way to late game. Combat can be a bit clicky/spammy, but with different combos and skill moves, you can fight however you want.
tl;dr

I've been playing this game, prior to the purchase on STEAM, so don't be fooled by the STEAM  time-log.  Don't believe the simple-minded negative reviews, that clearly are not used to "tactics".  Its a great 2D-scrolling application of a battlefield tactics game.  It is deceptively deep, in its use of special team tactics.  If your the type that builds a zerg-massing rush tactic... yeah, you probably won't like this game.  Deploy different groups of units and employ the use of support assets like Artillery and Bombers.
Recommend you play it on the harder levels, so you can appreciate the use of team and asset management more fully.

The game plays largely like a RTS on a 2D plane.  You spend money to purchase infantry/vehicle/tank/air units where you collide in a head-on battle with your enemy which is doing quite the same.  You only have so much money to work with at the start so you need to spend wisely.  I imagine the game's core enjoyment factor will be it's multiplayer which I have yet to try out.
The game almost plays itself in a sense, you have no real full control over the units you purchase, just in how many you purchase and when, which is primarily the strategy to the game.  If you purchase a bunch of infantry and your opponent purchases an airstrike, that's going to be a lot of money down the drain wasted on infantry.  Speaking of airstrikes there are several support options, such as carpet bombing, artillery strikes, cruise missiles, etc.  These aren't cheap, but they can take out nasty clusters of heavy armor rather quickly.
There is also the option to research vehicles, which is good to slow down the progression of a battle so you don't just pound the enemy with the biggest and baddest things you have on offer, and makes you try to manage your money a little more carefully.  I think once the game has the game-breaking bugs ironed out however it'll be a much better playthrough experience.  I'm honestly on the middle grounds for recommending this game or not, and the only reason why I'd lean more towards the negative side of things is only because the current day-skip bug.  Aside from that the game has many redeeming qualities, though I think a little more variance and strategy would help it a lot more.  Possibly in the form of building barricades to slow down enemy advancement or block projectiles, and really turning it into more of a chess-game where certain types of units are absolutely required to best others, because I feel many will just use the "strength in numbers" tactic, which can work, but it is a costly mistake if it doesn't.  Also a refresh timer on support would be a good idea as well, spamming artillery if you have the cash can do most of the work for you.

The game itself is amazing, and does everything Deus Ex Human Revolution does but better (Except storyline, but we'll get to that in a bit).  The gunplay seems to be brought to 2016 levels instead of Human Revolution or Deus Ex 1 levels (well it better be compared to the first Deus Ex), the new augmentations are really fun to use, and the city hub is very large and expansive, and for anyone that loves exploration, this game is right up your alley.
However, to get onto the microtransactions point, while the game would be better without them, the EXP and loot you get just by playing the game and exploring is good enough to progress without using real money, though I guess for all the doubters this could change in future Deus Ex games.
Also, on the storyline part, while its really enjoyable and intriguing, apparently ends in a cliffhanger, ending when the plot starts to really get good, so it might not feel complete at the end, in order to set up sequels.
Finally, the performance is pretty good if you're willing to spend time optimizing the game to your computer.  While I was initially really sad that I couldn't run the game on Ultra with my GTX 970, the game runs fine at the high preset, and looks basically the same without halving your framerate. Word of warning, do not enable MSAA, it will kill your frames since deferred lighting engines sacrifice good AA for better lighting. So try to look up people with similar specs with your computer in order to find out whether you can run it and what settings you can run it at.
At the end of the day, I believe that this is a pretty great Deus Ex game, despite the setting never really investigating into the Augmented and Pure people conflict as much as I would liked it to.  But despite my love for this, if your already busy playing a bunch of other games and not as big into Deus Ex as I am, maybe you should wait for a sale to get it, and hopefully a sequel will be released alot faster than 5 years, because I really do hope Deus Ex's modern games eventually branch into Deus Ex 1's story...

Torchlight II can be summed up in 2 words.............
This game I had gotten on sale shortly after I played the demo and I literally nerded in my pants. Out of all the top down RPG games I've played this is one of the greats, it's nicely balanced, graphics are beautiful, the sound is well done, and it's a joy to play for hours on end. I personally look for character uniqueness in a game, customizing the look of a character, nothing pisses me off more about an RPG than having to play as a pre made character, that to me is an adventure game. A Role Playing Game should allow you to create your character, a virtual you, and go out into the world to explore and create your own story. I will admit I wish you were able to do more customization on your character but they do give you enough to make yourself unique and as you play you do find or buy your own armor so it all works out.
Battle system is well done, battles can be both challenging or easy depending on the route you choose to play the game at, if you do the side stuff (dungeons, exploring, etc) boss battles can be fairly simple but still fun since you are the proper level or higher to fight them, if you only stick to the main quest the game can get pretty difficult (But still possible to beat). There is also a good amount of fighting styles you can implement along with the basic ranged or close and personal styles, you can literally play this game to the style you are most comfortable in. The other nice thing is that the class you choose in the beginning is only a preferred, if you choose to be a marksman and want to fight with a sword later on, you are more than free to.
The bad part of this game (If you can call it that) is you will lose hours of your day glued to your screen playing it, this thing is like a lays potato chip "Can't just play a little bit".
All in all It is really good, has co-op online or over Lan if you choose to play with friends, it's fun as♥♥♥♥♥♥ especially for a game now 2 years old going on 3. For $19.99 you are stealing this game as is, you won't regret spending the money. I give this game a 9.5/10

Can we just acknowledge the fact that this is a pretty good game? It's not quite as enthralling off the bat as Human Revolution was, but it builds into a complicated conspiracy that's just as captivating as any other game in the series. The characters are, for the most part, smartly written, there are a lot of hidden items and passages, and the gunplay is decent. I feel like there is a bit of a mouth smoothing effect going on that I wish I could turn off, but I mostly run stealth anyway. The villans are very...Squeenixy I suppose, just very stereotypical japanese super-people esque, but some of the characters are wonderfully fleshed out through side-interactions and snooping around.
So it has microtransactions! So what? It's a single player game, and some people just don't want to put in the time or energy to unlock everything.  Leave it alone. You don't have to buy anything. In fact, not once was the idea ever shoved down my throat or revealed to me in any way that pulled my attention from the game. Actually, it wasn't introduced at all. I honestly had no clue that there WERE any microtransactions until I read a negative steam review, and upon re-opening the game, realized that there was a store button in the main menu.
As far as performance goes, I will say that there is quite a bit of stuttering when first loading up a map, however I think that may have more to do with my computer than the game. I went ahead and turned off MSAA and Volumetric effects from the start, and I'm getting 50-75fps most of the time with everything turned on or to high except my textures which I turned down to medium. I'm running an AMD FX8620 at 4.0ghz, an Nvidia 670, and 8gigs of crappy offbrand DDR5. Still, the game looks pretty wonderful.
In summary, I think this game is worth what it's asking. It's a beautiful work and the designers should be proud. Yeah it's got a few bugs, but what deus ex doesn't? If you're sitting around waiting for the price to drop, I wouldn't get your hopes up. it doesn't look to be happening for quite a while.

Okay, let`s start with good sides of new deus ex game.
Pros:
Setting.
I`m satisfied with it. Better than HR but not a masterpiece, just good and I could believe in everything happened in that world. Shame that Devs couldn`t present main characters to the player which kills the atmosphere sometimes.
Gameplay.
It`s like Human Revolution 2.0 we all deserved. Not very useful new augmentations, personally I only used one of them in stealth/no kills playthrough. Cover system is much better than HR but still has some disadvantages. Enemies are smarter than in HR but still dumb as hell.
Side missions.
MUCH BETTER THAN IN HR. They are interesting, entertaining and add some info to the world of deus ex. 8/10 to side missions, -1 because of their "run there, then there, then there..." mechanics which sometimes happen like in HR and -1 because it`s not a masterpiece sides.
And that`s all for pros.
Cons:
Optimisation.
Can`t say much because I played on i7 + gtx 1080 and it ran smoothly entire game. I didn`t measure the fps but I`m sure it was 60 and higher. So I advice to just wait for a patch, that`s all.
Story.
This entire game is a prologue to something bigger,
. I sincerely hope that deus won`t end like "Assassin`s Creed"`s year/game dev policy cause story in this game is total garbage. Can`t even compare it to HR because it`ll be like "nothing vs full packed plot". Like wtf were you thinking SE?
AI and Stealth.
AI is still dumb and stealth isn`t necessary. You can maximize Invisibility augmentation and battery + buy some battery pack and you can go anywhere without alarms no exceptions. And game can`t punish this strategy. And AI... just remember HR, it`s the same but now enemies can use augmentations too, which adds some difficulty.
New energy system.
Personally, I didn`t like it. First thing they changed: player have one huge battery, not 2-5 like it was in HR but now every augmentation activation reduces maximum size of this pool which is a bit more difficult to maintain. And here goes their second innovation: it`s so many batteries in this game that you can provide electricity for the entire planet. It`s cheap, it`s common. So more hard to maintain but a lot of energy packs. Dunno, seems unpleasant to me.
Actually that`s all for this review. Do I recommend this game? If you`re a fan of Deus Ex or cyberpunk genre - buy it and you won`t regret it. If you want to get good gameplay - it`s 50/50, depends on do you want a good story with remarkable characters or not. If you are here to get a strong plot with twists - high chance of getting upset guys. I`ll give a thumb up just because I`m a fun of this series. Peace.

The seventh installment of Tekken is the ultimate realization of the series' endlessly deep and rewarding mechanics, but like many recent fighting games, it lacks the content and polish necessary to make a major impact with both noobs and veterans alike.
Tekken 7's mechanics have been slightly streamlined compared to past titles, and although streamlined has become a dirty word to those familiar with fighting games, they haven't been changed at the cost of depth. For example, holding back on the ground now initiates a safe back roll (although still punishable). In the same vein, some new characters have very simple playstyles and inputs that cater to new players, though your favorite Mishima is still just a few hand cramps away. Harada and his goons have really struck a chord offering more game to inexperienced players without anything feeling braindead or overpowered. The new screw system which replaces bound, is simple to understand and helps balance the cast. Additionally, the powercrush system opens up even more depth. Armored moves add a whole new layer of depth in the neutral, and choosing to sacrifice rage for a rage art or super allows a player to make explosive decisions in the clutch. The new slow motion-camera zoom that activates when a player has low health and nearly gets hit makes for unbelievably hype moments, showcasing the complicated three dimensional hitboxes, and clenching anuses worldwide as spectators watch in horror.
With so many amazing improvements to Tekken's gameplay, it's unfortunate how lacking the game is in all other departments compared to previous titles. The particle effects and textures look great in the UE engine, but the dull drab design of the stages (no footprints in the snow?) do them no justice. The netcode isn't bad, although the matchmaking system is quite a barebones mess. There's also an uninteresting and short story mode, strange roster decisions with lots of core characters missing, and a completely garbage customization mode that may as well not exist. Typically, these things aren't to be expected in a fighting game, but when older installments have all of these features and more, it's hard to ignore.
I would absolutely recommend this game to veterans of the series, or anyone looking to challenge themselves. Just understand that if you don't get into difficult online fighting games, you might not get your $60 worth.

This game is a very fun experience to play through.  It is still in early development and it shows, but with time this game can really shine and become something amazing.
**PLEASE NOTE:  I obtained this game as a gift and the game is in Early-Access at the time of review.  I try to be middle of the ground when reviewing but this still must be noted**
GRIMM ECLIPSE is a third person "hack and slash" game (as seen by the tags) that uses the Rooster Teeth RWBY franchise.  Players have the ability to choose who to play as between the four protagonists of the series:  Ruby, Tang, Weiss, and Blake.  In a cooperative (or solo) group the players battle through hordes and waves of enemies.  As somebody kills enemies they obtain experience points that level players up; at each level an ability point is gained.  This point can be spent to improve the abilities of the chosen character or saved for more expensive upgrades (the most costing 2 points).
One flaw with the gameplay is that it gets repetative after a few hours.  It is a fun, a truely fast paced game, but once the charm of it fades then the game begins to feel the same...
The difficulty of RWBY GRIMM ECLIPSE was slightly disappointing.  Traditionally "hack and slash" games are not very difficult so it isn't a huge deal.  Players can utilize the ranged attacks and strong attacks to blow through most enemies that the game throws at the player.  The upgrade system makes it feel like players are significantly stronger then every enemy at times while other times it feels like you are a level 1 again.  The game has a lack of difficulty settings that creates a disconnect for people who have experience with these types of games.  If a difficulty setting could be added then the game would be more appealing for both casual and players looking for a challenge.
This game as very few adjustable settings for game customization.  The video settings are very lacking in their options, there is a fullscreen button, a resolution option (with 3-4 resolutions), and a single graphical adjuster.  This isn't a big deal as the game isn't terribly resource intensive, but on lower end machines expect to play on "potato" settings on a tiny window (I mean one of the smallest I have ever seen). There is no master volume slider which can be disorienting if you want to lower every sound equally; not a big deal but is a slight inconvenience.
The performance of this game is what is to be expected from an early access game; some spots run perfectly while others produce an intense amount of lag.  During play play I would experience frame drops occasionally but only near certain spots (like near a single wall).  The nature of these lag spikes indicate that small parts of maps are not optimized well or have a lot of things to be rendered near them.  Generally my computer (containing a GTX 745, i7-4790) ran the game at frames above 50fps.
I have tested slightly with a 6 year old Dell Studio 15 laptop on the lowest resolution with potato graphics settings.  The game is playable frame rate wise but the small resolution causes the character to be left off screen at times.  It can still be enjoyable if you really want it to be...
Online play was pretty smooth with occasional jumps (to be expected from every game).  This was reassuring as it meant the game engine was well optimized for online play, a major piece of this game.
One last test system was a custom built computer with a GTX 980, i7-4790K and the general framerates were good.  There was some bazar shuddering of the camera that wasn't traditional lag on this machine (my first mentioned machine experience the same thing from time to time, but not this severe).  I do not know what caused this skipping.
RWBY:  GRIMM ECLIPSE really excels in its art style and sound design.  The game looks like the RWBY web-series, it is nice to see a game that sticks close with the material it is given.  The graphics made me feel like I was enjoying another episode of the hit series, I was hoping for this and Rooster Teeth delivered.  The scenery can look beautiful so don't just blow through the game if you decide to buy!
From a sound standpoint the game sounds like it should.  It has a pretty good balance and it sounds like what you would expect.  The only complaint was no master sound slider as mentioned earlier.
This game has a lot of room to grow but it is still an enjoyable experience.  I got through the current campaign in about an hour of game time.  This wasn't a bad thing as it is still early-access and a big update is scheduled to come out soon.  Unfortunately, this game automatically takes people back to the lobby after they get as far as the game allows and everybody loses their levels.  This was unfortunate as it felt like an hour wasted for progress sake.  I hope the final game supports a save of character feature so players don't lose their level 10 Chitty Chatty Yang Yang.
The last major complaint is how similar all the characters left.  Each of the four characters had a different cosmetic look to them but the way they feel is very similar.  Some characters might have different roles overall but at this point they all felt the same amount of "featherless".
Add content, optimize the game more, and make the characters a little bit more distinguished and the game will be improved a ton!  In its current state I do recommend buying RWBY: GRIMM ECLIPSE if you have friends who are also going to play it.  If you are not a big fan of RWBY I still recommend it if you are a fan of hack and slash games and want to try something new.
NOTE:  Over time the price will increase as the game is updated so consider soon if you want to have a lower cost for a potentially higher benefit!

How interesting and captivating the story is matters the most to me when I am reading a visual novel. I have a hard time sticking through some to the very end, and sometimes some activities in them seem cumbersome. In Memory's Dogma, I didn't quite have any of these issues, and I ended up getting invested in it pretty quickly.
My initial reasoning behind buying the game was its plot and the art style. The fact that it has voice acting is just a plus, in my opinion. But it is a very good plus for this story. The VAs did a great job and it really helped give shape to the characters and their emotions and actions.
I don't think I am capable of giving a proper analysis of the story in-depth, but I would like to highlight some important aspects about this story to help raise a point on what to expect before buying (without trying to spoil the story).
1) This starts off as a murder mystery, as implied in the title's description
2) It is not JUST a murder mystery.
3) It basically switched genres after the second in-game day.
If you wre looking for a visual novel grounded with very real questions, like 'what defines someone as being real' Or do memories make up what a person is in their entirety', then I don't think this story will satisfy you. It starts off really well in that regard, and raises some interesting and thought provoking notions of the story being told here, but it's pretty clear that by the end of it this isn't where the story was going at all. it just seemed to start out like that.
Genre switch: It still does an alright job of making the story composed, but there are times where it inadventerently forgets its self and seemed to care very little about some of the characters introduced. This isn't to say it isn't good after the switch, but it does leave a lot to be desired. There could have been far more done to make it better.
Characters: The characters were well put together and a little cliche, but it was done well so it wasn't overbearing. A quirky habit or two; unique traits each character has that don't stand out too much but are identifiable were really nice touches. And of course there are backstories!
Issues: As far as my playtime goes, my game only crashed once near the beginning. After and up until the end I encountered no crashes. I did have another issue while using the scroll wheel on my mouse to go through the text. It suddenly got locked into the archive of text, but I managed to fix this by just using a normal mouse click, and then continued using the scroll wheel. Besides these, no other issues were encountered.
I can't recommend this as a murder mystery story. The way it started off and the sudden genre change was too drastic and made the mystery aspect seem unimportant; however, as the genre it sort-of morphed into, it ened up being alright.
Was it worth the price? Almost. If the story flourished a bit more, then I would be able to recommend this game for what I expected it to be when I bought it, but as it stands, critically I cannot. As a casual reading? It's alright. So I suppose I would recommend it as a casual reading, but probably only as a casual visual novel.

I'm a patron for lizarts. Which means I've put in more money in this project than the selling price. I wish I could tell you all that this is a fantasic story, with great artwork and music. But I can't. So let me get the good things out of the way.
The voice acting is premium. If you want fantastic voice actors and that's all you care about then you're gonna love this.
The art is pretty good. I won't say it's top tier but it's not bad.
With that let's talk about the story. It's a scam. This is not a hard Scifi, this is an X-men/Heroes Plot. This is Science Fantasy masquerading behind the few brief moments of SciFi. The concept and question posed at the beginning NEVER get addressed. There are plot holes and twists everywhere, it's like trying to throw a ball straight and having it go in every direction but the one we thought it would. Up down left right, behind you. It's a story with no form and a weak foundation. I bashed my head and rolled my eyes through it.
I have 3 main reasons why I believe I wasn't able to like or endorse Memory's Dogma. They are as follows.
1. The beginning of Memory's Dogma hit home as a strong SciFi, human fundamentalist plot. We were led to believe it for almost the entire 5th day. there were no implications to suggest that it would transition into Science Fantasy and when it did it was harsh and sudden. The brashness made me lose my faith and trust in the writer. The switch to fantasy ruined any hope of seeing or feeling my humanity in the story. It shattered my suspense of disbelief, I no longer believed the events were possible inside their own world and especially within mine. Specifically the armed man and the reveal of powers brought this story into the fantasy realm and thus losing the solid foundation to ask any real questions.

2. the characters acted in a manner that was counter to realistic logic. I'll give two examples. Hiroki tried committing suicide in order to get to Sorano but why? It was common knowledge that the dead's memories are stored for 49 days after their death. Shouldn't he invested his efforts into speaking with her there? The reason given was that he was unable to face her but yet that was his goal with attempted suicide. If he believed the only way he could stand to see her was to atone with his life then he was delusional with self-hatred and grief which leads to an emotionally unstable MC.  But once he wakes up after a suicide attempt, he engages in rational conversation as if nothing is wrong with him instead of being despondent

3. There is a scene that brings together all the negative aspects of MD. That is the bombing scene and it broke me. It goes as follows: We run into the cosplayers on the street for the first time. They are looking for directions. we tell them off and no. They say they are in a hurry and then a bomb goes off. Everyone starts running, fast paced music goes. Tensions are high because our friend might be caught in the bombing. There is a police officer obstructing us. We get to the scene, and queue casual music.

Our friend that we worried about casually said hello to us, the police officers on the scene casually chat with us, there is no one else at the scene even though sirens were said to be going off and going in the direction. Absolutely no one is worried about another bomb going off, no one seems shocked, deaf, or pumped full of adrenaline, no one feels like they just risked their life and no one cares that people probably died. Let's just all sit here and have a nice cup of tea, reminisce about that bombing, and enjoy the smoke going off in our background. Mind you these are
that have never met you or your friends before and just previously tried to prevent you from entering the scene. Just casually chatting with you.

Suddenly dramatic music kicks back in. There is a swordsman coming at you, the cosplayers quickly behind him. there is a bystander in the way, let's cut her in half, and then he reaches us and we learn... That his sword is attached to his ♥♥♥♥ing arm. Once he gets five meters to the group he stops and enters a fighting stance.
the unarmed group. The police then take out theirs guns and  aim at the guy with the sword arm that just killed a civilian. No surrender, drop your weapon, put your hands up. Just take aim. Cosplayers catch up, battle scene commences, cosplayers lose. Apparently that spear is real and they too have special powers. Main heroine runs away, and MC gains magical super healing powers by Microchip that manipulates your Dna after being brutally stabbed in the stomach by the armed swordsman.

EDIT: I finished the game two days ago, a day after I bought it (faststest time for me with a visual novel), but before I make a complete review, I need to let my feelings sink in for a week. Mediterranean Chicken and Pasta
Makes: 4 servingsPrep: 5 mins Cook: 15 mins Carb Grams Per Serving: 38
Ingredients
1 6 - ounce jar marinated artichoke hearts
1 tablespoon olive oil
12 ounces skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
1/4 cup chicken broth
1/4 dry white wine
1 teaspoon dried oregano, crushed
1 7 - ounce jar roasted red peppers, drained and cut into strips
1/4 cup pitted kalamata olives
3 cups hot cooked campanelle or penne pasta
1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
Directions
Drain artichoke hearts, reserving marinade, and chop them.
In a large skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat; add chicken and garlic. Cook and stir until chicken is brown.
Add the reserved artichoke marinade, broth, wine and dried oregano.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat. Simmer, covered, 10 minutes.
Stir in chopped artichokes, roasted peppers and olives.
To serve, spoon chicken mixture over pasta. If desired, sprinkle with feta cheese.

First off, I'm going to start by saying that I've been playing Mortal Kombat since it's early days on the Super Nintendo and Genesis. Those games never failed to keep me interested, I found them more interesting than the homework I was supposed to be doing, lol. Anyways, onto my review.
What really drew me into this game was the ability to play it locally on PC with my wife and MKX's sheer crazy brutality the installment has (not speaking of the special move) The overall presentation is nice and it feels great. Yes, it is a bit slower than any previous games but it's a good slow. Granted I do prefer the faster combat of the previous game but the fighting in this game actually works to a degree, it actually feels strong and impactful.
Visually, the game is pretty compelling if you have the machine for it (and thank goodness I do!) I mean it's detailed enough to where you actually see beads of sweat on the characters, all the way down to the smaller details in the clothing. Still on visuals, there are times where there's a framerate drop while you're in the middle of fight and it could mean life or death for your character.
As far as sound goes...hmm, well there were times where I had to restart the game to fix some crackling and lipsync to sound mismatching in story mode but if you can hear through all of that, good on you.
The storyline is damn fun for sure, it's like you're immersed into a interactive movie to a large degree. I won't spoil anything for you but it was a good storyline. It takes the events of '98's MK4 on the PC, N64, and PS1 and sugar coats it with some twists and turns but the story is still the same at it's core.
I really wish I could say more but if you're looking for a game to play at parties, a fan of the originals, the need to beat stuff up after a long day at work, gore, and the pleasent sound of bones breaking this game will quench that thirst for sure.
Pros:
- Great Graphics, feels real, and looks amazing.
- Gameplay is slow, but it delivers a more impactful feel as opposed to previous installments.
- Love the amount of characters to choose from.
- The Storyline is probably the best one I've seen ever in this franchise.
Cons:
- Frequent framerate problems.
- Sounds are very crackly at times as well as lipsync mismatches (specifically in Story Mode)
- Questionable business practices.
All in all I think it's a fine addition save for the few problems I've mentioned above.

-A fantastic and memberable story that makes you feel very involved through its gameplay.
-Fun mechanics that don't feel overused as the game changes up even the simplest of obstacles as you progress.
-A pleasant interactive world which will leave you wanting to explore every nook with and how you can affect the world around you.

I didn't know what to write, so here is the wikipedia page on a chocolate chip cookie.
A chocolate chip cookie is a drop cookie that originated in the United States and features chocolate chips as its distinguishing ingredient. The traditional recipe combines a dough composed of butter and both brown and white sugar with semi-sweet chocolate chips. Variations include recipes with other types of chocolate as well as additional ingredients such as nuts or oatmeal.
The chocolate chip cookie was invented by Ruth Graves Wakefield. She owned the Toll House Inn, in Whitman, Massachusetts, a very popular restaurant that featured home cooking in the 1930s. Her cookbook, Toll House Tried and True Recipes, was first published in 1936 by M. Barrows & Company, New York. The 1938 edition of the cookbook was the first to include the recipe "Toll House Chocolate Crunch Cookie" which rapidly became a favorite cookie in American homes.
Ruth Wakefield stated that she deliberately invented the cookie. She said, "We had been serving a thin butterscotch nut cookie with ice cream. Everybody seemed to love it, but I was trying to give them something different. So I came up with Toll House cookie."A different version of events says that Wakefield is said to have been making chocolate cookies and on running out of regular baker's chocolate, substituted broken pieces of semi-sweet chocolate from Nestlé thinking that they would melt and mix into the batter. They did not and the chocolate chip cookie was born. A still different history of the cookie derives from George Boucher, who was at one time head chef at the Toll House Inn, and his daughter, Carol Cavanagh, who also worked there. Contradicting Nestlé's claim that Wakefield put chunks of chocolate into cookie dough hoping they would melt, the daughter stated that the owner, already an accomplished chef and author of a cookbook, knew enough about the properties of chocolate to realize it would not melt and mix into the batter while baking. Boucher said that the vibrations from a large Hobart electric mixer dislodged bars of Nestlé's chocolate stored on the shelf above the mixer which caused the chocolate to fall into the sugar cookie dough mixing below. He claims to have overcome Wakefield's impulse to discard the dough as too badly ruined to waste effort baking them, leading to the discovery of the popular combination.
Every bag of Nestlé chocolate chips sold in North America has a variation (butter vs. margarine is now a stated option) of her original recipe printed on the back.Every bag of Nestlé chocolate chips sold in North America has a variation (butter vs. margarine is now a stated option) of her original recipe printed on the back. During WWII, US soldiers from Massachusetts who were stationed overseas shared the cookies they received in care packages from back home with soldiers from other parts of the US. Soon, hundreds of soldiers were writing home asking their families to send them some Toll House cookies, and Wakefield was soon inundated with letters from around the world asking for her recipe. Thus began the nationwide craze for the chocolate chip cookie.
Although the Nestlé's Toll House recipe is widely known, every brand of chocolate chips, or "semi-sweet chocolate morsels" in Nestlé parlance, sold in the U.S. and Canada bears a variant of the chocolate chip cookie recipe on its packaging. Almost all baking-oriented cookbooks will contain at least one type of recipe.
Practically all commercial bakeries offer their own version of the cookie in packaged baked or ready-to-bake forms. There are at least three national (U.S./North America) chains that sell freshly baked chocolate chip cookies in shopping malls and standalone retail locations. Several businesses—including Doubletree hotels, Citibank, Aloha, and Midwest Airlines—offer freshly baked cookies to their patrons to differentiate themselves from their competition.
There is an urban legend about Neiman Marcus' chocolate chip cookie recipe that has gathered a great deal of popularity over the years. To honor the cookie's creation in the state, on July 9, 1997, Massachusetts designated the chocolate chip cookie as the Official State Cookie, after it was proposed by a third-grade class from Somerset, Massachusetts.
Chocolate chip cookies are commonly made with white sugar; brown sugar; flour; a small portion of salt; eggs; a leavening agent such as baking powder; a fat, typically butter or shortening; vanilla extract; and semi-sweet chocolate pieces. Some recipes also include milk or nuts (such as chopped walnuts) in the dough.
Depending on the ratio of ingredients and mixing and cooking times, some recipes are optimized to produce a softer, chewy style cookie while others will produce a crunchy/crispy style.[7] Regardless of ingredients, the procedure for making the cookie is fairly consistent in all recipes: First, the sugars and fat are creamed, usually with a wooden spoon or electric mixer. Next, the eggs and vanilla extract are added followed by the flour and leavening agent. Depending on the additional flavoring, its addition to the mix will be determined by the type used: peanut butter will be added with the wet ingredients while cocoa powder would be added with the dry ingredients. The titular ingredient, chocolate chips, as well as nuts are typically mixed in towards the end of the process to minimize breakage, just before the cookies are scooped and positioned on a cookie sheet. Most cookie dough is baked, although some eat the dough as is, or use it as an addition to vanilla ice cream to make chocolate chip cookie dough ice cream.
The M&M cookie, or party cookie, replaces the chocolate chips with M&M's. This recipe originally used shortening as the fat, but has been updated to use butter.
The chocolate chocolate chip cookie uses a dough that is chocolate flavored by the addition of cocoa or melted chocolate. Variations on this cookie include replacing chocolate chips with white chocolate or peanut butter chips.
The macadamia chip cookie has macadamia nuts and white chocolate chips.[12] It is a signature cookie of Mrs. Fields bakeries.
The chocolate chip peanut butter cookie replaces the vanilla flavored dough with a peanut butter flavored one.
Chocolate chip cookie dough baked in a baking dish instead of a cookie sheet results in a chocolate chip bar cookie.
Other variations include different sizes and shapes of chocolate chips, as well as dark or milk chocolate chips. These changes lead to differences in both flavor and texture.

As somebody who has been active in the Napoleonic Wars Linebattle community for over 8 years now, starting back in Battlegrounds 2, and following Mount and Musket and M&B Napoleonic Wars, I was really looking forward to the early access release of Holdfast: Nations at War and from all what I have seen so far, I have not been disappointed although you can clearly see that the game is still in an Alpha Status.
So let's start with a the pros & cons before going into the summary and recommendation:
+ The games graphics are quite nice and enjoyable, especially on high graphic settings, although I must admit that the graphic style might not be liked by everybody. The graphic details especially  are really nice and show the devotion to the game by the developers.
+ The game mechanics are, all in all, quite solid for an early access game compared to other early access games I have played so far. The game is playable and enjoyable, although you can clearly see that there is need for more updates, tuning and reworking things like the melee system.
+ The different game modes are enjoyable and already have a high variation from 'Army Battle' - which is basically the Linebattle mode - over Siege, Coastal Siege or classic TDM to full Navy Battles where you fight ship against ship. Everybody who enjoys playing in the Napoleonic era can find a play style for himself.
+ The great potential the game has to offer is also a positive argument for Holdfast in my opinion. Especially seeing the roadmap of the developers to include features like cavalry and more, I think that the game can become quite great. Although I am sure it is still a lot of work to include all the mentioned features and fixes, the current status of the game already shows the developers' devotion towards it.
- The game mechanics still show a kind of roughness, especially the melee system. There needs to be a reworking of this so that for example the melee fights become enjoyable and smooth. The hit-box detection can be quite frustrating at the moment when you hit an enemy on your screen but the hit is not counted, so your opponent doesn't take damage. The same goes for the Naval Battles where the end status of the ships is not taken into consideration for the round result - also the handling of the ships is quite weird in the sense of manoeuvring and hit reactions on enemy ships. These things need to be fixed soon, but I am confident that this is not a feasible goal.
- The problem with high server latency is something that is currently being worked on but at the current state of the game it is quite a huge problem, because it makes playing on a full server nearly impossible. But as I said, the developers are currently working on this.
- Some animations are missing or need some reworking, like for example the hit reaction in melee, which is missing at the moment. I would appreciate some reworking of the sword fighting animations since they look quite unnatural.
All in all I can say Holdfast: Nations at War is a solid early access game in which you can learn the basic game mechanics and enjoy different game modes already with nice graphics. It is a great opportunity to get an impression of battles in the Napoleonic era although some things are tarnishing the game experience. The melee system needs reworking and attentive updates so it becomes smoother and more reactive towards the players mouse input, for example in blocking. Warband shows a very good example of how a smooth and quick melee system can work and I am sure the developers have this topic on their to-do-list. Still the very basic game mechanics are working and the game is not "unplayable" as some other reviews might suggest.
For people like me, that enjoy the Napoleonic era in general, playing as a  Napoleonic soldier and fighting in melee or with a gunpowder weapon, may it be on land or on sea, it is an enjoyable experience already. Especially as soon as the high latency issue is fixed. But keep in mind that the game is still early access and some people might get frustrated by the weird hit-box detection or the very slow and unresponsive melee game play. If you expect to be frustrated by those current issues I would suggest you wait for further updates and development before you actually buy Holdfast.
For everyone else I can recommend the game. As future updates release I will update the review.

Thief: The Dark Project is one of three game released in 1998 that gave birth to the stealth based genre and basically laid the foundation for future games to come. Unlike modern stealth games which give you the option of fighting your way through mobs, you almost always want to stay hidden and strike from the shadows. Mobs usually take quite a few hits to go down and your character Garrett, although an adequate fighter in his own right, is quite squishy and will usually go down really quick. That's not to say that the direct combat method should be avoided, it's actually quite doable, however, the clunky combat system, questionable collision detection and lack of an aiming reticle makes direct combat more trouble than it's worth.
The stealth mechanics I thought was innovative although can be quite laughable at times. Thief incorporates a cover system that allows you to conceal yourself in dark, shadowy areas. A "light gem" indicator tells you how visible you are to the mobs around you, however, a flaw with the system is that enemy vision AI is dependent on the light gem, so you can literally stand right in front of a mob and as long as your light gem is indicating that you're hidden, they won't notice you and will walk past you as if you were invisable. Sound also plays a part in stealth with AI responding to noises you make such as footsteps or the impact of a thrown item against a wall. Different floor types can affect the way your footsteps sound. Your gadgets are mostly based around stealth are actually quite creative. Water arrows lets you douse torches to darken a room, moss arrows lets you create soft patches on the ground to walk on to dampen your footsteps, etc. Level design is organic and open ended similar to Deus Ex, giving you more than one way to reach your destintion.
If you can get over the outdated graphics (and if you're a real gamer, you should) you'll find that Thief still manages to hold it's own even by today's standards. Solid gameplay, well written story and the atmospheric soundtrack all blend well to create an immersive experience. The game is lengthy enough to keep you playing for quite a while. It's challenging but not unfairly difficult and the lack of a mini map, way points or instant checkpoints shouldn't detract you. It's actually a nice throwback to a time when video games didn't hold your hand as much as it does now. Completing it is very rewarding, especially if you're patient enough to play through and immerse yourself in the whole game and sadly, patience is a trait that most gamers nowaday lack.
