Then why should you play this game?
- Landscapes: just stunning. I've been spending some minutes on every ingame bench I came across. However, for some reason these benches weren't located at the most beatiful sceneries imo.
- Music: the first time I heard the female voice I wasn't really sure if I liked it. But after spending half an hour in the game you start loving it and you'll associate it with the emotional plot in this game.
- Puzzles: this game is all about solving puzzles. The younger brother has certain abilities that the older one doesn't have and vice versa. This game would be best playable with a controller, but it wasn't necessary.
- Storyline: Something that you'll never ever forget for the rest of your life. Thinking back about it over a year after playing it still makes my eyes watery. This story is about eternal love, endurance, setbacks and hope. I have 2 brothers and could relate to lots of moments in this game.
505 Games, thank you for this masterpiece that I'll cherish forever in my mind.

Overall this is turning out to be another great Deus Ex game despite the early bugs and a less than perfect console port.

If you were looking for a good horror game, don't even consider this game. Not only are the graphics absolute trash, but the whole game seems to revolve around collecting the remaining two pages in the rooms and finding items. Finding the items is an absolute nightmare and I only managed to find the crowbar, matches and a spike pit featured in the trailer video, all in one hour. That is literally how long it takes sometimes due to poor game design and repetitive room layouts. The room layout is so repetitive you easily lose your way and have difficulty even telling where you are, it's essentially a walking, searching and escaping simulator all mashed up into one. Not to mention the AI for the Hat Man is atrocious, since all it does is "teleport" to a location directly in your field of view, namely in front of you. He goes through walls and can't be shaken off, as he'll just "teleport" directly in front of you again when you have all five pages of the journal. He looks like some image taken from google and plastered onto a model and called the oh-so-scary Hat Man.
As for the Shadow people, I never even encountered any of them. The only thing I'd seen that would even possibly be close to that was at the beginning when you click on the journal and a creature shows up to steal your soul, but I think even then that's just the Hat Man. It's a bit like Dead by Daylight, Slender: The Eight Pages and Vanish all combined to make this pathetic excuse for a game. You walk away and instantly the rooms have changed, making it impossible to find your way back. Some hints or even an explanation of what to do would be nice so I'm not aimlessly wandering around halls, running from the dreaded Hat Man, who's kill animation makes me want to throw up.
Shockingly enough, the audio and atmosphere in the game was tolerable. Audio would get extremely repetitive, but the occasional radio playing badly done music was fairly creepy. Also a falling tile or light, whatever it was, was a good trick, but the novelty wears off really quick and you grow to expect it. Same for the mysteriously moving wheelchairs, although those can get you caught if you're unlucky (Or daft).
So overall, this game isn't really something you should buy, especially at full price. If you're really that desperate to try it, wait until it goes on sale, that way you won't be as disapointed. I'm disgusted people say it's a quality game and recommend it, as a troll or not, because this is worse than Rob Zombie's '31'. And that movie was terrible. Really, if you want a quality game that still has the room changing mechanic, install Vanish on GameJolt, it's good and free.

I can't believe this went under my radar for so long. I discovered it this holiday and couldn't put it down for a full day and night. It's an easy game to pick up but not easy to master. The later levels get pretty brutal. The balance of difficulty was spot on for me.
Toy Soldiers is a unique type of tower defense game. Unlike most in the genre, there's no pre-determined path for your enemies. It's an open battlefield and you have to plan for it, filling your weak spots as you go. It also allows you to take control of any one of your units. That alone really immerses you in the game. In later levels it even gives you your own tanks and planes to pilot.
The WW1 theme is done incredibly well. The era just seeps through its pores, from music to loading screens to shouts on the battlefield. And I like watching the infantry units striking poses during battle that I'm familiar with from the actual toys. The boss fights take this up a notch. When they roll out at the end of the levels it makes you feel like you're in a period movie, oozing with melodrama and larger-than-life enemies.
If you're a fan of tower defense or the WW1 era, absolutely get this. The rest of you still have a good chance of finding something to like, as well.

- Level cap at level 40, which you can reach long before the end of the game

- No challenge unless playing on hard
7/10

I played this game back then and decided to finish it this time around because of the Steam Sales.
It's a decent game but it has a lot of flaws. If you can stomach those flaws then you'll probably like the game.
-Story and Charcters are your every cliche in a fantasy setting. Overall the story isn't interesting and the characters aren't compelling. It's hard to even care much for most of the NPCs.
-They use the same voice actors multiple times and it starts to get weird that every other character or NPC sounds about the same.
-Invisible walls! Tiny pieces of cobblestone or rocks can become impassable although you should by all rights be able to walk over it. You're basically a demigod near the end and you still can't jump over certain terrain that visually you should be able to.
-The game has a lot of tedious fetch quest and it hurts since your character runs so slowly.
-The travel time between quests. Fast travel helps but you most of the quests are in between locations and you have to run slowly looking for items or NPCs.
-Very stiff contorls. It basically means that combos can often become awkward and that you can't cancel an attack once you click on the button. It just feels so STATIC although the attack animations and combos plus different weapon tactics are somewhat entertaining the first time around.
-Crafting in the game is a chore and more of an afterthought. You'll have no reason to use it once your character is upgraded enough and you can find better items through loot drops or chests.
When it was released it had nothing new to offer the genre and it didn't age gracefully either.

IMAGINE IF GTA, DMC AND METAL HAD A SON, THIS IS IT.
THE GOOD STUFF
++Great Soundtrack.
++A big world to explore.
++Enough main missions and side quests to keep you entertained.
++Jack Black, Ozzy Osbourne, Rob Halford, Lemmy Kilmister, what more could you ask for?!.
++Sandbox+driving+metal+RTS+hack n' slash = Brütal Legend.
++The final boss battle is awesome as hell, listening to metal wihle fighting demons wasn't a thing since Doom.
++The equipment you get later on is really helpful, and it makes the game flow really well.
THE OK STUFF
+The missions before the final boss are a bit annoying, but passable.
+Even with all of the side missions and collectables there isn't that much of a reward, besides some extra songs (which are mediocre for a reward) and more weapons for your character. With that said, they aren't that hard to find so you're not spending half-an-hour looking for those goodies.
+The main campaing is really short, just 22 main missions and a final boss. It could've been a little longer.

THE WHAT-WERE-THEY-THINKING STUFF
-The driving controls are near horrible, they take a lot of time to get used to, and even then they are pretty bad.
-Some of the voice acting is lame.
-There are cutscenes that should make you feel anger/sadness, but they fail at it.
-The RTS in this game is somewhat confusing.
-The ending is not that satisfying, they could've worked better on it.
I TOTALLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME
Even with it's flaws, Brütal Legend it's one hell of a game, definitely worth playing.

ROTT is for old-school gamers. It looks, plays, and feels like old-school FPS games. Do not be fooled by the screenshots, this game does not look as amazing as it seems. It really feels like someone took the old Wolfenstein 3D engine and remade it. Movement in the game feels old-school, you kind of bolt around on a cloud of air. The weapons are over the top and fun to use. There are secret areas just like FPS of old. Each level ends with a summary screen showing you how you did. There is a health bar instead of the now norm of no health, screen gets red until you get out of combat.
If you've never experienced the joys of installing a handful of floppies and wandering claustrophobic corridors in search of secret areas filled with treasure and beating your friends high score, then you might not get this game. If you think this is a revamped series then you are wrong. I mean, it is well done and there is more outdoors less cramped corridors, but basically it's hardcore old-school and it makes no appologies for it.
I recommend this game for players who have an itch to play those old-school shooters, but can't stand the controls/graphics of the originals. The levels aren't terribly long and you can hop in for a few minutes and kill bad guys while you wait for your wife/girlfriend to finish doing whatever it is they do that takes so long and gives you an excuse to play games while they do it.

I can say that this game is one of the rare few that actually lives up to the 'old school' claim quite well, although it still has a few modernisms that may stick out like a sore thumb in contrast to the classic game.
Despite the game starting out with a very rocky start, e.g: bugs, performance issues; some which might still persist to this day, it is much more stable and optimized lately than before. It is worth giving it a try, especially since the game is still having content being made for it by the developers, new features are being added, user maps are being made, amongst other things. The AI is still on the bad side though, but it shouldn't discourage anyone much.
Fans of very fast paced action, absurd, wacky humor and gameplay and so on should find themselves enjoying this game. Pick it up whenever it is most convenient and have a blast.

This is Deux Ex: Human Revolution on steroids; if you loved the previous game you will adore this one also. The story expands on events from the previous game (although you do not have to play the previous games to play DE: MD, I would recommend it as it is fantastic!). However cash grabbing really spoils the game.
These are a bone of contention at the moment in the PC gaming community, but in my personal experience the game looks great and with excellent framerate as long as you accept you have to
You can also turn off things like sharpening to suit your personal taste. IMO the graphics are not designed to be maxed out on current hardware, like Crysis.
Same gameplay as previous, with extra augmentations, new crafting system, sidequests have greater effect upon the city of Prague and the story. You can play the Deus Ex GO app on your phone too, to get extra Praxis if you wish (although the app must be bought too). The game does not appear as dichotomous, in that you can alternate between stealth or lethal gameplay easier than in DE:HR where it was best to stick to one style only.
The city of Prague is well designed and beautiful. The soundtrack and voice acting are excellent as per the last game. The motion capture has also been much improved, so faces look more realistic.
I can't comment too much on this at the moment as I have to play more, but the story expands upon events previously, with a much darker tone.
Yes admittedly they do not affect the story bar making it easier (P2W gg ez??), you are not punished if you don't buy any, and are not even mentioned in the tutorials or story mode. However, it is still totally obnoxious to have payments in a game which already is £40/$60 and has DLC/season pass. The payments are also not exactly tiny, including buying 5 praxis kits for £3.99! Then worst of all, these are one time use! It doesn't matter if these don't affect you, because I worry this is the start of a slippery slope of microtransactions in full price games. Maybe next it will be that you have to grind for things that can be purchased...
This is just ridiculous. Hold on to your saves where you claim them, because once they're gone you cannot claim them in new games you start. Cash grabbing.
Currently there is an issue for M+KB users, where mouse acceleration cannot be turned off and it does occasionally cause you to zoom past wherever you may be aiming. I hope this gets patched but that remains to be seen.
Overall I think Eidos Montreal have done a wonderful job creating another Deus Ex game for the fans, however I think Square Enix have taken advantage of its good name and are milking it for $$$ (don't forget the quickly turned around Augment your Preorder). If you can look past that you will enjoy the game, but if you have a moral issue with single time use microtransactions in a full price single player game then only buy this on sale to show the publishers this is not acceptable.

Ok, so to finish main story took me 17h. Then I've checked Breeches and separate Jensen Story.
After all of this gameplay it's hard for me to decide what kind of note should I give: good or bad.
I'm leaning towards postive note because in general the game is very good.
I've medium hardware and yet this game run, maybe not smoothly, but very close to.
It experiences some fps drops, yes. That's normal in here but I've got used to it. Hard to say how would it run if I've had better computer.
I've read about crashes: happend to me only once during a cut scene, somewhere in 80% into the storyline.
I've read about microtransations: tbh I've really noticed them and checked them out at the end of the game, earlier I've only saw rage on the internet.
Story is good and sharp. Side quests are like 50/50 good and complex to shallow and boring ones.
Locations: vast. A lot to explore and I've really liked wandering around.
Actual gameplay: interesting. New skills for Jensen are pretty cool. The cooldown stat to worry about was quite interesting but I've set it up at the beginning and never had to worry about it again. AI seems to know sometimes a little bit too much. Trigger alarm, hide at the other side of the facility and they still know where you are :/ After some time they drop pursue but it was irritating.
Graphics: even on medium hardware beautiful. Really.
So I wrote the pros more or less, now the cons.
The biggest sin: got to the end of the game. Killed boss, checked on vips and then quest log told me to kill boss again. And now I was stuck and couldn't do anything because he was dead already :/ I've needed to load earlier save and play it differently so I could see the actual ending.
Fps drop are annoying, hard to say what's really causing them because on small booth you can get 10fps for a few seconds and at a open location with lots of lights and npc it runs smoothly.
Lights are sometimes a little bit too bright. You're getting through some corridor and suddenly you can't see♥♥♥♥♥♥and trying to scratch your eyes out.
GUI is for consoles. On PC it's clunky and annoying. Shopping is taking ages just to start or end it, completly unnecessary.
Additional Jensen story was way too short. In and out in like 10 minutes.
So we've got to the bottom and the actual note.
Yes, I recommend it.
Yes, I had fun playing it.
Yes, it has it cons but it's still a very good game.

In Kabitis you play as a little character called, very originally, Kabitis. Apparently your family has been kidnapped by a generic villain and your goal is to save them from this generic villain by platforming through poorly designed levels, annoying sounds and the most ridiculous enemies.

In Kabitis you jump around incredibly generic settings picking up generic items, that do not say what they are because the developers expect you to know by magic, killing enemies in the most generic way ever. Imagine, you take the Mario franchise; you rip out all it’s good aspects and then make it look like sonic the hedgehog. It’s that the core aspect of the game is so unenjoyable that it ruins all the remaining parts.

Most of the levels in kabitis exist of a flat plain and a few platforms, most of these levels are fine with relatively diverse opportunities for jumping and moving around; not that this is encouraged as there is almost no reward for doing any of it. As the game progresses it becomes more and more clear that het developer is probably quite lazy as certain levels are completely flat only for the last part to have 2 parts to beat the most ridiculous boss.
I can see that the time and effort put into creating these levels went downhill like a car off mount Everest, it started off great and after a while the ambition plummeted into oblivion with only scraps of the original being mashed together into what is supposed to be a “new level”
The graphical capabilities of Kabitis make me believe that it was originally created for the Nintendo DS as it does not even have mouse support; you simply move around the cursor with the arrow keys. There are many problems with the graphics, the primary one is  that everything has poorly made textures, the animations, that barley exist, are most of the times 2 frames playing after each other  and when a player sees multiple objects next to each other you never know if you can walk on it or not because depth does not exist in the painfully bright world of Kabitis.
For a 90’s Sonic game these graphics would’ve sufficed but in a world where there is so much more available it’s just plain bad developing if a developer cannot get a background higher than 240P.
Kabitis, although originally worked on with much ambition fell into a dark trap of talentless crap which is a waste of the players and the developers time. Kabitis is so flawed that the small part of good aspects are made obsolete with the other parts being so ridiculous.
It’s a wonderful failed attempt that I would not recommend even to hardcore platform fans.

What's not to like about Solarix?
If you're a fan of atmospheric horror, you want to buy this game.
If you're a fan of a solid isolation science-fiction setting, you want to buy this game.
If creepy and unnerving narration can set the mood, you want to buy this game.
If you even like knocking people unconscious and hurling their bodies around like dolls, then you still want to buy this game.
I've already banked quite a few hours playing, and I'm really pleased with how the difficultly levels change the gameplay entirely. On easy setting, there's an element of stealth, sure, but you do have the option to just run around shooting everyone, albeit carefully. As soon as you up the bar, however, you need to creep in the shadows and create distractions as well as any Adam Jensen or Altaïr. There's enough design in the world to keep you immersed in the story but not enough to distract from the game at hand.
Let's talk price. If you can convince yourself to go and drop sixty dollars for a AAA release that might disappoint you, then you can definitely pony up twenty and get a game that supports indie devs and will genuinely hold your attention, and who knows? Maybe it'll even make it into your top ten. I know it did for me.

Here is my attempt at rating/reviewing “Solarix”:
Right from the start you can tell that this game was made with the influences of such games like System Shock, Doom, and Thief. However, it manages to step out of the shadows and grant a fresh experience into a genre that has thus been lost since the early 2000’s.
Is it the best game I have played? No. It is worth the asking price? Yes. Why? Because it might not be an AAA title, it does show merit and passion that has been missing from games. Yes the game has bugs, and yes the developers “have” and “are” working on numerous patches to fix these problems. Even with the remaining technical bugs, the game is fun, enjoyable, and just down-right frightening.
Review breakdown:
+Story
+Soundtrack/Audio
+Environmental Art
+Gameplay Mechanics
-Replayabilty
-Graphics are a bit outdated compared to newer game (but to be fair it was build using UDK)
-Difficulty can ramp to being super hard at times
Overall this is a great game and everyone should support the team behind Solarix. If you’re not sold just yet, wait it out and I’m sure the devs will patch everything out.

Have you ever wondered while playing an RPG inside a weapon or armor shop, "I wonder how it would be to have this job?".
Well this game is exactly the answer to that question. More or less of course. This game has the elements of running a business. You don't necessarily have to sell armor and weapons. You can be versatile in your store such as, health/mana potions, arrows, different types of seeds to grow, and the helper bot. There is currently one game mode you can play with and that's called "My Shoppe". Here you basically set up your shop the way you see fit and earn money. Starting the game off is a little slow though as you only have little income and can order potions to start. You can buy some pedestals and sell your potions that way. Eventually you'll earn enough money to buy and sell things at a higher price.  Selling items are easy. Keeping track of what's missing, and when to order them is another thing. Currently in the game you can talk to the customer and see what they are interested in buying so if you have it stock put it out for sale!  Also having to keep track of what items are priced at a level a customer will want to purchase it at is a challenge in itself.  What keeps you on your toes is having thieves who decide, "This is way too expensive for my taste," and then end up stealing your items. Sometimes they get away. If you're quick enough you can ZAP! them with your magic or slay them with your trusty short sword. (ZAP! is my personal favorite). Don't forget about the Barbarians either! As your shop does well you will experiance random waves of Barbarians. Sometimes you get only one. Sometimes you get six. It's up to you to defend your shop. If you're interested in giving yourself a challenge or a "quest" then you can do so! Quests such as "Sell X amount of these certain shields" and earn yourself 1,000 Gold. Let's not forget the Skyrim references in this game!
Pros:
-First Person
-Clean Player Movements
-FPS is Stable
-I have 7.7 hours on it and it hasn't crashed once
-The UI is easy to read
-Game handles well to various types of resolutions to fit your monitors needs
-Various choices of "furniture" for your store (Weapon/armor rack, hat rack)
Cons:
-Save game bug (The worst con of them all)
*AI pathing is sketchy (Which you can now "reset" their paths by pressing "J") *
-Sometimes the combat is meh (meaning you look to slay a thief and kill him and an innocent)
-There's no real tutorial (It's just a menu explaining things)
So in all these pros weigh out the cons. I believe this game to be fun at it's state and obviously it being an early access game there is much to be added and fixed! They even have a roadmap set up to see what features will come when. Having that save game bug is a downer though. Especially if you binge play one day, and it reverts all your money and most of your object placement progress, but it's alpha and it's a good way to learn the ropes. I reccomend this game in it's current state, and the greatest thing is it's only $4.99! There are plenty of games out there that charge $20 and have an hour of game elements.

IMAGINE IF GTA, DMC AND METAL HAD A SON, THIS IS IT.
THE GOOD STUFF
++Great Soundtrack.
++A big world to explore.
++Enough main missions and side quests to keep you entertained.
++Jack Black, Ozzy Osbourne, Rob Halford, Lemmy Kilmister, what more could you ask for?!.

++The final boss battle is awesome as hell, listening to metal wihle fighting demons wasn't a thing since Doom.
++The equipment you get later on is really helpful, and it makes the game flow really well.
THE OK STUFF
+The missions before the final boss are a bit annoying, but passable.
+Even with all of the side missions and collectables there isn't that much of a reward, besides some extra songs (which are mediocre for a reward) and more weapons for your character. With that said, they aren't that hard to find so you're not spending half-an-hour looking for those goodies.
+The main campaing is really short, just 22 main missions and a final boss. It could've been a little longer.

THE WHAT-WERE-THEY-THINKING STUFF
-The driving controls are near horrible, they take a lot of time to get used to, and even then they are pretty bad.
-Some of the voice acting is lame.
-There are cutscenes that should make you feel anger/sadness, but they fail at it.
-The RTS in this game is somewhat confusing.
-The ending is not that satisfying, they could've worked better on it.
I TOTALLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME

Heres an arugment for the three things I just mentioned.
Balance: If you listen to the pro scene and their tier list you can divide it in two groups. Characters that can exploint and characters that cannot. Eventually it becomes a combo fest where one player attacks and the other player waits. If you get smashed into a wall it's pretty much game over. It takes the fun away from the whole game. If you're good at memorizing button sequences this game is for you. If you're looking for a balanced fighter, its better to look somewhere else.
Design. Endless juggling, getting stuck against the wall, rage art, small levels, aweful loading etc.

-Remove rage art or make it optional. Hitting two buttons to get 50% of a Healthbar with armor is not fun nor competitive.
-Increase HP by 20%. Matches are over too fast. It takes 1 or two combos to finish a match, it's not fun nor competitive.
-Add a rematch function without having to load the same settings again and again and again.
-Increase combo difficulty so that juggles get dropped more.
Optimization: For a fighting game, the gameflow is full and utter♥♥♥♥♥♥and the loading time are a disaster. I know most of you folks don't mind waiting a bit. But once you've played it for a long time you'll notice how much waiting in accumulation you have done.
In short, game is too hard and long time players can exploit combos, juggles and walls to ruin the whole competitive experience. Not Fun!

First off I would like to thank the developers for creating this wonderful little game.
Three amazing things about this game:
1. I thought the story to this game was beautiful. There is no dialogue, but yet you know everything that the characters doing and saying to each other. The characters are wonderful and there are a variety of different characters to meet. The story has a few twists which were unexpected. The basis is that you play as two brothers who go on a jouney to get their father medicine. This game is short as I completed the story in about 3 hours and spent 1 more 100% achievements. I also really connected with the characters and felt as though I was going with them on this journey.
2. I am someone who has played (and still plays) very old games so I have never cared about graphics really, only that the game plays well. Therefore the graphics have to be pretty astounding to impress me. This game's look impressed me. It has a cartoony style, but it looks amazing and the variety of environments are all beautiful.
3. In this game you use both brothers simultaneously. Control one brother with WASD and the other with arrow keys. This creates interesting gameplay as you need to use both brothers to complete puzzles. There are a lot of puzzles in the game and though sometimes I thought "how do I do this?" I never really got stuck. Therefore it was challenging but kept the game flowing. The are also a few sidequests which add a lot to the game even though they are short. There is a lot in 'Brothers' for such a short game.
I must add that it was an absolute pleasure to spend time unlocking these achievements. Even though I have 100% this game I will be replaying it because I loved it.
Overall beautiful graphics and astounding environments, extremely engaging story and characters and exceedingly good gameplay. This game is a pleasure to play.

An incredibly addicitive and thoroughly enjoyable instalment to the loot horde genre. Made by the guys that brought us Diablo I + II (evidence of their legacy is intertwined throughout the game, from the HUD to skill-trees), Torchlight 2 is seen by many as the spiritual sequal to the Diablo series, despite its title.
The good:
The price. Even when initially released, which is when I bought the game, it was less than €20. The game has been on sale for less than €5 many times since then, there was even a weekend earlier this year when the game was available for free. At this price there's no reason any fan of the genre could have for missing out on this title. And like I said, for those who just want to test the water, the game is often available for a price that will all be assure that buyers remorse will not be a factor.
The mods. With the Steam Workshop the downloading and installing of mods is made simple. Furthermore, the array of mods is so vast, that the varation of gameplay and levels means you can tweak the game to suit your particular style, or difficulty preference. New character classes, levels and more basically ensure entirly new games, with the Torchlight feel, are available for free at the click of a button. The modding community have also inserted some completely necessary tweaks to the game, that in my opinion should have been available from the start: such as fre entrance resurrection (everyone left a portal at the entrance anyway) and a shared-stash big enough to suit your needs (no longer have the need for countless mule characters to store situational equipment).
Loot mechanics. Unlike previous Diablo games (unsure of Diablo III's mechanics as I've never played it) or indeed Borderlands games, you no longer have to worry about people looting all the good equipment because they have slightly superior latency. Each character has a seperate pool of items that drop per mob, meaning everyone gets their fair share of loot. I've found that this had additional benefit as those I played with were usually more willing to trade items, or indeed give items to the relevant class for free - thus increasing your likelihood of getting the piece of equipment you've been hunting in multiplayer games, not decreasing it like in old-school Diablo titles.
Gameplay:
I've sank 300 hours into this game. And although I haven't played this game in a couple of months I do plan to sink a lot more time into it. What more needs to be said? This game is addictive, the combat is well balanced, (difficult at times, but with concentration and the right skill + equipment setup every situation or fight can be done with the boss hitting the floor before you do.) and the replay factor, even without the mods, is huge.
The bad:
The story. Typical evil force rewoken, hero needed to send it back to wenst it came. Copy & Paste job from boring plots 101.
The huge selection of mods mean that a pick-up multiplayer with a random selection of people is impossible. Unless you and some on your friendlist agree on a particular set of mods, prepare to go solo.
Conclusion:
Can't recommend this game enough, one of the greats in my book. Although multiplayer is where it truly shines and unfortunately the modding has worked against random multiplayer games. So I'd suggest you maybe get the 4-pack when on sale on steam (will be less than what I paid for 1 copy of the game & that was more than worth the price) and get some friends to blast through it with you. The story might suck, but you'll be having so much fun you won't care, & if you do, just play Gone Home or something instead.

After finishing the game:
In HR the world building was nearly all connected to the main quest, so everybody got to see most of the game.
In MD, the world building is via exploration and side quests, if you do only the main quest or the side quests which pop up as part of the main quest you lose half the game. Also the world building is mainly fleshing out details, with little new information about the big background events.
Even though it took me nearly 50 hours to go through the game and I can't complain about play length, the MAIN quest story is too short and of too little consequence in MD. It's not DLC length but not far from it either. Nothing really important happens, you clear up a single terror attack and stop another and that's it.
In HR you get introduced to augmentation, the issues surrounding it, the Illuminati and how they want to control their world via Picus, Corps and merc squads. Then you stop the grand master plan in a do or die situation.
IMO MD is not a train wreck, but not great either. It's interesting enough if you want to learn more about the Deus Ex universe, but probably less so if you are mainly interested in taking down quest points. In design terms it probably would have been better to have a longer and more involved main story line, while introducing the many POI and some side quests in DLC's. This would have made Prague feel a bit empty on initial release but IMO would have still been the better choice.
MD still gets a thumbs up from me because of the many game play improvements and the world building in general, BUT the next Deus Ex game has to go back to HR style when it comes to main quest design.

Core Game
----------
If you loved previous Deus Ex games you are going to love this one.
It builds upon DE:HR and adds some of the feel of the original Deus Ex in terms of exploration and discovering interesting side stories and secrets. The core gameplay is more fluent and tighter in every single way with fun new Augs to play with.
As it stands there are a lot of negative reviews on steam but I do advise to take them with a pinch of salt and make up your own mind whether or not this game is for you. Like I said the core game experience is very much on point.
Performance
------------
For me the game is running like a dream and I have had 0 performance issues.
It is getting harder to support all pc system configurations these days so in case you are having issues I'm sure the devs will do their best to fix it with the data you provide them.
The controls feel tight and responsive but can take some getting used to in the first 10 minutes or so. Everything can be customized to your liking and it is advised to tweak the mouse sensitivity to something that works for you as the default setting is way to sensitive for most players.
MICROTRANSACTIONS AND DLC
--------------------------
As for the microtransaction and DLC "issue". To be honest I only noticed there were microtransactions after everybody started complaining about it. If you don't like it, don't use it.
It has absolutely no impact on the core game. Developers track data on how much those things get bought. If people stop using those features then developers will stop adding them. But as long as people do buy them ... .
I notice a lot of people not recommending the game because of this even though they are loving the core experience. Personally I would love to see more Deus Ex in the future and if you would like to as well I suggest you ignore the Microtransactions and DLC for now and just let it be heared to SE instead of writing of the game based on some secondary OPTIONAL features.
One thing I do hope they patch though is the fact that Pre-purchase, DLC and Deus Ex Go unlocks are limited to a single save. That stuff is just plain stupid but should be easily fixable. So I do hope that they consider adjusting this.
MOBILE APP
-----------
Deus Ex: MD supports a mobile companion app on both Android and IOS. It allows you to read mails, Ebooks, track player stats and read up on the Deus Ex Universe on your mobile device. Throughout the game you can also find hidden collectables that can be scanned using the app to unlock behind the scenes interviews and insights about the making of the game.
This is a nice touch, works well and is a fun out of game interaction. It does however require you to have a Square Enix account so if you're not into that than this could frustrate you as there is no ingame way to access the making of content. In my case I allready account so this was more of a pleasant little addition to the game. Again this is fully optional and you are in no way required or forced to create an account if you don't want to.
OVERALL
--------
Great game, good fun and a worthy follow up to Deus Ex: Human Revolution. Worth the purchase, just ignore the Microtransactions and DLC untill they are no longer single save only if you want to purchase DLC to begin with.

I'll start here: this is an awesome game, despite some issues it might have, it is totally worth the full price today.
Go buy it and have an awesome time playing it!
Some people are reporting crashes but the dev team so far has been fixing things quite quickly so I'd expect those to be over soon. I didn't experience any crashes myself.
There are some other glaring issues with it which I'll give my 2 cents on further down.
Why is it such a good game? one word - gameplay. Stealth is challenging and fun, and the level designs are absolutely brilliant.
Every coroner of the game is just oozing with detail, whether it's a puzzle like hidden places to find your way in, reading material to reveal more lore and getting more background, and you can even find secret side quests in some places.
I've played more than 70 hours so far, and this is just 1 playthrough, probably covered about 80% of the world (well, city). Art and sound design is just amazing, and an integral part of the game's experience. It sets well the atmosphere and grows darker as the game progresses.
The game is very flexible, you can play it in many styles - exploration, stealth, combat (rambo style / ninja style) and you can (and probably should) adjust your gameplay to each mission.
About the story.
It does fall short from HR, yes. HR had a brilliant and engaging main story. In MD the main story is smaller. It seems the intended focus was more into doing a lot of side missions that each reveal different aspects of the world.
MD gives you this rich impressive feeling that you are part of the world, yet not so much of an "adventure like" game (dystopian adventure..) like HR, where you have a lot of emotional climaxes and plot shifts.
You don't have for example scenes like when you stay to save Malik in HR when you crash on a roof in hengsha, or when you hear that Megan isn't actually dead, or the ending itself, the aug incident was huge in HR.
The main mission in MD is overall ok, not amazing, but holds it together. You get a feeling of disappointment in the end because the game works so much on absorbing you into the world and into dealing with so many details it throws at you that when it does end it feels abrupt and premature, and leaves you a bit dissatisfied.
BTW, midway through the ending credits there's another cut seen that's totally worth it. Basically what the main story should have been in this game.
Now I do have to say a few words about what everyone's saying:
1. microtransactions. Personally I think it was blown out of any reasonable proportions .. You absolutely don't need to buy anything to play the game. I'm guessing it's just there for people with money who can't be bothered getting used to the game's difficulty.
2. The weapon pack DLCs are for one playthrough use only, very strange decision but meh...
3. Yes, graphics are heavy and sometimes buggy. This is the worse of the 3 and I don't have a good one to answer that.
I started with running the game on an i5-6400/GTX 960/8GB RAM and for a while there even tried to drop from 1080p to 900 to get a solid 60fps... Currently running the game at medium settings on 1080p at ~45fps it's not too bad (given my rig is not amazing) and hopefully they will optimize (the game looks amazing even in medium settings).
Upgrading my RAM to 16G helped a lot of stuttering and loading times, I wouldn't recommend it with only 8GB (unless maybe you've got an SSD)
Overall I think Mankind Divided delivers big in gameplay and immersion, falls a bit short in the story, and yet succeeds very well in creating the next stage, a kind of transition stage within the Deus Ex world.
I'm off to play some Rambo Jensen style now ;)
Hope this helps!

TL;DR This game basically has all of the charm of Magic Circle. ..Not the...not the GAME Magic Circle, the eventual end product that happens at the end of Magic Circle designed to parody terrible hack products designed to make a cheap buck off steam.
To be more specific, the control scheme is overelaborate and is based on switching between six different options each with their own submenus on the fly, the game's idea of a 'tutorial' is basically a stripped down helpfile, You can helpfully hit spacebar for a joke about being unable to jump that is funny precisely once, instead of making spacebar do something useful. What with it being a convenient button to press for a variety of functions. But no, let's make an endless joke about how you have an arrow in the knee and cannot jump. I assume from that that this thing has been in Early Accesss since Skyrim was trendy.
The gameplay drops you right in without any real guidnace, but I was able to faff about and eventually figure out NOT to buy any furniture except for two pedestals, upon which I placed one mana potion and one health potion. I jacked up the prices to 2 gold, only to have a customer flip me off for being expensive. I then figured out the problem.
2 gold (203%) was too expensive, but it turns out 2 gold (159%) was a perfectly acceptable price. I may have those percentages wrong, but the principle is still sound, customers can tell precisely what percentile you've raised the prices even if the actual gold cost remains the same.
So I kept going, as a stream of customers proceeded to gaggle into my store, stare at my two pedestals, frantically beg for flowers and vegetables, laugh at my prices, and then leave.
Wait, no, they didn't leave. They stood there for ingame hours, continually angry about my lack of flowers and vegetables. At least the satisfied customers OH RIGHT THEY STAYED TOO. Eventually I would murder some from time to time just to clear it up, as only 20% of my customers would leave at any given time.
So eventually I managed by the end of the first day to get to the point where I could cycle through pairs of gloves, and as I watched the outside world near closing time, the doors closed..trapping me inside. Not my shop, I was trapped inside the doors, and could not move, helpless to watch as I could not pay my tax bill, which...didn't seem to cause any sort of problem whatsoever. Perhaps the inspector was kind enough to realize I was trapped inside a wooden prison, able to see out but forever immobilized.
So yeah this game's <3<3<3<3ing awful.

Just got SOLARIX over the weekend and its influence from both SYSTEM SHOCK and THIEF is definitely there in a very strong respectful manner. Within the first five minutes the much different look and atmosphere of the environment reminded me of the first SYSTEM SHOCK game where everything felt new and alien with the pleasure of me learning the world as if on my first day in school or at a job.
The sound effects and ambience is a work of pure otherworldly intensity combined with the placement of the game world's inhabitants in the right spots it really can get dramatic along with heart pumping startling. I love the voice acting which gives off a sense of me wanting to trust these disembodied voices in this hostile environment yet something tells me to hold back and see how things play out. Audio logs are also very well done with a serious side to them in the same manner as the ones in the first SYSTEM SHOCK game where i feel like am in a environment of scientists and workers who treat their jobs with very strict disciplined standards.
Stealth is full of high tension reminding me of the fear i had playing the first two THIEF games as i try not to be seen or caught. Using ones environment to stay quiet and invisible is paramount to survival and or taking out enemies unnoticed. One more reason i feel like trusting the artificial intelligence voice AMI which runs the complex or the anarchist sounding female who pipes in with crazy talk or maybe not. Time will tell. The isolation felt in such a game world definitely has me reaching out for any possible allies. That male voice though from the preview trailers i have seen seems way to sinister to trust and thus far ingame i have yet to change my mind. Now that i think of it he reminds me a tad of H.A.L. from 2001 A SPACE ODYSSEY.
SOLARIX definitely disconnects me from reality with all its atmosphere. The scaling of the environment is excellent sometimes giving me a feeling of being on the set of the first ALIEN movie with a sense of grandness. I also love the fact that i dont have to go total stealth by using properly timed head shots on enemies who can kill me in an instant if am not extremely cautious.
Graphics have a certain cold retro hardcore style with its mixture of blinking lights and strangely comforting computer monitor screens amidst a worn industrial facade as if neglected from centuries of wear and tear.
Thus far am having a frightfully fun time with SOLARIX. One of the reasons it feels so much like SYSTEM SHOCK is it has me constantly learning and adapting ratching up the tension and keeping me on the edge of my comfort zone.
SOLARIX definitely feels like "old school" pushed to the max of excellence. For someone who appreciates the gameplay and art direction of the first QUAKE, SYSTEM SHOCK, TERMINATOR FUTURE SHOCK, THIEF, ARX FATALIS this is a masterpiece of artistic intensity.
SOLARIX a dark malevolent future where the truth unfolds as a forboding mystery novel upon the id of your mind's eye. Buy it.. play it and pray its only a.. game.

Given the amount of time I played Street Fighter IV, MVC3 and Mortal Kombat (2011), this sequel meets the hype set by the 2.5D fighting games of the preceding generation. It doesn't reinvent the wheel like its predecessors, but it does raise a bar for the new generation. I love it! Just wish I wasn't so lacking in patience and focus right now, getting older in years and its hard for me to dedicate myself to a hardcore, in-depth fighting game that's more than just fan service. And that's what MKX is.
Just wished they had fleshed out the story a bit more (and that the tie-in comic didn't muck up some continuity) for a longer campaign; and focused on allowing us to play those characters which are clearly playable & UNIQUE, but locked as NPCs: Rain, Sindel, Kabal, Nightwolf, Enimra (Smoke), and maybe Stryker (his style/moveset seems to be incorporated into Sonya, Cassie and maybe Jackie). Didn't think too much of the Fujin, Li Mei, Sareena and Bo Rai Cho cameos either.
Anyway, off the top of my head:
PROS:
* The different styles for the characters (3 p/character) make the roster feel nearly thrice as large. Quality over quantity!
* EXCELLENT Krypt adventure: the best one yet and leagues ahead of the horrific Krypt in MK9. They could flesh this out into a full-fledged old-school dungeon crawler if they wanted.
* X-rays are more visceral than ever, as well as Fatalities being at their prettiest and nastiest, and despite the drop from 60fps to 30fps depending on your setup, they animate seemlessly from kombat. Brutalities are the best example from this: sometimes you'll finish a fight and all of a sudden there's gore flying everywhere straight from a special move or kombo.
* Additional small tweaks to the kombat make this game simultaneously deeper and faster than previous installments, and even more/less juggly (depending on the character selected);
-- tech throws (throw escapes) give more disparate frame advantages for the faster player
-- there are cancellable throws (you can burn a bar in the super meter to cancel your throw to set up combos)
-- air kombos are faster and more fluid (this is a deceptively simple statement: watch one of Ermac's styles and you'll see how air kombat has evolved a bit)
-- you can run like in MK3, and this allows for some really hard kombos (Cassie makes good use of running,for example)
-- you can't dash backward infinitely; your back dashing is also tied to an "stamina bar" that running makes use of. So no more playing keepaway.
* Tournament ladders are a lot of fun, more focused and manageable than Injustice's equivalent and MK9's 300-event challenge tower. Whenever I log on, a lot of the time I just do that.
* Every activity you do, except maybe the Krypt, contributes to the Faction War.
* KOTH mode in online kombat performs actually better than MK9's, which is good considering how laggy the former's was. It is still laggy, mind you.
CONS:
* Online kombat is still a pain in the butt to make happen, on any platform. Connecting to a player is like magic or requires a Ph.D in patience.
* Many players experience graphical and performance problems for the PC port (not me, however, I got lucky).
* The campaign was about 3-4 chapters too short, IMO, which is important considering how many new characters there, are, what actually happens, and how many different segmented subplots have to come together. Basically feels like it was rushing toward the end.
There really isn't much for me to complain about, actually.

It's a really great game, there's a lot about it that I like.
However the cons largely outweigh the pros.
Regardless of what people are writing and reviewing about the game being fixed and what not - it really isn't.
There's still a lot of lag in multiplayer. I can play the single player game mode just fine with no lag or FPS issues, but in multiplayer the lag is horrendous. I've played against friends with relatively similar ping (about 30-50ms) to me and they were suffering from the same lag as well. It's nearly December now and this is still happening. It's upsetting, but maybe it'll be fixed in the future, but for right now I have my doubts. By the way it's not FPS lag either because we all capped close to 60 fps or more.
Other than the horrendous multiplayer latency issues the game itself is great. Lots of gore, lots of fun. Having to buy so much DLC is kind of homosexual though, but great game nevertheless. The story mode is shorter than I may have wanted, but the story is pretty lame to begin with.
If I had to rate the game for content I'd give it a 7/10

I never played the original Rise Of The Triad, but I like old school FPSes, so I've been looking forward to this remake for a while. I'm happy to say that ROTT doesn't disappoint.
The combat is fast paced and the weapons feel enjoyable to use. There are no "press a button to stick yourself to a wall" cover mechanics, although obviously you can still use walls for cover in a more natural way.  Enemy AI is pretty dumb but there are lots of them so if you're careless they can punish you. And when you take damage, there's none of the regenerating health nonsense. You need to find health packs, which come in the shape of food. And if you shoot the food with a rocket before you collect it, you can "cook" it so it heals a larger amount, which is a nice touch.

One area where I felt ROTT's combat was lacking is tactical depth. There isn't much variety in either weapons or enemy types so there's almost no requirement to figure out "this weapon works best against this enemy". Robots can only be damaged by rockets, but the rocket launcher pickups are so frequent that you'll probably just use them against every enemy anyway.
Level design is fantastic, like a puzzle box where you have to find switches and coloured keys to unlock doors. The environment is often as dangerous as the enemies, as you squeeze between spinning blades or make precise jumps across narrow platforms over instant death spike pits. There are secrets to find and you can rocket-jump to reach high ledges.

You can choose between five playable characters who each have different stats for movement speed and damage tolerance. I chose the British guy because that is my nationality and his 2 star speed / 4 star endurance seemed like a good pick for my playing style. There is no skill progression during the game.
The story is as basic as you'd expect from a 90's FPS. Terrorists (who don't actually look even vaguely Chinese) are planning to do bad stuff, kill them. The heavy rock music adds to the intensity of the combat. I had some occasional issues with framerate stuttering, but after checking the forum for advice I disabled motion blur, and afterwards it seemed more stable.
Overall ROTT is a pretty good choice if you're in a "turn off your brain and enjoy the action" mood, especially if you're a fan of the old school. The singleplayer campaign is a little short, I got an achievement for finishing in under 4 hours, but my actual playing time was 8 hours (I guess it didn't count time lost to deaths). Either way, I'd suggest picking this up on a sale.

The game is probably rated mostly positive because of the quality and fun it brings.
But once you play the game more  you notice that it lacks balance, design and optimization.
Heres an arugment for the three things I just mentioned.
Balance: If you listen to the pro scene and their tier list you can divide it in two groups. Characters that can exploint and characters that cannot. Eventually it becomes a combo fest where one player attacks and the other player waits. If you get smashed into a wall it's pretty much game over. It takes the fun away from the whole game. If you're good at memorizing button sequences this game is for you. If you're looking for a balanced fighter, its better to look somewhere else.
Design. Endless juggling, getting stuck against the wall, rage art, small levels, aweful loading etc.
Here are a few things that need to change imo to make this game accesible for everyone for a long period of time.
-Remove rage art or make it optional. Hitting two buttons to get 50% of a Healthbar with armor is not fun nor competitive.
-Increase HP by 20%. Matches are over too fast. It takes 1 or two combos to finish a match, it's not fun nor competitive.
-Add a rematch function without having to load the same settings again and again and again.
-Increase combo difficulty so that juggles get dropped more.
Optimization: For a fighting game, the gameflow is full and utter♥♥♥♥♥♥and the loading time are a disaster. I know most of you folks don't mind waiting a bit. But once you've played it for a long time you'll notice how much waiting in accumulation you have done.
In short, game is too hard and long time players can exploit combos, juggles and walls to ruin the whole competitive experience. Not Fun!
Worth the money.

Kabitis is a 2D platformer game that takes on the old-fashion design, similar to the classic Mario games. You have the main character who can collects coins (or gems in this case), hop on enemies to kill them and everything else in between. Except, that the new twist is that the gems you find can be used to purchase items that aid in your transverse. These functions include; purchasing a platform that can be placed in the map, and bee that helps collect gems. You can even buy/sell time, too! This is my first time playing a game that uses this system, so it definitely deserves credit for the originality.
I have not tried the multiplayer mode yet, but can see the game being entertaining with another player.
The controls are all right, and the art definitely gave me a nostalgia trip. Bright tiles, and background, with enemies that have a patterned and predictable movement as well as the flashing of our character when losing a life. The music was jazzy and fun. When played in a loop however, it can become irritating over time.
Some downsides to the game would be the lack of any checkpoint. This can be upsetting to some players who have progressed really far into the game. Another is the lack of pause when opening the store menu. The timer still runs, regardless. There isn’t any option to mute or adjust the volume, graphics or controls either so we’re very limited in terms of game settings.
In other words, yes there were flaws, but my experience was all right. Kabitis was developed nicely to establish ancient styled platformers. This can also be frowned on though, by its lack of proficiency in the genre in our time. Hence, the negative reviews. Overall, my experience exactly grand, but it was worth trying out. See for yourself!

This is such an odd little game to review, that I'm not quite sure how to proceed. I'm not familiar with any of the other games by this developer, so I'm coming into Kabitis with no expectations.
Kabitis has you trying to rescue your friends, who are being kept in a cage. Of course, you'll need to reach the end of each level before the timer runs out, and when you finally reach them after traversing several levels within each stage,
. Along the way, you'll be able to activate random powerup blocks that might deliver something positive (such as additional time) or negative (such as removing time). I particularly enjoyed the little bee that flew along with me, killing my enemies - until it turned on me! O_O  You'll also collect different colored gems to use in an in-game "store," although it's difficult to tell what you're buying.
I'm 50 years old, so this game hits some unexpected nostalgia buttons for me. It's very similar in style and tone to those old classic Sega Master System games such as the
series of games. The palette is bright and colorful, and the music is charming.
That said, that's about all I can say. The controls, while not exactly sluggish, aren't as tight as they could be. That charming music becomes grating after a while, as every level within each individual stage uses its own same, short theme. The translation to English is poorly done and, at times, nonsensical (although this might hit some
too!).
There's wonkiness; some expected, and some not: Pressing escape takes you into a window (instead of the expected menu); nothing will bring you back to fullscreen, including alt+enter. Although gamepads seem to function just fine, there seems to be no way to remap controls, nor is there a sound control. Entering into your "powerup store" will not stop the timer, nor will it freeze the on-screen action, which is just poor design. Standing in a hitbox spot (such as flames) will only damage you once, and then won't hurt you again for as long as you're standing there. Finally, and perhaps most important: There doesn't seem to be anyway to save a game, and dying near the end of a level brings you back to the start again (so: no checkpoints). This might be true to the era, but that doesn't mean it was ever a good thing to begin with; at least most early console games offered a continue code.
So, why the positive rating? Simply because Steam doesn't offer a "Meh" rating option. I can't say I hate it, but I can't say it's
exactly, either. I did feel the motivation to keep trying to get to each new board at least, and that's something. As long as you know what you're getting, it's worth the 99 cents.

I usually don't write reviews of games but here it is. Right, first lets get this out of the way... this game cannot compare to system shock, deus ex etc. I really like cyberpunk, horror and stealth games so I decided to give it a go and I wasn't left disappointed. You need to overlook a few things in this game maybe even a lot such as getting stuck a lot,  enemies become alert for litearlly no reason sometimes, it's extremely hard to knockout someone because you have to be standing up to do it and do it from behind (as with pretty much every other stealth game) however if you stand up and take even a single step the enemy will become alert, turn around and kick your butt. Also it doesn't really give that much information about what to do and where to go (I personally prefer it this way, I feel like games nowadays make it too easy for the player) which maybe a problem for some of the more impatient gamers. As other people have said, you WILL crouch throgh most of this game.
Well those are the bad things about this game (ones I can remember at the moment). So why give it a positive review you may ask? I don't know whether it was intended but I found the game more creepy than scary although it was a bit scary on maybe 2-3 occasions, that being said I really enjoyed the creepiness. I really enjoyed the story it kept me playing the game and wanting to get to the end, to understand what is going on, see what's caused it, how it ends etc. As I mentioned before I love stealth games and although the stealth may have been quite broken every once in a while, getting through the game without using your weapons or using them very rearely was fun and quite challenging at times.
Overall I think the game is worth a playthrough, it's not "amazing" or "mind-blowingly good" but it will keep you entertained for the few hours that you play it and if you get bored or angry at some of its faults, the story will keep you going.

You know how Diablo 1 was roguelike-inspired, and really closed in tight, so that enemy herding and controlling the pace of encounters was really important?  And then how Diablo 2 went to these more expansive environments with wider corridors, so that DPS and HP and other numbers started becoming more important than roguelike stuff?  And then how Diablo 3 was basically an MMO?  And how it's all about making you feel awesome with avatar strength and higher numbers, but how it's really goddamn tedious, too?
Well, Torchlight 2 is like if Blizzard didn't forget what fun was, but just went balls out making a really smooth and streamlined Diablo 3 instead of the mess they released.  It's not roguelike-inspired, it's a "make you feel awesome for like zero effort" type game.  But of that genre of game, it's pretty well put together and has mechanics in place designed to take literally all the tedium and unpleasantness out of the experience.  What you're left with is a completely mindless clickfest that exposes this simple truth:  that some adversity in games, the right kind of adversity where you learn and overcome things, is necessary for a lasting fun experience. This game was such a wonderful surprise. This nostalgic awesomeness of a game is a remake of the 1994 insane FPS. With most remakes, I've become accustomed to the resulting game being completely different and usually terrible. The number of times I've fired up a remake with the hope of revisiting the childhood glory days of DOS only to have the game die and empty its bowels of cover systems, microtransactions, mumblecore dialogue and tactical-ness into my tear filled eyes has added up to a point where I now rarely try out a remake. This is one of the exceptions.
Firing up the game, you are greated to metal versions of music from the original game, and doing a little research, it is in fact the great Lee Jackson, of Grabbag fame. We're off to a good start. Be warned and be patient when you fire up the game. If you haven't played an FPS from pre- Half-Life 2 in a while, you will have a learning curve. Don't look for cover behind chest high walls, don't run straight at enemies, watch your health, and enjoy that movement speed. Are there secrets? Yup, a lot of them, some are in the same place as in the original game. And they are fantastic; the best toys to gib enemies are hidden well.
Speaking of gibs, there are lots. How much? It makes most blood spurting anime blush, and that makes me happy. Want to create a variety of gibs? Cool, well you have the insane arsenal from the original, tweaked a bit. Want to fire a mini-nuke? Enjoy the firebomb. How about shooting a wall of fire across the ground? Give the Flamewall a try. Want to rocket jump? Pick up a rocket launcher, I like rocket jumping with the split missile, it seems to work a little better. Rocket jumping is limited here, but it comes in handy to get to a few secrets, still fun though. The weaponry continues with The Dark Staff, Excalibat, God Mode, Dog mode(it's exactly what you'd think).
The one downside I can find in this game is the minimal transfer of multiplayer awesomeness from the original, but I suspect the community will mod a lot of those features in SOON. Everything else is exactly how it should be. If you're looking for a plot driven, quick-time circle jerk with a cover system, look elsewhere. If you're looking for a hilarious, challenging, wonderfully self aware ode to the old school FPS, then by Joe.... this is a must have.
Everyone who has a soul should buy this game, and cry tears of joy for Wolfenstein 3d returned.
Only get this if you have a beastly machine or don't mind 10 - 30 FPS on average even while not on high settings. Otherwise, very fun game. Too many jump puzzles though.

It might be the MMO world which de-emphasizes any build-up to an interest in the story, or it might be that most of the NPCs have a large list of pointless conversation pieces telling me the exact same thing that another NPC just told me (none of which matter or are interesting). It might also be because when they introduce an NPC with some amount of potential, like Agarth, he just sends me on an errand and sits back. I do know that some degree of the not-fun has to do with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Skyrim-esque skills, which are neither fun nor intuitive - I'd rather not put points in lockpick because I'd rather never have to do it. Also, how do you farm an herb and get zero materials? Am I eating the plants as I'm farming them? Am I farming them with a flamethrower and rendering them unusable? Talk about unsatisfying.
Either way, the game emphasized all the negative aspects of an MMO - grinding and pointless fighting, uninspired dungeon design (because, again, it is endless hack and slash, not anything inventive), a story that felt both non-urgent and uninteresting, and a host of mini-game mechanics, like a dumbed down lockpicking mechanic, that make the game more laborious than fun.
If you wanna play an MMO, just choose one of the free ones with an interesting story or mechanics (at least in an MMO I have abilities to spice up combat). There just isn't much reason to play this compared to what else is out there.

Not a horrible game but not as good as it could be. I understand it's in Early Access but the gameplay is pretty shallow and repetitive: go to area, hack n slash Grimm, go to next area, hack n slash more, go to final area, hack n slash while guarding a thingy. It feels like they could add a bit more to the gameplay and playable levels (which I'm hoping and sure they will). Visually the game looks incredible. Cel-shaded (I think) like the anime, and the characters look like their anime counterparts nigh exactly (aside from the now constant jabs at Yang having 2 arms), and the world looks pretty incredible, though no secret areas (yet...).
I know it's in early dev still but these are some things I personally would like to see added eventually:
-Giant/titan bosses (Something where you'll need teamwork and different strategies/team attacks to take down the boss)
-Team/teammate specials (Ability to use special attacks with your teammates like Ruby and Weiss's Freezer Burn or Blake and Yang's Yo-Yo attack)
-Better levels/level end goal (Currently it's just hack n slash and protect a thing for 4 waves but it'd be nice to have something more dynamic or interesting instead of the same thing over and over again)
-Deeper story/plot (Currently it seems that some company that went under in the past is messing with some communications equipment and since they just through you into the first level right now, you don't really get any backstory on anything and the "story" seems pretty shallow right now. Even an option to play through the anime storyline would be nice)
-Beacon Hub area (This is an online multiplayer game [with offline currently in beta] so instead of just being thrown into the first mission, they should add Beacon as a hub area where you can find a party, go on missions, maybe participate in events, etc.)
-Full party in offline/ability to change characters mid-level (I know offline beta just came out but it'd be nice if in offline mode you were travelling with all of team RWBY instead of just one character. Right now [because it's beta] you choose a character then go into the game but you ONLY have that character the entire time. No AI partners or character switch available, and if you wanted to play another character, you leave the game, go back into offline and choose a new character, but you start the entire game over again as that character. So a good idea would be to be able to have AI partners in offline mode [or maybe even online mode just as place holders] that you can easily switch between with the push of a button/menu option)
Just some recommendations I've got for the game that might make it a bit more appealing to those who aren't die hard fans. Bottom line: As the game is now, I can't in good consciousness recommend this game as incomplete as it is. If you're a big fan of the game or just want something to kill time, then I'd say go for the game. If you're not that kind of person, save your money for when it's more complete. If they make the game as a whole, from gameplay to story, more interesting then I'll change my review.

Do you dream of adventure, slaying dragons, fighting giants, drinking your profits away the night before your next quest?  Or do you want to be the person selling to those fools who risk their lives for a moment of fame?
If it's the latter, you might enjoy this game, one part "adventurer tycoon", one part janitor, and all parts fun, this game is about that most loved (still counts if you love to hate them) role in adventuring, the equipment merchant!
The game starts out a bit slow, order a few cheap items, sell them for as much as you can get away with, and quickly progresses into the realm of real (mostly) legal highway robbery!  Ah, the life of a merchant, just be aware that even in your little slice of heaven you will still have to deal with the most dreaded of adversaries... customers!
It's a fun little romp of a title that can be a real time killer, but you may eventually get bored with the "rinse/repeat" (buy, sell, murder a shoplifter) nature of the game as it is right now.  It's an Early Access title, so anything/everything could change tomorrow, but even as it is, it's a lot of fun if you like other games in the genre.

In my opinion Shoppe Keep is a very fun game that takes alot of cognitive work and multitasking, especially when you first start out. (excluding the 3 hours of ingame time of pure sweeping) I am going to present a list of my personal Pros/Cons of this very new game.
PROS__________
1. Presents a whole new and interesting perspective of gaming
2. Has manageable scenarios/tutorials that provide challenges
3. Has a Personal shoppe mode allowing you to create your own store
4. Takes cognitive work and planning to succeed
5. Decent graphics/animations on the NPCs
6. Good graphics for the items and the shoppe itself
7. Levelling system for your character,
based off of how much you sell
8. The Music would go in my top 5 List of video game music
CONS__________
1. AI is clunky and has trouble with maneuvering,
which can get you stuck with no way out
2. AI can refuse to accept that some items are free,
and sometimes treat them asthough they are extremely expensive
by trashing the items or ignoring them
3. A little too much dirt left behind by walking NPCs,
not too big of a problem, but a nuissance
4. Barbarians are able to attack through the walls,
meaning that some furniture can be destroyed,
if placed close enough to the wall
5. A little too easy to level up and needs more skills to invest in
6. Has a small amount of bugs scattered around
SUGGESTIONS__________
1. Needs more items and more variety (already has a decent amount,
But once you're rich it gets lame)
2. More skills to invest in and maybe special abilities
3. More of that Sweet Sweet Music
4. Able to Support the Steam workshop
5. Able to customize the size and actual shoppe itself,
E.G the wall colour and shape of the store
All in all this game is very fun and entertaining for me and it manages to do so in a very early state.

This game had the potential to be a rough gem, but instead it just turned out to be a poor copy of better games like System Shock 2 and Deus Ex.
The story is ripped straight out of System Shock 2, the devs call it "inspired by System Shock 2," but that's like saying a story about a chemistry teacher named Billy Black who makes meth with his former student Jose Purpleguy is "inspired by Breaking Bad." It's a BS excuse for not being original enough to come up with your own story.
The "stealth" is atrocious, you can stand right next to an enemy and they won't see you as long as you're not directly in front of them, but if you even DARE to stop crouching and try to walk 15 feet away from them, they will instantly swivel around and instantly firing/running at you. There's no enjoyable aspect of this, you can't fight enemies outright because the developers were too lazy to live up to the "open-ended levels for combative playstyles" they lied about in their description, so you must spend almost every minute of the game crouched down, sneaking past these enemies with awful AI that is supposedly "Advanced."
The audio is awful. Every 5 minutes the game plays this looping hissing sound that alternates between stereo and mono, which causes my ears to hurt within 15 seconds of it starting. The voice clips are muffled and of poor quality; I had to resort to subtitles to understand what the hell anybody was saying in the audio logs. Speaking of subtitles, there are an insane amount of spelling mistakes, it's like nobody even tried to spellcheck this game. In the first 30 minutes you go looking for a "PoweCell" and listen to "Incorent Audio Recordings".
The game is extremely linear, there's almost nowhere else to go besides where the plot tells you to go, so the game consists of crouching around, solving extremely easy puzzles, and listening to the characters who are all D-grade versions of characters from System Shock 2.
This could have been a good game, but instead its just a game filled to the brim with flaws that ends up being a poor copy of System Shock 2 rather than its own game.

I'm going to try and be constructive here and honestly I went into this game with an open mind, but it is a total let down. People who compare this game to System Shock, Deus Ex or Dead Space don't know what they're talking about. Solarix is a Science Fiction game with a Cyberpunk & Horror theme, that is where the similarities start and end.
This is a terrible mix of stealth, FPS and horror where you will spend 90% of the game crouching to avoid near sighted enemies who almost humorously go into an alert state from a single footstep the moment you leave the crouching position.
There is no customization or character skills, no inventory management and I counted all of 2 jump scares in the entire game. There is a total of 3 weapons, 1 of which is non-lethal and rarely works due to poorly coded hitboxes and the other 2 you're given very little ammo for. Lastly every single objective consists of going here or there, flipping switches and finding access cards.
Visually it looks like something from a decade ago, though maybe this was done ironically? And it is often choppy and stuttering for no apparent reason even on an i7 and 780ti.
I would call this a somewhat polished early access game at best. It supposedly has a length of about 7 or 8 hours, though I finished it in half that time even with numerous restarts due to glitches and bugs. There is a boring storyline here about a virus, engineers, corrupt AI systems, etc, with little to no character development and just on the whole everything feels very sloppy and unpolished.
I can see these guys (the developers) are fans of actual good games like System Shock 2 and so forth and you can see their influences, but Solarix can't even hold a candle to those games, try as it might.

Rise Of The Triad is a game that falls short of greatness. I'm not an♥♥♥♥♥kisser nor a hater, so I wanted to give my thoughts. ROTT is a shooter game, a reboot of the 1995 shooter of the same name. For the time, it was a rough game, but the wackiness helped it become a cult classic. The new game has been made to keep the same gameplay, the same wackiness as the original. The gameplay is execellent, blasting through enemies with an arsenal of weapons. The level design is quite good. It really stays faithful to its roots. The multiplayer is mostly absent, because not enough people play it. There are MP events, but they still only attract a dozen of players. This is one of the most poorly optimized games I've ever played. The framerate can drop massively at parts, and it can be annoying. Quicksaves have been added, too. If you're looking for a solid SP game that you can spend a while in, this is the game for you. If you're looking for the next Unreal Tournament, look somewhere else. It seems that people either make this game sound better than it actually is, or they make the game sound worse than what it actually is, so tread carefully. It's a solid game, but not a GOTY.
