TL;DR: I love this game, but the newest DLC packs♥♥♥♥♥♥me off to no end. SO I refuse to buy them until RT quits being greedy.
Opted in for the Beta, love the new combat system, but now my Logitech Gamepad F310 doesn't work like it used to. My left stick is no move. I bought the game Early Access, so I may as well do the beta♥♥♥♥♥♥ right?
My controller worked just fine until I got the Beta DL. I have to use the D-pad to move my charrie! I can accept that on an old school port, but this? No! Maybe I got some settings wrong, but the freaking gamepad worked like a charm until I Dl'ed the Beta stuff.
Edit 3/16: Since this review my gamepad works properly now.
I also wanted to expand on things a little. The combo system is awesome, thus far I've only played Weiss, but since she's my online go-to gal, that's mainly so I get some good practice in. But like I said the combo to special system is awesome. Also awesome is the counter system, I like how you interrupt the enemy attack instead of just blocking and taking either reduced damage, or no damage.
Sort of tying into the counter system, I really like the stagger/stun system. Stagger an enemy trigger a special, for Weiss it's an single strike and then a small AoE. I really like the first upgrade for it and will probably unlock the third upgrade fairly quickly.
Lastly I like the Ultimate system. It's a meter that charges when you attack enemies, but unlike before, it now starts at zero. So now, rather than depleting a meter when you use Nova, Peirce, or Barrage, it's a meter than fills with your combo. I don't think the combo specials charge it, I was too busy watching other things, but I'm pretty sure they don't deplete it. Also, it pops the button combo up over the meter when it's full, which kinda helps you notice that it's full without taking your attention off your fight. Love the power and radius upgrade, especially when you bump it to level two.
And yeah, basically, two mother-loving thumbs up on the combat revision. There are a few other things I could go into, but this covers the meat and potatoes of the changes. Get those voice-overs in and release it.

This is a great game. R.A. Salvatore is an author I adore, and the richness and detail of the world live up to Demon Saga and Forgotten Realms -level storytelling. The art is fantastic, and the gameplay is addictive. I've played through it a few times now, and I never tire of it.
The main premise (you are "fateless", with no pre-written destiny) was apparently not written by Salvatore, and that's nice to know since it makes no sense. Sure, you get to write your own fate, but so what? in any RPG you get to choose your own "fate". It seems like the storyline missed an opportunity to incorporate the struggle between a game's inherent linear story (if you want to complete the game, you DO have to follow the storyline, so you aren't really without destiny, are you?) and the idea that you are a character without a destiny. That aspect is never explored, and yet you're constantly being told throughout the game that everyone's really amazed by you because you have no pre-determined fate.
Aside from that, the game is perfect. The combat is FUN, the RPG elements are solid (in fact, you can change classes and skills quite easily), and the world is huge with lots of side quests.
The artwork is gorgeous, and it's boldly high fantasy. Every outfit, every cottage, every vardo, and every monster is as fantastic as you can imagine. Nothing is spared, visually, for this game world. And the world is HUGE. Every time you think you've surely reached the end of the map, there turns out to be yet more to explore, and yet another culture to learn about.
I played this originally on the PS3, and I've easily played every quest and every DLC. I've played as every available race and class. Nothing is better than anything else; everything in this game is equally fun and powerful. Special abilities are a pleasure to gain and use, the weapons are nuanced and addictive, and when you level up, you feel like the most amazing gamer who ever lived. This. Is a fun game.
And if you like lore, then this is an enchanting game. There's so much to learn in this game. There are books to read, and magical messages to listen to, dialague, hints, clues, ruins.
It's not all just running around killing stuff, either. After my 5th or 6th playthrough, I eventually decided to approach it from other angles.  You can do all kinds of research and exploration, and you'll discover lots of cool items to craft and potions to brew.
So many ways to play just one game. My only wish is that there was a native Linux port.
Highly recommended.

Ah, Kingdoms of Amalur, how I love thee. Let me count the ways.
The lore. Oh, the lore. Is it not amazing to be running through the land, come across a stone, use it, and this beautiful music comes on with someone reciting some poetry? It's short enough that by the time I reach the next stone, or another destination, it's finished so I can hear another song or snippet of history, or enter a dungeon without having to wait until the voiceover's done.
Combat's somewhat unique. Every "branch" has multiple weapons that does more damage with it, or unlocks some different moves. KoAR isn't exactly like Bayonetta or DMC - there aren't enough unlocks for each weapon to string beautifully into dance moves across a bloody floor, but there's enough of them to make a difference in combat.
The story's not the most out of the world. You die. You get resurrected. Your fate's changed to the point where you can change fate, if you can follow that. Never mind all that. I
the House of Ballads' stories and lore. I won't ruin it too much, but it does indeed follow our realistic meaning of immortality, that we may remain alive through song and stories.
One of the only real problems I seemed to have with the game is, at the beginning, being somewhat of an OCD player who hates going back to old maps because new things popped up, I felt really "compelled" with a gun to my head to choose the path of all three branches (Might, Finesse, Magic) in order to unlock a Destiny that adds +1 to skills. It was the only way for me to explore the early game, while being able to see secret doors and chests, etc. Otherwise, like a previous play through, I'd have to unlock Level 8, then put those points in, then run back into an under leveled place to complete the map 100%.
Other than that, it's a distracting enough ARPG that has a silent protagonist who broods, slays lots of things, in order to take on a villain that's killing everyone and everything.

Solarix is a pleasant surprise amongst the Stealth Horror" genre.
Its a very different game from your average stealth romp, it plays similar to Thief, mixed with a hint of Deus Ex and all wrapped up in System Shock 2 sauce.
The game's story was a great and pleasant surprise, although it defintely overwhelms you at first as you are thrown alot of details, some which you won't really get until later in the game. Where the story really starts picking up, the characters start to become fully realized in their intentions and things come full circle. I won't spoil it one single bit for anyone that wants to enjoy it for themselves, it is honestly deeper than it is initially thought up as on the steam store.
The Locations have a good variety to them, and remain for the most part open world. They also do a excellent job of building atmosphere, like all good horror games.. you are spent the majority actually all of Solarix, alone. Absolutely alone, with nary a friend in the world. Just trying to get by guards and zombies. There are things to pick up that don't initally come over on the subtitled conversations or audio logs, like little computer tid bits, actual audio/video onscreen and a few of the characters. There is every now and then always a sound of a nearby zombie/strogg/idk. Some of the ambience sounds repeat which is a bit annoying but nothing too serious.
The Gameplay can tend to be a bit repetitive in the first half as it introduces its mechanics on the colony. There is a bit of confusion also in the level design in the first half and it made me a skeptic of what else the game had to offer. By the second part, i started getting better and started really enjoying the game, the atmosphere and the story. It wasn't triple AAA but it was entertaining and i liked the homage to the games of the past like System Shock 2. (One of my favorite games of all time.) If i had any tips to give to you, its that guns may seem like a very easy way of taking your enemies out at first and running past zombies is totally possible, later in the game is absolutely not lenient on you. Use the electric back prod, stay in the shadows and keep your guns locked and loaded for something scary or if things go wrong.
I came into Solarix with bad impressions, the presentation of the beginning didn't exactly thrill me after experiencing Ghost Ship CDF, which was also built in UDK and it felt like a very similar vibe. Until i really dug into it.
In terms of horror, at most the game gets unsettling, like you defintely wouldn't want to stick around for an extended period of time. Nothing like system shock 2 where you didn't feel safe at all because of the occassionally respawning enemies. Solarix has a good reason not to do so, because late in the game enemies are much more difficult to handle. Requiring more ammo and different tactics to take out your enemies. It almost turns into a puzzle game of when to  strike during the patrol pattern. I grew to like it.
Now, comes down to the bad parts.
The AI isn't very good, and can give you some seriously weird moments where you'll walk directly past a enemy and he won't give a single ♥♥♥♥. Where he'll glance at you for a moment, you'll sh*t yourself and he just walks right past you. Yes, alot of that will happen while you are playing Solarix. So much its kinda jarring. I wanted so badly for the enemies to interact with each other, particularly the mercs and the zombies. Or to see a merc so very rarely, freak out and lose his♥♥♥♥♥♥and start killing his comrades. Stuff like that would stop the AI feeling like a bunch of patrol patterns and little else.
The story at the start is too overloading, it either doesn't tell you what the point of being there is or who these characters are and what is their purpose. Maybe its a way of not patronising the player but it got confusing for the first half. Some of that confusion is absolutely intentional however, so don't jump the gun and that is as much of a spoiler as i am giving you for the second half of the game.
I'd also say that if Solarix would have been developed in another engine, it would have looked a little better. I mean it doesn't look bad by any means, just not great.
The gameplay feels a bit repetive, just a little. If they kept it fresh towards the end it would have been great.
Maybe add in a another enemy type for that extra challenge towards the end because once i got to a certain point then that was a breeze.
I feel the price point is right, for the amount of fun that i had with it. I would recommend hard for an extra challenge because normal wasn't particularly challenging except for the very end. If you love sci-fi horror games, its still worth the spin even if it isn't particularly scary. If you have played Deus Ex, System Shock 2 or Thief then you will like this game, i am pretty sure about that.
I'll probably come back to it after awhile and replay it on hard, since i had a fair amount of fun with it.
TL:DR?
Fantastic for the money provided you like the mediocre mechanics and well crafted story. Just expect it to be a little rough around the edges in places. If you like old school stuff like deus ex, thief, system shock 2 then consider buying it because it is a blast.

I haven’t played a good horror game for a long time! Since Outlast actually but everything changed! Everything changed when I tried Solarix, a game created by Pulsetense Games and published by KISS ltd! Solarix is a science-fiction horror game featuring open-ended levels for both combative and stealth-focused playstyles. The devs have managed to combine old-school sci-fi horror with next-gen style and graphics.
The story follows an electrical engineer desperately fighting for his life, after an infection wipes out an interstellar research station. He must contain the disease, battling both the remnants of the crew and his own fracturing mind. The goal of the devs is also to go beyond jump scares and cheap thrills. Solarix is about a world that overpowers you with unease, insecurity, and desperation, forcing you to confront your own role in the horrors to come. Solarix is definitely one of the good representatives of the horror genre games.
It features a lot of jump scares, like for example that zombie in the window that really scared the hell out of me in the beginning of the game. Another aspect I loved is the whole atmosphere the game creates. Dark, full of horror aspects but everything has such a unique feeling at the same time. Moreover, another aspect worth mentioning is that I liked the balance between stealth, FPS and horror.
Basically it is up to you to choose how you are going to play the game! Are going all stealth? Avoiding your enemies and try to hide in the darkness or just kill everyone? It up to you!
Also, a strong positive of the game is definitely the storyline. You try to understand what happened? Who are you and what you have to do to survive! However there are some negative aspects I should mention! Since I reviewed the beta version of the game! There were bugs in the gameplay and the music. Also, sometimes I felt a little bit lost inside the levels, I didn’t know what to do or go! Another thing that it should be improved a little bit is the dialogs. They should introduce better the characters to the player and who they exactly are and their role in the game. But that creates a sense of mystery which is great and you eventually learn more about them as you continue your journey.
To sum up, this game is a lot of fun, scary and delivers an incredible gameplay experience! Totally recommended it by me to all horror and sci-fi game lovers out there!
Verdict: 8/10
+ Atmosphere
+ Jump scares
+ Balance between stealth, fps and horror but play your way at the same time
+ Storyline
- A lot of characters in the game are left without a proper introduction to the player at first. Who they are etc...but that creates a mystery aspect since we are learning more as we play the game about them

Let me start by saying this is my first review, and everything expressed in this review is a matter of personal taste.
The game is fun. Living the life of a Shoppe Keeper is a cathartic experience that's nice to wind down after a hard day at work. What really appeals to me is you're not forced to kill enough people per level/day to be classified as a medium sized natural disaster, but you can if you want. There's no rule to say you can't murder all your paying customers as well as thieves. There's a tax placed on you for murdering innocents, but honestly it's so small that ocasionally I started zapping people for giggles.
Buying shelves and placing them is fairly simple, ordering items is also simple. It'd be nice to have a snapping feature so I can place tables and shelves and such end to end with no gaps and agenst the walls. But what I have to say is my favorit thing about this early access release is how much effort the devs are putting in to listening to the players.
For instance, my two personal peeves in the game were how you had to remove every item from a shelf in order to reprice them, and how customers seem to be mudmen from the plannet swampzilla for the amount of dirt they track in. In a quickly implimented patch, door mats were introduced, which stop customers from tracking in dirt, and it was made so that changing the price of one item changes the ones already placed as well. These are supposidly only temporary fixes with improvments comming as development continues. This shows that the devs are listening and they want this game to be fun.
However, the game is not perfect. It's early access, so there's bugs, missing features, and some things that are just kind of obnoxious at present. The tax system for instance seems to be there only to soak up some of your money. There are no guards, no improvments made to the outside town over time ect. I guess the mayor of the town just sleeps on a bed made of solid gold in his mansion made of solid gold or something. It's also a bit to easy to accidently incinerate an innocent with your zap spell because it has a large hit box, but as someone who kills the civies for giggles that's not really a big deal to me personaly. There's also an upgrade that makes it so you can't kill innocents, which I've ignored because every now and then i want to be the evil shop master of the demon realm.
This game is well worth the price of entry, and if you're looking for something origional and fun it's right here. I truly look forward to this games future and hope that the devs can take this game from good to great. It has real potential to a powerhouse of time wasting.

Well, here's one hell of disappointment. You'd think, someone who grew up playing oldschool shooters and wishing for the last couple of years for a proper sequel to Painkiller is going to like this game. That's what I thought, at least. I knew about the game having problems with performance and being full of bugs - that's why I didn't buy it at launch. But, there have been like 2 huge patches. So naturally, I expected - that most of the problems got fixed. Nope! I have no idea how bad it used to be, but as for today - which is with patch 1.2, this game is still a mess.
While the level design is great, being a faithful remake of original game from 1995 and there are some pretty neat throwbacks to old games, not to mention easter eggs and references to new games. This is pretty much where the fun with Rise of the Triad ended for me. It's just such a generic Unreal Engine game - and it feeeeeeels like it. It has literally everything problem common with Unreal engine based games, I've experienced. From freezes when loading a chunk of a map, through problems with texture streaming (which can be reduced, at the cost of ever bigger freezes when loading a chunk of map), lackluster, unresponsive movement mechanics (common for most Unreal based games), awful loading times (even when loading a save file) and many more. Even when it comes to performance, it ultimately ends up being very disappointing with framerates below 60fps on medium settings. That alone wouldn't be bad, but the fact is - it doesn't even feel like 60fps - it feels like half of it, and no - that isn't just a problem with vsync. It just always felt laggy and unresponsive. Which is a damn shame - cause, I really wanted to like this game. I wanted to recommend this game to other people - but in all honesty, I can't. Not with this type of uneven graphics. Not with this type of performance and that type generic of a gameplay, which is even made more boring due to extremely dull shooting mechanics. The only fun I got in it was of exploration of levels, but even that turned out to be annoying, due to mentioned earlier movement system. Having bought it 66% off, I still feel bad that I spent the money for it. It just wasn't worth it. Not even a bit. All this game did, was made me realize, that I really should have bought
or just save the money for the new

An exercise in frustration and riding the hype train. For all its bells and whistles and the promise of old school fun, it didn't deliver. The singleplayer campaign is a prime example of poor 90's game design with traps, puzzles, and enemy spawns that require memorization to beat vs skill. The game's combat is primarily find a firebomb and use the ammo for it as efficiently as possible while picking off individual enemies using your mp40 with stun locking animations. Boss fights are essentially finding a way to glitch the boss and/or cheese the fight. There's no real skill involved except for maybe the last boss but that's also based on knowing where the armor pickups are; you can still cheese it by glitching the boss into a wall. Most of the later levels are designed really poorly with only a few of them being fun to run through. The first set of levels delivers the experience really well with overwhelming enemies that you have the joy of exploding into bits but it doesn't stay that way. The multiplayer is really the only good selling point. It's fast, frantic, and rather fun but the lack of players and servers in all areas doesn't paint a good picture for it. Supposedly the devs are planning for bots later on down the line but I'm not holding my breath.

Rise of the Triad is a remake of the 1995 game of the same name, you are part of the HUNT team (High-risk United Nations Task-force) and you must infiltrate the Triad base while killing hundreds of Triad members with a moderate range of weapons.
You can choose 1 of 5 characters, each with their own stats, such as the big bulky guy who can take a large amount of damage but is very slow, or play as the female asian woman who is the fastest of the group but also the weakest in terms of defence. If you want my recommendation I would say pick a fast character with good defence, as running around at the speed of sound is just so much fun. No matter how you play as though, the voice acting will be bloody horrible but in a good way that I ended up laughing.
You start with a basic pistol which does pretty low damage until you get another pistol in which you can then duel wield, even though weak it still felt very fun to use. However, you will then recieve heavy weapons which are by far some of the best weapons in the game. You can rocket jump and absolutely destroy enemies. There are a total of 7 different heavy weapons, which range from rocket launchers (BOOM!), flame throwers (SSS!), and heat seeking missles (beep beep).
However, the absolute best weapons in the game, are the powerups and the magic weapons. For powerups you have God mode, which is not just infinite health, you are actually a God and you can zap enemies killing them in 1 hit. Then you got dog mode which turns you into a dog where you can bite enemies and do AOE (area of effect) attacks. Then you have the brilliant Excellebat, which is a bat that acts like a sword, everytime you hit an enemy they will blow up leaving a bloody mess everywhere. The final magic weapon is the magic staff, which shoots an electric beam as well as creating a shield for you.
There are also powerdowns, such as the mushroom which makes you feel like you're on some acid trip, and a bouncy powerdown which makes you bounce everytime you come into contact with a wall.
In each stage there are a number of secrets, when you find these secrets you can get special weapons, ammo, health, and easter eggs which takes me back to the old Quake days. In fact, the entire game is basically an old school game which non-regerating health, keys, floating spinning weapons, coins floating around for points, etc.
I will however say, that the A.I. of the enemies is abysmal, I see them regularing forgetting to shoot their gun at me, walk into walls, standing in place, and so on and so forth.
The bossfights are kinda mixed bag, the first and 3rd boss fights are pretty entertaining, but the 2nd one was very dull where you just stand in a room waiting for the guy to stop shooting, then you move out shoot at him, and repeat the same process. And the final boss holy cow it is bad, it starts out pretty cool, you're flying with the flying powerup, but once you beat the 1st form of the boss, the 2nd form is just the final boss running towards you and you just keep spraying.
Also the final boss kept glitching out on me where I had to reset.
Oh and the last problem I have is the freaking bugs. I've frequently got a bug where I could not fire my weapon until I restarted a checkpoint, the enemies would freak out and become deformed, and many textures were broken on me.
Although the last complaint may seem a bit major, I cannot deny that I had a blast while playing Rise of the Triad, it's mindless fun, and that's all I need.
There is multiplayer, however I've never managed to get a match with enough people which is shame.
Also when you type in the chat and press enter, the game will actually read it out in a robotic voice like microsoft Sam, which is pretty bloody cool.
Once I've managed to join a populated server, I will edit this review detailing how it went and how it works.
Last thing to mention is the brilliant soundtrack, almost all of the music are remixes of the soundtrack from the 1995 version and it is kickass!
Rise of the Triad is Excellent, and is how you make a proper reboot of a beloved first person shooter.

As a fan of the RWBY web series, this game is something I was highly anticipating.  When the product came out on Early Access, I knew it was going to be incomplete so I went in with your standard Early Access expectations.  Yes, there are only four levels at the time of the writing of this review, but those levels are enjoyable to replay time and time again provided you are into this kind of game.  And I believe it will only get better as the game grows closer to completion.
As far as the drawbacks go, the game is not without several flaws.  I find myself fighting the camera more than I fight the Grimm.  I don't believe it pans out far enough most of the time and, with the recent addition of zooming in outside of combat, you often see the camera clip through the ground and show the sky box for a brief moment.  I'm sure this will be fixed eventually, but for now it does throw me off.
One more plus about the game, is that it is DualShock 4 compatible.  You won't need any extra third party software to play the game using your Playstation 4 controller.  They have taken care of that on their end and it works just as well as using the Xbox controller.
I guess what I'm trying to say is, this game is not perfect.  Not yet.  But it's still leagues better than a lot of other games that get greenlit on Steam.  If you're a fan of RWBY or a fan of these types of games, then I say get it while it's still fifteen dollars.  They have said the price will increase as the game is completed.  And if you have never seen or heard of RWBY until now, this might just be a nice introduction to the series before you actually watch it.  Or, watch it first and then see if this game still interests you.

My review will be mainly about gameplay mechanics. The game mechanics in its stage presently has improved tremendously since testing last year in 2016. Movement animations and combat were a bit underdeveloped in '16. Now in '17 though, the character has fluid movement and combat animations. You can move while reloading (not present in Mount & Blade: NW). Reload actually uses the stick into the musket, nice bit of immersion. Officers can use Lanterns at night, and you can turn lanterns on in the environment/buildings/battleships. Officers can use spyglasses. Currently you can't drop weapons or pick them up. Melee attacks at the same time + angle (i.e. up-stab) cancel each other's out. There's no chambering that I know of right now. Bump hits don't exist (which was a problem in M&B:NW, zero damage hits). You can feint attacks. For those that don't know how combat works, infantry bayonets only up or down-stab, and swords have 4 way directional attacks. You can block by blocking the respective side of attack.
NAVAL COMBAT:
Naval combat is a great addition to NW. Each boat has designated classes, including musicians, officers, sailors. There currently is no cannon reload animation in early access, but that doesn't stop the huge 30+ inch cannons from feeling powerful. The shot types of cannon are 1. Cannonball and 2. Chain-ball. The chain ball is used to take down the enemy Masts, and the cannonballs can take out enemy sailors/damage the boat's integrity. Boats can be destroyed in various ways, and you can launch emergency rowboats once it sinks.
Environment destruction:
You can destroy Fort walls with cannon currently, damage buildings and destroy ships.
Weather:
The environment dynamically changes. One minute a grassy field can turn into a white, shiny snowfield. Or it could turn to a moonlit night, riddled with fog, or a downpouring, bright-thundery rain.
In short conclusion, there are still things to add animation-wise, and Cavalry needs to be put in still. The devs are open to improvements and will listen to feedback on their website forum. The game brings many new unique features and draws from M&B:NW.

Ah, Kingdoms of Amalur, how I love thee. Let me count the ways.
The lore. Oh, the lore. Is it not amazing to be running through the land, come across a stone, use it, and this beautiful music comes on with someone reciting some poetry? It's short enough that by the time I reach the next stone, or another destination, it's finished so I can hear another song or snippet of history, or enter a dungeon without having to wait until the voiceover's done.
Combat's somewhat unique. Every "branch" has multiple weapons that does more damage with it, or unlocks some different moves. KoAR isn't exactly like Bayonetta or DMC - there aren't enough unlocks for each weapon to string beautifully into dance moves across a bloody floor, but there's enough of them to make a difference in combat.
The story's not the most out of the world. You die. You get resurrected. Your fate's changed to the point where you can change fate, if you can follow that. Never mind all that. I
the House of Ballads' stories and lore. I won't ruin it too much, but it does indeed follow our realistic meaning of immortality, that we may remain alive through song and stories.

I never played the orginal GunZ, so I can't really say anything comparing it to this or anything about "K-Style". I can however write a review based on my experience with this game, so here goes. (I'm gonna type this as I go, might revise a few things here and there) To start off, for an early access game, this is beautiful. Gameplay is fast-paced and exciting, controls are fluid and responsive, and everything I've seen has been aesthetically appealing (How the aesthetics look could be different for other players, because the game sets a default graphical setting depending on your computer. Mine was defaulted to low, but today I decided to try a higher setting, and going from low to medium is like going from 8-bit to 1040p HD. Anyways...) So far the game has been very good. I love the diversity in character weapons and skills, and each character I've played (all but Elena so far) has been fun in a unique way. There are many different strategies that can be used with each class, which keeps playstyle diverse even when multiple people play the same character. However, as much as I love this game and don't want to say anything bad about it, I kind of have to give some constructive criticism here so the developers can continue to improve it. Firstly, although its not too big a deal, there is a little bit of balancing issue with some of the characters. I know with this much variety its hard to keep perfect balance between classes, and the developers have done a wonderful job with the balancing, but two weapon types in specific need to be addressed here. There's Max's flamethrower, which is extremely overpowered in close quarters, and there's Elena's grenade launcher. I haven't noticed too much abuse with the grenade launcher, but for balance I would reccomend making it damage the user and/or making it less accurate. I have, however, noticed a very large ammount of flamethrower abuse. To prevent this, I would reccomend decreasing the range, as well as damage or ammo capacity. Second off, I realize that with a free to play title developers need to find a way to make money. I can understand in-game purchases and feel they are justified, but only to so much extent. There are a few things that should be changed, for the developers' benefit (look, more people will buy things if theyre cheaper) and for the players' benefit (more fun stuff for everyone). #1, I really want to play through the campaign, but its impossible without spending a ton of money on revival coins. I havent actually checked how much they are, but from what I've heard, theyre 5 bucks a pop. Sure, you dont HAVE to play campaign, but I find it enjoyable sometimes to kill a bunch of weak enemies instead of get the crap beat out of me by other players. If they were to lower the price on them, (or better yet get rid of them) I would be very happy, or even if they would mess with a few of the numbers so enemies don't 3-shot you and drop more med-kits. #2, I enjoy having horse masks and top hats as much as the next guy, but people probably arent going to buy them at 10-15 dollars each. I probably would have bought one by now if they weren't so damned expensive, because I love this game and want to support it, but dont want to spend $40 on accessories. #3, I hate to be nit-picky, but each character has a "starting kit" available for purchase that comes with a costume and a good weapon. While I dont see anything wrong with that, the price tag on each one is a whopping $35, and that was when it said %50 off. I know after all that it may seem like I berated the game, but if it did that wasnt my intent. I intended for the developers to read this and maybe take my suggestions, so that a great game can get even better. While I didnt talk about the good as much as the bad, I felt it would be difficult (and boring for any of you that read this) to try and stretch out the positive more than I needed to. In conclusion, this is an excellent game and I most certainly reccomend playing it, but I dont really reccomend planning on too many purchases unless your wallet has a lot of money in it. I'd give this game around an 8.5 to a 9 out of 10. If you actually read down to here, congratulations, you'll probably be able to tolerate school text books if you havent gotten through school already. Thank you for reading this, and have a wonderful day full of gaming. That about sums it up, cya! :) (Edit: Forgot to mention, the music is top-notch. Theres not a ridiculous ammount of tracks, but the ones they do have are really good and never get old)

The gameplay is fun and makes your brain engage more in what's happening (uses a controller). I will play this again just like I'll watch all the Miyazaki films again.

First things first in only one word: EPIC
Now, let´s go into detail.
Background:
I loved the first game. I played Torchlight for many hours, always trying to get the next best item. It had a fair loot-system and a "quick-to-learn" skill system - Even though there wasn´t that much to "learn", as the Skillsystem is very intuitive. The Story wasn´t that interessting, but at least motivating enough to go on. The only thing I would´ve criticized is, that there was absolutly no way to give your character some unique look. But that´s not that important while playing a dungeoncrawler, right?!
Story:
Theres nothing I can remember, to be honest.. Evil dude has to be killed. Very generic, but this game isn´t as storydriven as, for example, Diablo, so it doesn´t really matter in my opinion. :D
Graphics:
The graphicstyle´s kinda standard for a comic-look kind of game. In retrospectiv, it didn´t changed that much, when you compare it to Torchlight 1. But it doesn´t really matter! The publishers created a, in my opinion, very interesting and good-looking world, each world has a unique look and they don´t re-use previously used locations. But as always, graphics are a very individual thing to judge about. BUT I do have one little thing to criticize: Even though Torchlight II offers some kind of optic changes for your character, they all seem to look the same! When I create a Berserker, I don´t really want to only create a crazy lookin´ dude - just sayin´. I have not found any other optic possibilities in the Steam-Workshop, but that´s nothing that changes the way I think about this game.
Game mechanics:
It works perfectly. The hack n´slay elements are working good, the skillsystem is easy to get in, the loot-system works fine for me. In comparison to Torchlight I, they didn´t changed that much. "Never change a running system" seems to have been the maxim of the developers - And they were absolutly right with following that. Even though I haven´t seen anything in this game, it keeps me motivated. Could spend many, many hours of playing, having long playing sessions about 4 hours long.
That´s what a dungeoncrawler should do!
Conclusion:
If you want a numberal rating, I will give this game a 9/10, for being a solid second title, for doing (almost) everything right and keeping you motivated through the hole game. You can spend endless hours in this world, while you´re loot-hunting or just playing with some friends in multiplayer (don´t play multiplayer that much, so I didn´t talked about it, but the multiplayer works perfectly). Buy this game. It´s just fantastic. Enter the World of Torchlight II - Allons-y!

Have you ever wondered what it's like to own a shop during those brutal medieval times? Well, wonder no more, because Shoppe Keep is here. A game that will make you hate thieves even more and broom will be your best friend. Expected to manage your own shop by ordering a supplies, changing price tags and defending it from little thieves and groups of bandits; you are supposed to be a greatest 'shoppe keeper' in the world.
This game so far offers 19 scenarios, each of them more challanging then the previous one (obviously). From selling a few potions, to supplying a town for an attack, you will be the one to profit from it all. But it's not that easy. Various people will have different requirements. While one will be poor and wants a simple health potion, rich warrior will want some golden plated shield and you'll have to satisfy all demands if you want to be good.
Not counting on the fact, that you get minimum profit from cheap items and you will not sell expensive items that easily. Oh, and taxes. Yeah, you will be charged with taxes every 5 minutes. Oh! And thieves. People will steal from you. OH! And dirt... People are unbelievable pigs, broom is literally your best friend as I said earlier. Oh, and... Well, you get the point.
As you sell various items, you will gain XP points as in proper RPG game. Next levels will give you K-points, which you can exchange for different perks. One will give you a 10 % discount for your order, while another will make deliveries come faster or makes an entry fee for your shop.
After you finish first (or second?) scenario, you'll also unlock "My Shoppe" (Free Play) mode. In here, you can build your own shop with stands and tables and simply make yourself at home.
When it comes to a graphics of the game, there are certainly few things that needs a polishing, but it's quite nice game offering this (optional) cell-shade tint with enjoyable and minimal dubbing along with some sounds that might get repetitive after a while, but it's not a big deal.
Shoppe Keeps is not a one-of-a-kind game, but it's definitely a game worth your time and money. It has its idea and it seems that the creators are going the right way. More items, more shop buildings, more detailed options and this might be a great game.
Do I recommend this game? -- Yes.
Do I think you should wait for a sale? -- Sale for 5€ game?! Don't make me laugh...
Do I think that this game is really worth your time and money? -- Well... Yeah. And after all, you can always request a refund, can't you? (Please, don't, it's really worth it)

Pros:
Combat System is fast paced (Loyal to the show) - Characters hit fast, Move fast and combo fast. Just like the Show!
Constant Updates - The developers are working day and night to try and finish this game 100% and add another 10% everytime they have. They really love this game and are adding so much to it.
4 Player Co-Op - Having you and your friends play as all 4 members of Team RWBY is so much damn fun.
Skill Tree System - Though it doesn't add much, Its the best progression system we can get for a RWBY Game.
Locations - Looks exactly as if they were in the show.
Graphics - Not so great in the eyes of those looking for Unreal Engine 4 but Good enough to think "Yep, This is RWBY"
Cons:
Repetitive (Very) - You constantly fight the same enemies over and over and do the exact same defense mission everytime. Basically Horde mode with RWBY characters.
Short - The game lasts about two hours at the most finishing the first campagin (More are to be added in future updates)
Story - Its a simple "Find out whats happening" to then be left on a tiny cliff hanger...
4 Characters - For a RWBY game with only 4 characters is kind of a bummer. Especially in the universe of RWBY where there are over 20 Characters that could have been added. (Team JNPR, Team CFVY, Team SSSN) But that is asking for too much. Would like to see more characters though.
No Achievements - As a completionist, I look to games for achievements as a goal at times and seeing as how there isn't a lot to do in the game, it would be nice to have some achievements.
Note:
The game is fun for about 4 hours after completing the 1st Campagin mission along with trying every character out. From then on, There isn't much to do but replay the game over and over. It loses its touch after just a few hours. I will admit, I love the way they designed the characters specials and moves. They fit each other so perfectly. I just wish they would add other characters like Jaune, Nora, Prryha, etc. For the price of 15$ its O-K. But I'd say wait till its on sale at least 10$ because at the current state. It feels like a 10$ maybe a 12$ game. To me personally. I love the RWBY franchise and I will admit, This game is loyal to the series in every way possible.
Completionist Note:
If you are a completionist (Like me) You'll find yourself with very little to work with. No secret items (Other than artifacts that don't give you anything but XP). No achievements. The only thing we have to complete are the challenges within the Skill Tree. Some are basic like reach Level 10 with this character. Others are as follows - Kill 300 enemies with this skill or Kill 400 enemies with this skill. Basic stuff.

The year is 2013, and the First Person Shooter genre has gone to hell in a handbasket. The once sprawling, secret-filled maps of yesteryear have given way to liner corridors, with cutscenes every few steps. In trying to emulate blockbuster movies, videogames have lost sight of so much of what made them such worthwhile experiences. Regerating health has replaced healing pickups, and button mashing quicktime events have infected every inch of the FPS experience. Not to mention that most modern heroes are such wusses that they can't even wade into the crossfire without dying instantly, preferring to hide behind cover trading shots like spineless cowards. Thank god for Rise of The Triad, and for the awesome and ballsy team at Interceptor Entertainment for bringing it to us.
The first thing you're gonna notice when you start up Rise of The Triad is that the launcher lets you customize EVERY LITTLE DETAIL of the graphics settings. That's right, no craptastic consolization here. Once you get into the ingame menu you can finish setting the basics like resolution, brightness and stuff, as well as choose your FOV. Again, no consoleized BS here. The new soundtrack is utterly badass, with remixed tracks by Andrew Hulshult of Burying The Trend. The use of the Unreal Engine also makes for eye candy, Rise of The Triad has NEVER looked this good. It's good to see that the folks at Interceptor give a damn about what makes PC gaming sofa king awesome.
For one thing, the sprawling mazelike levels that made oldschool gaming so much fun make a triumphant return, with dead ends, keys to match up with doors, and a total boatload of secrets. Seriously look EVERYWHERE around you, chances are that little out-of-the-way nook or cranny is hiding something badassedly awesome. The team at Interceptor have hidden awesome references new and old alike all over the levels (Dopefish Lives!). Oh, and then there's the other thing that makes PC gaming especially kicking rad: MODS! Rise of The Triad fully supports modding, and even has it's own easy to use drag-and-drop level editor so that you can make your own insidious arenas of mayhem and death!
Ok, all that stuff sound fine and dandy, but how does it actually play? Well imagine someone took the original Rise of The Triad, made it prettier, added better mouse aiming and WASD controls, and then basically turned everything up to 11 AND added more cowbell. Rise of The Triad looks and plays effing amazing, with a perfect challenge level for any player out there. There's a veritable army of foes waiting for you to take them on, and enough firepower to deal with them all. And that's just the singleplayer, there is also a full fledged badass multiplayer experience to be had, and let me tell you it is utter forking bliss. What other game lets you turn into a dog, zip across a bridge at breakneck speeds, and then tear your enemies a new one with your razor-sharp maw? CoD's dog is a wussy chihuahua compared to this beast. Oh and if you want you can do 'shrooms while you blast your foes into chutney.
So let's chalk things up here: Big freaking guns, frickin awesome powerups, four massive single player episodes, enough multiplayer to choke a horse (one of those big Clydesdale things, not some rainbow colored friendship pony), more guns, mayhem, Dopefish, secrets, adjustable FOV, ludicrous gibs, and a guy who is seriously named I.P. Freely. How could you possibly go wrong with this fluffy stack of murder pancakes? If you don't go out and buy this game now, you are seriously missing out and should really reconsider your priorities in life. Rise of The Triad earns a solid 11 out of 10, and also pre-emptively wins the Slipgate Complex FPS of The Year awards for the next decade, or until they come out with a sequel. Go. Buy it now. Rise of the Triad is a serious WW2 shooter. You can choose to play as 5 different characters, all with their own phrases and strengths, as you battle through well crafted if unoptimised levels. Shoot walls and watch bits flake off. Shoot enemies and watch blood spew everywhere. Battle your way through historically accurate levels as you confront intelligent enemies. They have a great shot, can move quickly, will dodge your attacks and will even steal your weapons off of you and TRAP YOU IN A NET.
It's all good fun and there is a lot of replayability in the form of achievements and secret areas to find. It's the most full-on FPS game since Serious Sam (which itself is very serious) and really deserves to be played. The original game came out in the mid 90's and included God mode, Dog mode, spinning blades and bouncing platforms, all of which make a return in this game.
Better still, the people who have made this game are CRAZY. They've replied ALL IN CAPS to my fanboyish messages on youtube, to people on the forums and generally just don't seem to give a damn about how respectable companies are meant to behave. Do them a favour and buy this game. It's cheap and will most likely give you more fun than the more mainstream shooters. This sort of SERIOUS game needs to be encouraged. Long live the 90's!

This game is unadulterated fun with all the Rock and Roll legends and is just perfectly written for Jack Black, however,  the game has some major flaws.
First and most egregious since it's an adventure game, is: The camera is complete and utter garbage. Constantly getting lost or turned around during boss fights means you have no idea if the boss did their "special move" so I can attack it at the right time. This is a fundamental problem.  I've switched to a controller from the mouse, but it's not much of an improvement. The "lock" on button is critical when playing so you can flick the camera around which of course makes you want to throw up. The game palette which understandably makes sense for the type of game it is -- is way too dark, and there is no first person hud of any kind that tells you your health, the bosses health, minimap, etc. These didn't stop me from finishing the game, but it did make the experience a chore.
The writing has always carried Tim Schaefer's games and this one is no exception. Fantastic voice acting with authentic Rock and Roll legends.
If you love JB, heavy metal, and adventure games, buy this. Just don't do it for full price.

Let's face it, you're only contemplating picking up Brutal Legend because you're either a metal fan, a Jack Black fan, or both. Those are all good reasons to pick it up, but probably the
good reasons.
The moment-to-moment gameplay is decent-but-not-great, so that's not going to keep you enjoying this game. Combat can be tedious, the RTS elements feel out of place, the driving can be fairly enjoyable though. What's going to make you stay in this world is the ludicrous metal mythology and the pretty well-delivered comedy.
The world was inspired by metal album covers, so picture a few releases by Judas Priest, Manowar, and Iron Maiden, mash them all up, and you'll be half-way there.

Mount & Blade: Warband native is an excellent game. It offers an immersive and realistic single-player experience, along side an incredibly entertaining multi-player with fast paced death match servers and slower paced siege servers to provide a perfect experience for any kind of player. A phenomenal game with a single-player I myself have poured approximately 300 hours into. Something about invading all of Calradia with an army of highly trained Swadian Knights gave me a real objective that, unlike a lot of games, actually made me excited to complete the objective. Every feature of the single-player is well thought out and well implemented, I have yet to find a single feature that I think NEEDS improving; in the entire game I have yet to find a single issue that REQUIRES fixing as even the concerns I have about this game are minor and are certainly not game breaking, in fact a few of my concerns simply come from the perspective of newer players to the game. The few complaints I can make concerning the single-player are certainly minor but I feel that they must be mentioned to be fair and open with my reviews, the single-player is very poorly explained. The only guidance you get is at the very beginning when it explains the general concepts of a medieval society, companions are not explained at all and the vast majority of the features are left with no explanation so newer players are forced to learn by trial and error. I personally feel that this is a minor issue and overall rate the campaign as an 8/10. Multi-player is a completely different beast, however I still find myself with the same positive feelings and I am amazed by how well the rather simplistic fighting system works and flows. This is by far the greatest fighting system I have ever found, that is no exaggeration either. The ‘simple to learn, impossible to master’ system gives newer players an easy time as the 4 lanes of attack are easy to pick up and this is just the basics of combat and truth be told all you really need to know to be a competent fighter in the multi-player of native. However, later techniques and tricks like chambering and feinting can be used to give a player an edge, these tricks can take months to learn properly and allow people of a higher skill group to progress beyond the basics of melee combat. I must however be the typical “noob” and say that I do believe the 2 handed weapons need to become slightly slower as the current state of the game is either a 2 handed sword or a Bow and Arrow, I have been on servers with 30+ people with every single person there using a great sword or a bow & arrow, there is no way you can say the great sword is not over-powered when 80% of the player base use them and they can attack almost as quickly as a 1 handed sword. There we go, now call me a noob who doesn’t understand how difficult the great sword is to use and has no skill whilst I rate the multi-player experience a 7/10 due the great game-play which is slightly let down by some minor balancing issues which I think should be sorted before this experience is worthy of a 8 or a 9 out of 10.
---Napoleonic Wars---
Now this is my favourite way to play this game; 1200 hours of my life have been spent with this DLC and, whilst I am certainly not the best in the world, I have picked up on most of the things you can do in this game. I think you’d be hard pressed to find a part of this DLC I have never seen before. This DLC provides everything you could ever want from a game. Whether you’re looking for a bit of chill gaming with a few friends you can go on death match severs and use classes like the sapper or sailor to have a bit of fun, or you’re looking for a more competitive game then you can choose the battle type servers like group fighting where you will find many players who take the game seriously and will absolutely destroy you time and time again until you finally start to notice the difference as you start to climb the scoreboard and become the best on the server. Genuinely the best feeling ever, the first time you appear best on the server. 5 factions each with their own unique units, all in historically accurate uniform and still providing a whole range of play-styles with the different troop types. Riflemen for sniping enemies with extreme accuracy (as accurate as 19th century weapons get anyway) Line Infantry for holding the front-line, Light Infantry for doing the same thing as a Line Infantryman only being a better shot (Seriously why does anybody play line? Lights have the same melee stats but they can shoot better) Cavalry for annoying everybody because cav is basically the P90 in CS:GO and sappers/sailors for trolling and having fun without being top of the leader board and finally artillery for the people who want to come 1st place on the ‘Vs Bots’ servers but last place on any server that has actual players. There is a unit for everyone! This is the greatest value DLC for any game I have ever seen and I have yet to find anyone who told me they hated the game and managed to maintain their opinion after I taught them what a melee was and how to kill people. They soon became a fan. For this reason I give this DLC a 10/10 a perfect score for a perfect game!

Summary: This is one of the best purchases I ever made on Steam. I've always enjoyed fantasy RPGs, and this little know game is a solid 5 star gem of one. The game starts with you, the protagonist, waking up in the Well of Souls, a so far unnsuccesful experiment designed to resurrect the dead. Your resurrection has also imbued you with the unique trait that you are free from the concept of fate, to which previously every single person in the world had been. You and your knewfound gifts are then tasked to explore Amalur and take down the Tuatha, an army of evil immortals hell bent on the world domination and your personal demise. Some of the defining features of this game:
Combat: Some of the best combat I've ever experienced in an RPG. Simple enough in concept, its all about timing your clicks and mastering weapon combinations while weaving in spells when necessary. But what makes it awesome is how insanely good it feels. Think Shadow of Mordor, but faster and more epic. Plus there are so many weapons with so many stats that it almost feels like the fantasy version of Borderlands 2.
Upgrade sytem: Brilliant. Instead of forcing you decide to upgrade stats without having any clue what they do only to later have you regret your choices, KOA gives you three different upgrade trees: Might, Sorcery and Finesse. Unlike many RPGs, there is not an optimal way to spend skill points, rather upgrading is more about giving you flexibility in how you want to play. You can go full man mode hammer smashing tank with might, ultmate arcane master, become the deadliest assassin with finesse, or any combination of the three. Points in each tree unlock unique spells, weapon combos or perks that make levelling up fun and impactful. Best of all, at any point in the game you reset all your points and reallocate them however you choose (for some gold).
Story and World Design: Beautiful and original, KOA with leave you breathless at some of the worlds you find yourself in. The map is nearly Skyrim level huge, but also very well varied. There are dark caves, snowy mountains, massive forests, brooding castles, wide plains and many more, all populated with unique monsters, races and quests. You will never feel like the game is too small The characters and voice acting are spot on, if you like immersive RPGs then this one takes the cake. The art design is much more fantastical than many traditional RPGs, but I personally enjoyed it. Oh, and while there is a reasonable amount of walking, there is also a lot to do and see along the way, so I personally didn't feel like I was playing Hiking Simulator/Skyrim.
Main and side quests. With 60+ hours on this game as of this review, I have only just beaten the main quests, one faction quest (probably about a solid 10 hours itself) and a handful of side quests. This game has soooooo much to do that I'm not sure I'll ever get to it all. Oh, and I haven't even bought any of the DLC.
The only real flaw in this game is that it is pretty easy. Dying doesn't punish you at all if you save properly, and gold is so plentiful that after a point I never had less than 20 or so potions in my inventory, meaning as long as you restock enough you really shouldn't ever die. Even for your first time I would reccomend playing on hard difficulty.
Conclusion: A beautiful story, fun class/upgrade system and an immersive world collide to create this action RPG masterpiece. This was one of the few single player games that I found myself able to enjoy for hours upon nonstop hours. And for 20 bucks full price, I can't think of a better value on Steam right now.

What an odd game. Beautiful, but buggy. Clever, but a bit confused.
The game is a difficult platformer with inventory and limited character development, and procedurally generated dungeons. It has many small bugs (on Linux, anyway) but only very occasionally did they interrupt the game.
Crystal Catacombs does a great job of setting a particular, claustrophobic mood. Lovecraftian monsters, an intentionally tight field of vision (made more-so by darkness), and random maps populated by both easy and brutally difficult enemies all add to this vague sense of panic. The music, which I adore, is also unusual (is it modal? Is that right?) and adds to the experience.
The beautiful pixel art is the main attraction, but the graphics are not nearly as retro as the gameplay. That's neither an insult nor a compliment. While it's a platformer, the level design and advancement are a lot more true to the spirit of Rogue than glut of roguelike and roguelite cousins. Death is common, especially at first, and sometimes can seem unfair or arbitrary. Again, not really a insult or a compliment, but if you're approaching this with a strictly modern sensibility, I have a feeling you're going to be frustrated. And yes, the controls are difficult. Perhaps slighty more difficult than other similar retro games, but I didn't find them dramatically so, and I don't really think this is necessarily a bad thing. The game is very obviously designed to be difficult.
There are a handful of game-mechanic innovations I haven't seen anywhere else, also. As an example, the use of exploding...  flower-petals? I don't know that they are supposed to be, but they slowly drift down the screen on later levels, and do a fair amount of damage when hit. Usually easy to avoid, they sometimes make otherwise simple encounters more difficult, and provide an added source of urgency. This  is either genius or criminally unpleasant, depending on your expectations. I go with the former, but it's a matter of taste.
Everything about this game feels like it was a labor of love. It has flaws, and many debatable aspects, but it's definitely a work of art.

I think this is the first negative review I've made.
TL;DR you play as some chameleon-eyed♥♥♥♥♥mother ♥♥♥♥er who can't jump right and is really bad at finding cool things.
It's been said by basically everyone; the map design and controls combine to make an experience that is very difficult to enjoy. But none of the reviews I read really went into detail about why the controls fail. The original Castlevania was even more static than this, but it was fine because the enemies were also very rigid in their movement and attack patterns. In this game, you're expected to be making wall jumps and avoid flying enemies and projectiles that can move at any angle while still being stuck with very stiff movement. In short, the enemy and level design are in direct conflict with the fundamentals of how the game plays. Half the time you'll engage with an enemy, but have nowhere to jump because the hallways are all too short, and no way to back off quickly enough to avoid whatever it's probably shooting at you, and with the starting sword, you have be just about inside of an enemy to hit it. I found a shield once, but it had a durability bar that didn't recharge, and you couldn't move while using it, rendering it just about useless. The shield was also the only thing I found during my playtime besides health potions, so I can't even speak for any cool powerups to be found.
The problem with the platforming is that your jump momentum remains constant, even if you let go of whatever directional button you had pressed. I'm a novice when it comes to programming, but this should be an extremely fundamental problem that would take very little change to fix, but the devs have ignored it regardless. Wall jumps are wonky, and with how often you have to do them, it gets old quick. With the movement and combat as it is, trying to navigate the dungeons, I feel I'm fighting the controls more than the enemies. It simply lacks the mechanical fluidity we expect of a modern metroidvania game.
The idea is nice, and with some polish, it could be a great game, but it's received no love from the devs. The game's main saving grace is that the pixel art environments look pretty good. Get it if it's like 75% off and you're willing to subject yourself to the endless repetition of "how was I supposed to avoid that" deaths, or if they ever revamp the controls.

Controls are brought up throughout many of the reviews, and while they take a little while to adjust to, I don’t see that as a fault of the game. As soon as you figure out how to jump in this game you quickly find that there isn’t much to jump into at all and that’s really the bigger flaw.
Every biome has its own little quirks that range from floors being a bit slippery to falling pieces of annoying death that plague the entire level. Some levels seem to outshine others in frustration and challenge, but after a bit of adjustment the levels end quickly. Each biome also has some different enemies that all fall under the uninspired category. The monsters have predictable patterns, so learning how to kill them comes quickly. Both of these things are good because there is little incentive to explore levels: the treasure room can be useful sometimes, but otherwise the main goal is just to grab the key and move on. Leveling up can make your character very powerful so there is no need to bother with the shops in the game, especially because everything there is overpriced.
There just isn’t an incentive to play Crystal Catacombs. I had started to write a guide for this to help others out, but I gave up after a few hours because it just isn’t that fun to play. Some deaths feel cheap, but none of the victories felt satisfying. I think the only learning curve comes from the time it takes to learn how to jump, from then on its just eye strains and an over-too-quick feeling as you face the final boss. The final boss was actually pretty annoying, but more than that, I couldn’t believe there was just that was the end and with other content. Extremely buggy.  It runs sluggish even for a game whose highest resolution is 720.  But that doesn't really bother me as much as how impossible it is to play.  I first tried playing with a USB controller, and immediately noticed when binding my buttons that left and right in the menus don't work.  They don't work with my keyboard or with a gamepad.  I exited to the main game to see if I could move left or right at all, and I couldn't.  Then I messed around in the menus and came back and I could.  But that's how the bugs in this game are.  I eventually figured out that hitting the left and right arrow keys AT THE SAME TIME let you move the menu cursor over so that you could access the full menus.  Then I finally started playing the game.  I made it all the way to level 3 of the first area before I started getting suspicious that I wasn't leveling up.  I didn't know what the green bar was under the health bar because the game is devoid of tutorials or a manual.  While mashing buttons I froze the game by hitting the map button.  But I also noticed that I leveled up.  After mashing buttons again hoping that the game wasn't frozen I realized that hitting the map button moved the game forward by one frame each time.  So I rapidly started smacking the button until I was in the map menu, then started doing it again until I was back in the game.  I kept playing and sure enough, when my experience bar maxed out again it just stayed full and I didn't level up.  So I hit the map button again and just like the first time I leveled up by going to the map screen.  But after I got back in the game I looked in the inventory menu and saw that I was still level 2.  The next time I leveled up I correctly went up a level.  So I started to wonder if all of these problems might be from the controller I was using, so I whipped out my Steam controller.  I reset my buttons, and started playing.  Leveling up worked perfectly and besides not having a good d-pad, at least the game was somewhat functional -- until I died the first time.  Then jump no longer jumped.  B was now the jump button instead of A, and Y was now the attack button instead of X. I went to the bindings menu and everything looked normal, but I reset the bindings to the default anyway (by going to the keyboard and hitting left and right at the same time since you can't do that on a gamepad.)  Thank sweet Jesus this fixed it -- until the next time I died.  4 deaths and 4 binding resets later, you could say I'm... frustrated.  On top of everything the game just isn't that good.  Leveling up isn't satisfying because you don't immediately see any effects of doing so.  I think that your weapon has an experience bar, but I never got it to the second level, even after getting to the end of the 3rd level.  You have a mana bar, but I never picked up anything that used it, and I picked up at least 4 powerups.  I also never got a ranged weapon which made some big enemies almost impossible to kill without getting your health bar destroyed.  Don't get me started on the ice level with the most slippery ice you've ever experienced.  It's some mystical ice that defies the laws of physics and you never stop sliding.  And by reading the reviews I found out that this game was MORE buggy before, and that the devs haven't updated it in a long time.  Also, the soundtrack IS good, but there's only one track per area (not level, AREA) so in a game where you will be dying constantly you can look forward to hearing the same track for a long, long time.

Have you ever wondered what it's like to own a shop during those brutal medieval times? Well, wonder no more, because Shoppe Keep is here. A game that will make you hate thieves even more and broom will be your best friend. Expected to manage your own shop by ordering a supplies, changing price tags and defending it from little thieves and groups of bandits; you are supposed to be a greatest 'shoppe keeper' in the world.
This game so far offers 19 scenarios, each of them more challanging then the previous one (obviously). From selling a few potions, to supplying a town for an attack, you will be the one to profit from it all. But it's not that easy. Various people will have different requirements. While one will be poor and wants a simple health potion, rich warrior will want some golden plated shield and you'll have to satisfy all demands if you want to be good.
Not counting on the fact, that you get minimum profit from cheap items and you will not sell expensive items that easily. Oh, and taxes. Yeah, you will be charged with taxes every 5 minutes. Oh! And thieves. People will steal from you. OH! And dirt... People are unbelievable pigs, broom is literally your best friend as I said earlier. Oh, and... Well, you get the point.
As you sell various items, you will gain XP points as in proper RPG game. Next levels will give you K-points, which you can exchange for different perks. One will give you a 10 % discount for your order, while another will make deliveries come faster or makes an entry fee for your shop.
After you finish first (or second?) scenario, you'll also unlock "My Shoppe" (Free Play) mode. In here, you can build your own shop with stands and tables and simply make yourself at home.
When it comes to a graphics of the game, there are certainly few things that needs a polishing, but it's quite nice game offering this (optional) cell-shade tint with enjoyable and minimal dubbing along with some sounds that might get repetitive after a while, but it's not a big deal.
Shoppe Keeps is not a one-of-a-kind game, but it's definitely a game worth your time and money. It has its idea and it seems that the creators are going the right way. More items, more shop buildings, more detailed options and this might be a great game.
Do I recommend this game? -- Yes.
Do I think you should wait for a sale? -- Sale for 5€ game?! Don't make me laugh...
Do I think that this game is really worth your time and money? -- Well... Yeah. And after all, you can always request a refund, can't you? (Please, don't, it's really worth it)

Having played the original Grim Eclipse fan game, I can say that as of  3/6/16 this game has both good points and bad points.
The good is that we can play with friends a simple co-op system, more visual detail, more characters, and we have the promise of future improvement.
The bad is that the combat of the original fan game was smoother, in some ways more nuanced, felt stronger (better feedback,) did not have the visual desynchronization where our character is moving at a fair pace but the model does not show this for several seconds, and we did not have some British nob telling us to stow our moustache wax (though the bad voice acting and strange characters are as much a part of the series at this point as the distinct visual style.)
My recommendation is that the developers play the hell out of the original fan-game, as repetitive as it can get, and try to bring over the solid feel, fast pace, nuanced strike-and-dive combat, and weapon transformation.
I think this has a lot of potential, but so do several other games that are currently going nowhere fast. Unlike some of those games, I actually trust the Fans/Rooster Teeth employees who are working on this to get it right. I recommend buying it just to show your support for a series that many of us enjoy.

Driving mechanics killed a good game.
I would really like to give this game a recommendation, because it's charming, funny, has a lot of heart and I love Double Fine. I would be willing to forgive it it's boring fighting mechanic and pretty empty strategy mechanic (which doesn't have any real strategy to it). If this game only required you to complete one of these two chores (or a less bad "guitar solo" mini game) every now and then to move on to the next funny scene, I would give it 3 stars because that would be an overall fun experience. Jack Black and all his guest stars are just that fun, story is funny and the graphics are very pretty.
Sadly, there is also driving. Terrible, TERRIBLE driving.
Don't trust the other reviews when they describe driving as "not great". Driving a Yugo is "not great". Driving in this game leaves the impression that it has been designed by a race of ethereal beings from a non-physical plane of existence who tried and failed to imagine the experience of driving based on reading comics and studying photographs. Your car has no inertia and steering...I honestly never had a RL or virtual experience that is comparable to this steering. The closest thing that I can imagine would be driving a tank with super-traction tires on Jupiter. There are few missions that try to spice up the driving with shooting, but the aiming and shooting is, out of necessity, made very easy because keeping the car on course is challenge enough, unless that course is a straight line.
I finally quit the game when a mission (won't spoil the story with background) required me to use the to escape a pursuer. There was couple of U turns on the track and...I just don't know. Maybe one of those genius kids who figure out surgery on their own at the age of 6, without ever going to school, maybe one of them could figure out how to complete a semi-challenging driving course in this game without their hearts overflowing with hate and despair. I couldn't, so I had to quit and delete the game without completing it.

KoA: Reckoning is one of the most underrated, wonderful RPGs ever. DO yourself a favor, right now, if you haven't played this game yet and you like games like Dragon Age Origins, The Elder Scrolls, The Witcher and Fable, buy this game and see that it does something that most modern RPGs don't attempt...
Some of my issues with other modern RPGs as of late are the "build your own class". I'm not a huge fan, because it ends up feeling bland to me. where as when you play a game like World of Warcraft, you pick a race that is so colorful and interesting, then you pick a class that adds another layer of flavor.
What KoAR has done is incredible, it allows you to craft your own class without shedding that flavor by using a system called "Destinies". It's a sort of Tarot card system, that allows you to hand pick between 3 major class types, mixing as you like and then you pick a card or Destiny that encompases your choices and adds bonuses to your choice to incentivise your picking a card that aligns with the ability choices you have made.
It's the perfect remedy to bulding a class without throwing the baby out with the bathwater, or the classes out with the player's handbook...
The story goes a long way to explain the gameplay which many RPGs fail to do. It has a way to explain character death and resurrection which i find very interesting and until recently many games have not attempted to explain, like Pillars of Eternity.
The games armor and weapon models are some of the most fantastic I have EVER seen!!! Not to mention the character models/designs, designed by none other than Todd McFarlane, have like many other featrues in this game, gone the extra mile by creating extreme detail to the characters anatomy, animations and movements.
The combat is VERY fun and fast paced. As you build your character up, you gain more and more moves and combos that all intertwine on the fly beautifully!!! You feel a real sense of power when you dispatch your enemies because ultimately it was you who chose this path of raw power.
There are a few things some players take issue with in this game, but for me the quality of the game outshines any small issues I might have otherwise. I know some gamers have issues with the cameras FOV and height, and I agree it could be better, but it is no where near the problem that could reduce my fun and also combat, if you are adept at games like Fable, Skyrim, you should set the games difficulty to hard at the beginning of the game because if I remember correctly, you can't change the diffiiculty after you start a new game, which is the only other odd design decision.
Otherwise, PLAY KINGDOMS OF AMALUR RECKONING!!!
Such a shame this company didn't sell the amount of games needed to keep this franchise going, with an MMO that was on the way, its an utter shame that this incredible fantasy world was created from top to bottom and no developer has come forward to save this IP!!!
Get it with all the DLC on sale.

Zero Reflex is a bullet hell that doesn't accomplish what the genre is famous for. Bullet Hell games are meant to be extremely difficult, forcing you to navigate through hundreds of damaging shots at once in various patterns at high speed. But this act in Zero Reflex is absolutely trivial. The bullets and effects move at a snail's pace making them extremely easy to dodge and your character can only move in two directions, which results in the game feeling rather dull. There is no challenge.
Perhaps it picks up in the later levels, but you need to beat the previous difficulties to unlock them, and there is no information given on just how long you have to play before a difficulty is "Beaten".
I have no interest in playing a dull game just to see if it might fulfill its genre later on.

Someone said this wasn't a casual game. Tell you what, I sat there in queue for a half hour. Almost fell asleep while waiting.
